name: Columns
description: A single Columns sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke rising from the middle of a horizontal base line. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it can only modify a spell. Its angle, length and count would set direction, power and range.
effect: A spell component that controls the direction a target proceeds and shapes the area of effect into a column. Longer signs add pressure or power, and more signs increase range or quantity.

name: Dispersion
description: A single Dispersion sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke ending in a horizontal bar, with a shallow upward-opening curve beneath the bar. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. It resembles Columns with an added curve, which matches its role as a leaking variant of Columns.
effect: A spell component that makes the seal's magic pour or disperse outwards rather than beam in one direction.

name: Levitation
description: A single Levitation sign on a clean background: an upward-pointing arrow whose shaft rests on a short horizontal base line. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its length and angle within a seal would set how far, how fast, or how much weight the target is carried.
effect: A spell component that floats the target object into the air, often shaping it into a sphere when the Levitation signs are balanced. Longer signs increase travel distance, carrying weight, or speed.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring open. A Wind sigil sits near the bottom of the ring rather than at the center, with its short dashes on both sides. One greatly elongated Levitation sign runs from a crossbar near the top of the ring straight down to an arrowhead just above the sigil, so the arrow points inward toward the sigil. There are no other signs.
justification: The Wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves air. Levitation is a directional sign, and changing its length or angle changes the direction and strength of the spell. Here a single, very long Levitation sign spans almost the whole ring along one axis, so the moved air is pushed strongly in one direction, with nothing to balance it. Because the sigil is offset to one side and the sign is lopsided rather than symmetric, the result is one-directional thrust rather than floating in place.
effect: The Skysoaring Seal produces thrust in the direction of its Levitation sign. When drawn on something large, such as a cloak used as a sail, it can make that object fly.

name: Anti Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel showing a masked, robed figure in a pointed hat with arms spread at the top, and a dark-haired figure falling backward below, wrapped in streaming black ink-like strands and scale fragments, with blank speech bubbles. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible. The concentric pattern on the mask and the small round ornaments on the clothing are costume details, not a legible glyph.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The swirling black strands and scales show the result of a spell, not the glyph itself.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Boulder Stretch Rope
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a plain background. An earth sigil sits at the center. A single Stretch sign wraps around the sigil. It is drawn as a deep U-shaped arc that cradles the sigil from below, open toward the north, with its two ends hooking outward at the upper left and upper right. The outer ring's two ends meet slightly offset near the bottom, leaving the ring open there. No other signs are present.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone. The Stretch sign is meant to surround the central sigil, and here it does. It turns solid matter touched by the seal into long, flexible ribbons. With no other modifiers, the spell's whole effect is that one transformation applied to earth.
effect: Turns stone that comes into contact with the seal into a long, flexible ribbon that can be put to many uses.

name: Crushing
description: A single Crushing sign, a zigzag line with two peaks, on a clean background. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Crushing is semi-directional, so its orientation does not set a direction, and without a sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that crushes the target into ever smaller pieces, down to sand or powder for solids, with a larger sign giving finer pieces. When inverted, it temporarily reforms crushed material into its original shape until the spell ends.

name: Repetition
description: A single Repetition sign on a clean background: a circle with a dot at its center, two curved strokes around the dot, and a diagonal zigzag line that passes through the circle and extends beyond it on both sides. The circle belongs to the sign itself; there is no element sigil and no seal ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a full seal, so there is no element for it to act on. Repetition can also take the place of a sigil within a seal, but on its own it is a component.
effect: A spell component that keeps its target from changing by continuously resetting it to the state it had when the spell first took hold, including its shape and temperature. This can keep things from rotting, make soft objects spring back, or repair damage.

name: Stretch
description: A single Stretch sign on a clean background: an open arc curving over the top with short feet turning outward at each end. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. It is meant to surround the central sigil of a seal.
effect: A spell component that turns solid objects touched by the seal into long, flexible ribbons.

name: Coil
description: A single Coil sign on a clean background: two curved strokes that cross near the top and bottom, forming a vertical twisted loop. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that softens a target object. It affects only physical matter, so it has no effect on liquids or gases.

name: Concealment
description: A single Concealment sign on a clean background: an eight-armed star of crossing lines with a small eye-like mark at the end of each diagonal arm, four eyes in total. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that hides the target object, shrouding it in shadow.

name: Cloak Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, built from nested rings. The outermost band is a double ring lined with repeated chevron marks, matching the Windows sign. Inside it is a thicker main ring with a small break at the upper left, so that ring appears open. At the center sits a Concealment sign: an eight-armed star with eye shapes on its four diagonal ends. Four wind sigils sit at the north, south, east and west ends of the star. At those same four cardinal points on the main ring sit small circles with two curved arms, matching the loops of the Dancing Puppets sign. At the four diagonal points, Envelopment signs cross the main ring.
justification: Four wind sigils set the element, so the spell moves air. Pairing the wind sigils with the Dancing Puppets loops lets the object the seal is drawn on fly and be steered through the air. The central Concealment sign hides the target, and the four Envelopment signs wrap that effect around whatever the object covers. The outer Windows band connects two spaces that are not physically linked, so magic and objects can pass between them. The visible break in the main ring means the spell would not activate as drawn until that ring is closed.
effect: Makes the cloak it is drawn on fly and be steered from afar while draping it in shadow. It also links the cloak to a distant location, so spells can be cast through it while the caster stays elsewhere.

name: Crystal Ribbon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the outer ring open at the bottom. A single large Stretch sign surrounds the center: an arch that is open at the bottom, with short feet angling outward at each end. At the center sits a lattice sigil made of crossing diagonal lines that form a grid of small diamonds. This sigil does not match any of the five element sigils. No other signs are present.
justification: Stretch is drawn to surround the central sigil, and it turns solid material affected by the spell into long, flexible ribbons. The central lattice takes the place an earth sigil would hold in the matching stone-ribbon seal, so it sets the material to crystal rather than stone. As drawn, the ring is open, so the seal would not activate until it is closed.
effect: Creates a soft, flexible ribbon made of crystal, much like the stone-ribbon spell but with crystal as the material.

name: Crystal Shard
description: A manga panel of a hand holding a brush pen, drawing on an irregularly shaped flat surface. Near the center is a sigil of several crossed parallel lines forming a lattice, which matches the crystalize sigil. Its right edge is crossed by the pen. Three small Columns-shaped signs are visible around it, at the north, west and east. They appear to be drawn roughly upright rather than pointing radially, so their inversion cannot be confirmed. The lower right of the surface is covered by the hand and pen. No distinct ring line can be made out apart from the edge of the surface, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be determined.
justification: The lattice sigil sets the spell to crystallize its surroundings. The surrounding Columns-shaped signs give the effect a column-like area of effect. In their inverted form, Columns spread the effect horizontally, similar to Dispersion. A fourth sign may sit under the hand, and the ring is not visible, so the seal cannot be fully read.
effect: Likely causes several large, shard-like crystals to suddenly erupt from the seal. This assumes the covered lower part mirrors the visible signs and that the signs are inverted Columns.

name: Floatglow Lamp
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A light sigil sits at the center. Four Stability and Level Planes signs, each made of three wavy lines, sit at the north, south, east, and west points. Those at north and south run vertically, and those at east and west are turned to run horizontally. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates light. Stability and Level Planes signs balance the target in a plane in the air, letting it drift and turn while staying level. The Columns signs control the direction the target moves and give the effect a column-shaped area. Because the four Columns signs are evenly balanced around the ring, no side wins, so the push is straight up rather than off to one side. Alternating the two sign types around a closed ring gives a balanced, steady lift around a glowing core.
effect: Makes the object the seal is drawn on glow and float steadily in the air, holding it level as it hovers.

name: Floating Drops
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A wind sigil sits at the center. Two water sigils lie on their sides to the east and west, joined to the wind sigil by a horizontal line through the center. Each end of that line finishes in a sideways Columns sign near the ring, with the stem pointing inward and the bar facing outward. Eight paired signs are spaced around the inside of the ring, two near each of the north, south, east-upper and east-lower arcs, mirrored on both sides. Each pair is two Regions signs, one normal and one inverted, pointing toward each other so they cross in an X-like shape.
justification: The wind sigil moves air and holds things aloft. The two water sigils add water, so the spell combines both elements. The Columns signs at the east and west ends steer the magic along the horizontal axis. The eight Regions pairs each point both inward and outward against each other, so the magic manifests only directly on the ring rather than inside or outside it. The ring is open as drawn, so it must be closed before the spell activates.
effect: Creates drops of water that float in the air, forming only along the seal's ring.

name: Convergence
description: A single Convergence sign on a clean background: an outlined triangle with one point facing down. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that focuses a spell's magic down to a single point, and can pack loose particles tightly together so they become somewhat rigid.

name: Dancing Puppets
description: A single Dancing Puppets sign on a clean background: a circular band with small loops at four points and crossing strokes, leaving an empty space at its center. No sigil sits inside it and there is no separate seal ring.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it only modifies a spell. A sigil placed in its empty center supplies the element, and paired with a wind sigil it lets the target fly.
effect: A spell component that allows conscious manipulation of a target object's movement, even at long distances. With a wind sigil it lets the target fly and be steered through the air.

name: Reflection
description: A single Reflection sign on a clean background, shaped like an hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, with horizontal bars at top and bottom. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that likely makes the spell target a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on.

name: Windows
description: A single Windows sign on a clean background: a thick outer band with many identical slanted strokes running around it, enclosing an empty inner circle. No sigil sits in the center and no other signs are present.
justification: One sign, not a seal. It is built to line a spell like an extra ring of repeated markings rather than sit beside a sigil, and with no sigil there is no element for it to act on.
effect: A spell component that likely connects two spaces that are not physically connected, acting as a portal from one location to another.

name: Cooling
description: A single Cooling sign on a clean background: a vertical line with two dots on each side. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that likely cools the target down.

name: Gathering
description: A single Gathering sign on a clean background: a vertical stem with an upward-pointing chevron at the top and two short legs splaying from the base. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that lets a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect, much like Collection, and it possibly pulls that material in more actively.

name: Stability and Level Planes
description: A single Stability and Level Planes sign on a clean background, drawn as two parallel wavy vertical lines. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. It is non-directional, so it acts the same whichever way it points and cannot be inverted. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that keeps the target balanced on a level plane in the air, free to rotate and move but always held at that level, like an object floating on water.

name: Wind
description: A single Wind sign on a clean background: a small curled stroke with a loop at the top and a tail running down. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. It is asymmetric, so it is unknown whether rotating, mirroring, or inverting it changes its behavior, and without a sigil there is no element for it to modify.
effect: A spell component tied to wind, sometimes standing in for a wind sigil; its exact function beyond its relation to wind is unknown.

name: Aeriforms Defined
description: A single Aeriforms Defined sign on a clean background: three short strokes, a tall vertical line in the middle flanked by two shorter lines angled outward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its strokes match the modifier marks drawn beside the wind sigil.
effect: A spell component tied to air. It modifies wind magic, notably the wind underfoot sigil, though its exact effect is unclear.

name: Regions
description: A single Regions sign on a clean background: a caret-shaped chevron pointing upward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its direction depends on how it is placed within a seal.
effect: A spell component that sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. Pointing all signs one way sends the magic that way. Pointing them inward keeps it inside the ring, pointing them outward places it outside the ring, and opposing pairs confine it to the ring itself.

name: Strengthening
description: A single Strengthening sign on a clean background: an upward-pointing triangle crossed by a horizontal line that extends past both sides. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that makes the target object stronger, harder, and more durable.

name: Sights Set
description: A single Sights Set sign on a clean background: an upward-pointing arrow whose shaft ends in a small diamond at the bottom. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component that lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point or target by mental control.

name: Entwining
description: A single Entwining sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke with a horizontal bar at its base and a bracket-like fork at its top. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that makes the object it is drawn on, such as a ribbon, wrap itself around other objects.

name: Detection
description: A single Detection sign on a clean background: three vertical strokes of increasing height from left to right. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component whose exact modifier effect is unclear; it is known to support the function of the Glowstone Path spell.

name: Partition
description: A single Partition sign on a clean background: a small peaked cap above two stacked horizontal bars that bend down at both ends. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One directional sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward, and it can be elongated to stretch or shape those borders. What manifests inside that area is set by the other symbols in the seal.

name: Refuse
description: A single Refuse sign on a clean background: a diamond whose lower corner continues into two crossing legs splayed downward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Refuse is directional, so its effect follows the direction it points.
effect: A spell component that collects unwanted material such as waste toward the direction it points.

name: Solidification
description: A single Solidification sign on a clean background: two small circles joined by a straight vertical line, one above the other. Both circles are empty. There is no sigil and no surrounding ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell it is part of. The straight connecting line and the empty circles mark it as Solidification rather than a pair of linked seals.
effect: A spell component that makes the magic drawn within or connected to it more solid.

name: Binding
description: A single Binding sign on a clean background: two stacked arcs, a wide one above a smaller one, both curving downward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that halts the movement of the target material and binds it together, so it acts and is moved as a single unit.

name: Envelopment
description: A single Envelopment sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke with a short angled hook at the top and bottom, turned in opposite directions. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that makes a spell's magic envelop or surround its target.

name: Immobility
description: A single Immobility sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke rising from a horizontal base, flanked by two outward-curving arcs. There is no sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component that makes the target hold its shape and stay immovable relative to the seal, as if frozen, while still letting the target be moved as a whole.

name: Holding
description: A single Holding sign on a clean background: two facing parenthesis-like curves, each ending in a small hook at the bottom. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that holds the target in the shape defined by the seal while still allowing it to move.

name: Pointing
description: A single Pointing sign on a clean background: a central peaked shape crossed by a horizontal bar, flanked on each side by a hooked curl. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. It is likely non-directional, so its orientation should not change its effect.
effect: A spell component that makes the target manifest in a conical shape, which signs such as Columns can then direct.

name: Piercing
description: A single Piercing sign on a clean background: a vertical line through a small diamond at its middle. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Piercing is non-directional, so its orientation does not change its effect.
effect: A spell component that makes the target material manifest as projectiles or offensive attacks, with the number of Piercing signs setting how many projectiles form.

name: Mimicry
description: A single Mimicry sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke with a small loop at the top, a horizontal bar, a circle crossing the stroke, and two curved strokes at the bottom. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component that guides or imitates the movements of a target object. Paired with a decorative sigil, it makes the spell copy the movements of the creature that sigil depicts.

name: Glaives
description: A single Glaives sign on a clean background: a vertical stem topped by three upward prongs, with the outer two curving outward like a trident. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Glaives are an unusual modifier because they may be drawn outside the ring as long as they stay connected to it.
effect: A spell component that sets how deeply the spell's magic embeds itself into flesh.

name: Collection
description: A single Collection sign on a clean background: a horizontal bar on top with two lines crossing below it to form an open-bottomed X shape. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. Its open side is normally placed facing inward.
effect: A spell component that collects material above and around the seal so the spell can use it.

name: Billow
description: A single Billow sign on a clean background: four rounded loops joined at a central point, arranged like a four-petaled flower. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Billow has radial symmetry and no direction, and it can sit in the center of a seal in place of a sigil, but it remains a sign that modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud firm enough to sit on comfortably.

name: Diamond
description: A single Diamond sign on a clean background: a narrow, upright diamond outline. There is no sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component whose exact function is unknown. It likely limits a spell to objects inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected.

name: Selection
description: A single Selection sign on a clean background: a small square crossed by a vertical and a horizontal line that extend past each side. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal, so there is no element for it to act on. It is non-directional and looks the same from every side, so it cannot be inverted.
effect: A spell component that likely limits a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on.

name: Expansion
description: A single Expansion sign on a clean background, made of four sets of nested right-angle brackets arranged around an empty square center, with their corners pointing outward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Expansion is semi-directional, so its orientation does not set a direction. Corners pointing outward give its normal form, which enlarges rather than shrinks. Without a sigil it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that changes the size of the target, making it grow when the corners point outward and shrink when they point inward.

name: Crosshair
description: A single Crosshair sign on a clean background, drawn as four short strokes arranged in a cross around an empty center. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Crosshair is a directional sign, but without a sigil there is no element for it to aim, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that makes the seal's magic target whatever the shorter ends of the sign point at.

name: Rain
description: A single Rain sign on a clean background. It is a square with inward-curving sides and points at the four corners, with three short lines radiating outward from each side. The center is empty. There is no sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so it is inverted only by flipping it inside-out. It is shown here in its normal orientation, and its empty center is where a sigil would sit.
effect: A spell component that summons the spell's material, making it fall from above or come down like rainfall. When inverted, it instead creates an area the material cannot enter or is pushed out of.

name: Orb
description: A single Orb sign on a clean background: a small circle crossed by one vertical line that runs past it at the top and bottom. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. Orb is non-directional, so its orientation does not change its effect, and it cannot be inverted. Without a sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that creates a spherical space above the seal. Material poured directly into that space collects there and fills it from the bottom up, still affected by gravity, like liquid filling a cup.

name: Purification
description: A single Purification sign on a clean background, a small hooked curl like a reversed spiral. No sigil and no ring.
justification: One sign, not a seal. It is asymmetric, so it has no defined direction or inversion behavior, and without a sigil it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that likely separates waste from water, a small-scale counterpart of the Sigil of Purification.

name: Link
description: A single Link sign on a clean background: a small inverted triangle at the center over a looped stroke, flanked by angled zigzag strokes spreading out to the left and right. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so it only modifies a spell. It is likely semi-directional.
effect: A spell component that identifies and links two target objects that were broken off, removed from, or made from the same source.

name: Stillness
description: A single Stillness sign on a clean background: a vertical stroke crossed by two short horizontal bars, with curved strokes flaring out to each side near the base. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component that holds a magical effect in place, keeping it static in a single location.

name: Projection
description: A single Projection sign on a clean background: a horizontal bar with short legs dropping down at each end, open side facing downward. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component that projects a given effect outward, likely limited to images the rest of the spell specifies.

name: Launch
description: A single Launch sign on a clean background, drawn as two strokes that meet at a peak and flare outward at the base. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal. With no sigil there is no element for it to act on, so it serves only as a modifier within a larger spell.
effect: A spell component that makes the target generate in the direction the sign points, as a powerful but short-lived burst that can reach above treetops before running out, leaving behind anything else the seal produces.

name: Ancient Labyrinth Spell
description: A tall framed panel showing a winding path paved with scale-like stones, with a large white seal laid over its upper half. The seal has an outer boundary of dots and short tick marks, some T-shaped like small Columns signs, plus a few small chevrons resembling Regions signs. Inside it are two concentric bands of repeated glyphs: small figure-like shapes with dots and crossbars, flanked by V and inverted-V marks. None of these match any known sign. Above the seal, dense wavy lines fan out like rock strata. The center, where a sigil would sit, is washed out by a bright glow and crossed by the path, so no sigil can be seen. Because the outer boundary is drawn as dots and ticks, it cannot be judged whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: The repeated glyphs in both bands are unknown symbols that do not correspond to any recognized sign, and the center is hidden by light, so no sigil sets an element or intensity. The marks that look like Columns and Regions cannot be confirmed at this scale. There is nothing reliable to decode beyond the overall radially symmetric layout.
effect: The spell's effect cannot be worked out from the visible signs. It is known to manipulate gravity so that a person can stand upright only on the winding path marked by the seal. Anyone who strays from the path, or steps on a stone whose seal has crumbled, is thrown back to the starting point.

name: Ancient Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a sigil that matches no known element glyph: a tall oval enclosing two small stacked circles, with a curling hooked stroke running down the left side and another running up the right. Around it, eight figures form an inner ring at the cardinal and intercardinal points. Each is a square and a diamond nested together with a dot in the middle, close to the light sigil but without its protruding lines. Curved strokes resembling Launch signs join each neighbouring pair. Near the outer ring sit eight Convergence triangles, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point, each with a tip pointing inward. Between each pair of triangles is a three-pronged sign resembling Glaives or Stillness, eight in total, with the prongs facing outward.
justification: The eight light-like figures make up the inner ring and place the spell in the domain of light. The Launch-like connectors suggest that light is released in a strong outward burst. The eight inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point, which fits a concentrated beam rather than a diffuse glow. The Glaives-like or Stillness-like signs may hold the effect steady in one place. The central sigil cannot be matched, so its contribution is unknown, and most of the other parts can only be read by resemblance.
effect: A light spell that presumably creates a column of light.

name: Anicent Flames
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a flat sheet, seen in perspective, with the ring closed and fully visible. Smoke billows above it without covering the glyph. The center holds a small unmatched glyph: a short vertical stroke flanked by two dots, with two angle marks pointing inward toward it. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, two above and two below. At the four cardinal points sit circled marks. The north one looks like an Orb sign, a circle crossed by a line. The east, south, and west ones look like a circle enclosing an A-shaped stroke, close to Strengthening but inside a ring. None of these cardinal or central glyphs clearly matches a known sign or sigil.
justification: The central glyph does not match any known element sigil, so the element cannot be read directly from the seal. The four Columns signs are evenly spaced, so the magic should rise in a balanced column above the seal rather than leaning to one side. The circled signs at the cardinal points cannot be matched with confidence, so their modifying role is unknown.
effect: Creates a small fire that burns like an ordinary fire spell. Whether it has any special or forbidden properties is unknown.

name: Anti Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga page showing a robed figure in a tall pointed hood with an eye emblem, arms spread, above a second figure falling backward. Swirling black ink streams and scattered scale-like flakes surround the falling figure, and several speech bubbles are blank. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The swirling ink and flakes are an effect, and the eye on the hood is a costume emblem, not a glyph.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Beastwarding Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. At the center sits an unidentified sigil: a long vertical stem with two pairs of downward-slanting branches, framed by four bracket-shaped corners that form an open box around it. A light sigil sits at the east point and another at the west point. At the north and south points sits an identical unidentified sign, a diamond overlaid with two crossing curves, resembling a Diamond sign fused with a Coil sign. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the center and its stem pointing outward.
justification: The two light sigils set light as one element. The unidentified central sigil adds a second, unknown element, so the seal mixes two types of magic. The four Columns signs, evenly balanced around the seal, project the magic outward in a spread rather than toward one side. The north and south signs are unidentified, so their modifying role is unclear.
effect: Repels animals from the surrounding area. How it repels them is not certain, but the light sigils suggest it does so with light.

name: Beldaruit's Illusion Cloak Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A variant of the wind sigil sits at the north, an S-shape with four short strokes on each side instead of two. Six small Columns signs arc around the upper half, three on each side, with their stems pointing outward toward the ring. An Envelopment sign lies horizontally at the east and another at the west. At the center is a small circle on a stem that splits into two curved arms, shaped much like Dancing Puppets. It is flanked on each side by an unidentified diamond with a dot inside and a bar above it, with a single dot below. In the lower half, a set of three parallel diagonal lines sits at the southwest and another at the southeast. Two arrows point inward from east and west toward an eight-spoked star at the south-center, each with a dot outside it. At the south is a double arch resting on a horizontal line. A long diagonal stroke crosses this arch and runs out to touch the ring at the lower right.
justification: The wind sigil variant sets the element as air. The outward-facing Columns signs spread the effect outward from the seal rather than beaming it in one direction. The two Envelopment signs make the effect wrap around and surround what it targets. The Dancing Puppets-like central figure suggests the result can be shaped and moved. The diamonds, the inward arrows, the star, and the lower arch are unidentified signs. They most likely define how the airborne material looks and what form it holds.
effect: A smokesculpture spell that shapes smoke into a convincing illusion of an apprentice cloak and cap around the wearer.

name: Beldaruit's Illusion Cloak Spell
description: A manga page of three panels. In the bottom panel a hand holds a thin pen over an oval seal, seen at a steep angle and heavily foreshortened. The lower part of the seal runs past the panel border, so it is only partly visible and it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed. A row of about four small Columns-like signs runs along the upper edge, and a similar row sits along the lower right edge. A curved, S-like sign sits at the right side and a curl-shaped sign at the left. Near the center are a small diamond or house-shaped mark and an asterisk-like mark. Small upward arrow marks sit at the lower left, and short groups of parallel strokes appear scattered around. The pen tip overlaps the upper area, and the marks are too small and slanted to identify with certainty.
justification: No element sigil can be clearly identified because of the angle and size. The two rows of Columns-like signs set where the magic projects, and they appear to face outward. If the curved signs at the sides are Envelopment, they make the effect wrap around and surround a target. The central marks resemble shapes tied to guided movement, but they cannot be confirmed here. With the bottom cut off and the sigil unreadable, the seal can only be partly decoded.
effect: Likely a smoke-sculpting illusion that forms smoke into the shape of an apprentice cloak and cap that wraps around the wearer. This rests on the signs that can be read and assumes the hidden lower part matches the seal's known layout. The visible portion alone does not confirm it.

name: Billow Cluster
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. A Billow sign, a four-lobed clover shape, sits at the center in place of a sigil. Four Collection signs sit at the north, south, east, and west points. Each is drawn with its barred side toward the ring and its open side facing inward toward the Billow sign. No element sigil is present.
justification: The seal has no element sigil. Billow is a sign that can take the center position in place of a sigil, and it turns available material into a fluffy cloud. The four Collection signs, open sides facing inward in their usual orientation, gather material above and around the seal so the spell can use it. Together they gather material and feed it to Billow, which converts it into a cloud. Because there is no element sigil, the spell is not tied to one element and works on whatever material is directed into it.
effect: Converts any material directed into the seal into a soft, fluffy cloud.

name: Bird of Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line art on a white background, with the ring closed. A light sigil sits at the center, rotated so its square is set inside a diamond with the cross lines running diagonally. A Launch sign sits at the north point, its peak pointing outward. A Dispersion sign sits at the south point, with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. At the east and west points are two mirrored bird-shaped sigils. Each is made of paired curved arcs around a small chevron, with three short dashes on the outer side like wings.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the seal creates light. The two bird sigils are decorative sigils that sculpt that light into the rough shape of a bird. Two of them together still yield a single bird. The Launch sign sends the effect out in a powerful but short burst in the direction it points. The Dispersion sign opposite lets the magic pour outward rather than holding it in a tight beam. Together, light is shaped into a bird, flung out in a burst, and left to spread and drift.
effect: Produces a bird made of light that bursts outward and flies around for some time. It can serve as entertainment, a call for help, or a distraction.

name: Borrowshade
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink on a white background, ring closed. A Concealment sign sits at the center: an eight-spoked star with an eye shape at the end of each of its north, east, south, and west spokes. Four Envelopment signs, each a long stroke with a short hooked tail at either end, sit at the northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest points, set along the diagonals. No element sigil is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The seal has no sigil. The Concealment sign takes the central place a sigil would normally hold, and it hides the target. The four Envelopment signs, evenly spaced around it, make that effect wrap around and surround whatever is targeted. The result is a concealing veil rather than an elemental effect, and the closed ring lets the spell activate.
effect: Conceals the target's form and hides it from view. It gathers shadows around the target so that it blends into the darkness.

name: Boulder Stretch Rope
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn in black line. The ring shows a small gap at the bottom, so it appears to be ring open. An earth sigil sits at the center, with its horizontal bar, central stem, angled arms and two flanking dots all legible. A single Stretch sign wraps around the sigil as a large U-shaped curve. It opens toward the north and its two ends hook outward beside the top corners of the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone. It is fairly large within the ring, giving a moderately strong effect. The Stretch sign is meant to surround the central sigil, and it turns solid objects the spell touches into long, flexible ribbons. With no directional or shaping signs added, the seal is simply earth magic reshaped by Stretch.
effect: Shapes stone into a long, flexible ribbon that can be used like rope for many purposes.

name: Bubble Carriage Seal
description: A manga panel looking up at a seal drawn overhead, with two figures below. Only the lower portion of the seal is in frame; its upper half is cut off by the top edge of the panel, and speech bubbles cover the left and right sides. A large S-shaped sigil with radiating strokes sits at the center, matching the Sigil of Aeriforms rather than the plain Wind sigil. Small Columns signs alternate with chevron-shaped Regions signs in a band along the visible lower arc; the Regions signs point outward toward the ring. Only part of the ring is visible, so whether it is open or closed cannot be seen. Two inset diagrams in the lower corners compare the Sigil of Aeriforms, which has arrow-like strokes and dots, with the Sigil of Wind, which has short plain strokes.
justification: The Aeriforms sigil sets the element as air creation rather than air movement. The Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect. The Regions signs pointing outward make the magic manifest outside the ring and not within it. Together they shape the generated air into an enclosing volume around the seal. The visible band of evenly spaced Columns and Regions signs suggests they continue in an unbroken ring around the sigil.
effect: Creates a supply of breathable air and shapes it into a rough bubble that holds together underwater. This assumes the hidden upper half carries the same evenly alternating Columns and outward-pointing Regions signs as the visible lower half.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. At the center of the inner ring sits a Repetition sign in place of a sigil. Four Sights Set signs sit at the intercardinal points, each straddling the inner and outer rings, with the diamond end outward and the arrow pointing inward toward the center. Entwining signs sit at the north and south points between the rings. Entwining signs also sit at the east and west points, turned sideways, each with a Strengthening sign attached to its inner end.
justification: With Repetition at the center, this is a time spell. Repetition keeps resetting the object to its original state, so it resists bending and damage. The four Sights Set signs let the caster aim the spell at a chosen target with the mind. The Entwining signs make the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around that target. The Strengthening signs on the east and west Entwining signs make it harder and more durable. Together they describe a cloth that can be steered at a target, coils around it, and holds firm.
effect: Lets the caster aim a pennant at a chosen target with the mind and make it wrap tightly around that target. It also reinforces the pennant and keeps resetting it to its original state, so it resists damage and bending.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A page holding several labeled seals and panels. The relevant seal sits in the bottom right: two concentric rings, both closed and fully visible. A Repetition glyph fills the center of the inner ring. Four Sights Set signs sit at the intercardinal points with their diamond ends on the outer ring and arrowheads pointing inward toward the inner ring. An Entwining sign straddles the two rings at the north point, and another, mirrored, at the south point. At the east and west points, horizontal signs straddle the rings and end in a diamond and a triangle, consistent with Entwining strokes capped by Strengthening signs. A legend beneath names Repetition, Sights Set, Entwining, and Strengthening.
justification: There is no element sigil. Repetition takes the central place and continuously resets the object to its original state, so it resists bending and damage. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen target with the mind. Entwining makes the object it is drawn on wrap around another object. Strengthening makes it harder and more durable. Placed between the two rings, these modifiers act together on the object bearing the seal.
effect: Lets the bearer mentally choose a target and makes the pennant wrap tightly around it. The pennant is reinforced and keeps resetting to its original state, so it resists damage and bending.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A printed page with a fully visible seal at the top on a plain background, drawn in dark ink with all rings closed. It has an outer ring, a second ring just inside it, and a smaller inner ring around the center. A Repetition sign sits alone at the center of the inner ring in place of a sigil. Four Sights Set signs sit at the intercardinal points, diamond ends at the outer edge and arrows pointing inward toward the center, straddling the two outer rings. One Entwining sign sits at the north point and one inverted Entwining sign at the south point. At the east and west points, Entwining signs lie sideways with a Strengthening sign attached to each end. Beside the seal, the Repetition, Sights Set, Entwining, and Strengthening glyphs are shown individually. Below is a separate column of linked water seals that is not part of this seal.
justification: There is no element sigil. Repetition holds the center instead and acts as a time glyph, so the spell keeps resetting the object it is drawn on to its original state and resists damage and bending. The inward-pointing Sights Set signs let the wielder aim the spell at a chosen target with the mind. The Entwining signs make the object wrap around that target, and the Strengthening signs on the east and west Entwining signs harden and reinforce it. The north/south and east/west pairs mirror each other, so the spell acts evenly.
effect: Lets the wielder aim the pennant at a target with the mind and have it wrap tightly around that target. It also strengthens the pennant and keeps resetting it to its original state, so it resists damage and bending.

Its outline shows several concentric rings divided into radial segments around a darker central circle, with faint curved marks near the center. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told, and the seal is only partly visible at its upper edge where it fades into the water's glare.

Square stepping stones cross the water toward a stone arch bridge. A partly sketched deer stands on the right, and a hand holding a dip pen draws at the lower right. The stepping stones carry no readable ring, sigil, or sign, and the swirl patterns in the border are ornament, not seals.

name: Coco's Village Wash Spring
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a Repetition sigil, a small circle with an S-shaped line through it around an inner ring. Its S-line continues out of the north and south sides and joins two large, curling multi-hook sigils, one at the north and one at the south, which are Purification sigils. Each Purification sigil is flanked by two Columns signs set diagonally, at the northwest, northeast, southwest and southeast, for four in total. At the east and west sit two Partition signs, each drawn as a tall double-lined bracket with a small triangle pointing inward toward the central sigil. Outside each Partition sign is a cluster of three Refuse signs (diamonds with crossed legs) facing different directions, six in total.
justification: The Purification sigils set the magic as cleansing water, and the Repetition sigil they connect to keeps resetting the affected water to its earlier clean state. The diagonal Columns signs push the effect outward from each Purification sigil. The inward-pointing Partition signs outline the area of effect around the center, and the Refuse signs gather unwanted material and waste toward where they point, separating it from the water.
effect: Makes the water shine brightly and purifies it of waste and contaminants, repeatedly restoring it to a clean state so it stays a reliable source of fresh water.

name: Coco's Village Wash Spring

Inside the black ring glow a few pink nested lens-shaped lines, but they match no sigil or sign, and no seal structure can be made out.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The glowing lines inside the ring are decoration, not a readable sigil or recognizable signs.

name: Counterclock
description: A manga panel of an open book held by a hand. On the right page, a ring is filled with straight lines that cross into many triangles, arranged in a star-like pattern. No element sigil is visible at its center. Fingers cover the right edge and lower part of this seal, and the drawing is too small to pick out individual signs. The ring looks closed where it can be seen. On the left page are smaller glyphs: an eye-shaped mark resembling Repetition, a swirl-shaped mark, and a round seal with spoke-like marks around a central circle.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil. It is built entirely from straight lines forming geometric shapes in a star layout, which marks it as a time-type spell rather than one driven by fire, water, earth, wind, or light. No individual sign can be matched, so the reading rests on this overall geometric structure. The covered portion may hold further detail that cannot be read.
effect: Reverses time on the target, undoing wear and other damage. The effect lasts at most a day, and when it expires the target returns to the state it was in before the spell was cast, though the seal can be drawn again to repeat it. The exact parameters of this seal cannot be read because the hand and the small scale obscure its signs.

name: Counterclock
description: A manga panel. A seal is drawn on a bare chest, framed by the open edges of a shirt that two hands hold apart. Inside the ring is a six-pointed star built entirely from straight lines, with smaller triangles and nested geometric shapes radiating from its center. There is no recognizable element sigil and no identifiable sign inside the ring. Small branching, arrow-like marks sit outside the ring at the upper left, upper right, left side and below, but they are too small and roughly drawn to match any named sign. The right hand covers part of the ring's upper right edge and the shirt edges hide parts of the left and lower rim, so the ring is only partly visible and whether it is open or closed cannot be confirmed.
justification: No element sigil is present, so there is no Primary Tetrad element. The design instead relies on a six-sided star of straight-line geometric shapes, which is the defining structure of the Counterclock family of time spells. These spells work without a sigil and are distinct from the Repetition sigil. The outer marks cannot be matched to known signs, so their modifying role cannot be decoded, and the hidden parts of the ring prevent a full reading.
effect: Reverses time on the target to undo wear and other damage. The effect lasts at most one day and is not permanent. When it expires, the spell vanishes and the target returns to the state it was in before the spell was cast, though the seal can be drawn again to repeat the effect.

No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panels.

No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.

name: Crystal Shard
description: A manga panel. A hand holds a brush and is drawing on a rounded surface. Near the center is a grid-like sigil of crossed parallel lines, matching the crystalize sigil, with its lower right corner crossed by the brush. Three T-shaped Columns signs are visible around it, at the north, the east, and the west to southwest. Their bars and stems appear turned relative to the center, which suggests they are inverted. The hand and brush cover the lower right part of the surface, where any further signs would sit. No ring line is visible, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be read.
justification: The crystalize sigil sets the kind of magic, turning surrounding material such as air or water into crystal or ice. Inverted Columns signs make the effect manifest outward and sideways rather than as a single upward beam, much like Dispersion, and more Columns signs widen the range or quantity of what is generated. Together they send many crystal formations bursting outward from the seal.
effect: Causes several large, shard-like crystals to suddenly erupt from the seal. This assumes the hidden lower right part holds matching inverted Columns signs that mirror the visible ones.

name: Dragon Smokesculpture
description: A manga panel of two hands working on a large seal, with one hand holding a pen. No ring edge is visible, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen, and the seal runs past every edge of the frame. The left hand and fingers cover much of the left side, and the pen hand covers part of the right. A vertical central motif runs down the middle, topped by teardrop-like shapes and stacked marks. It does not clearly match any reference sigil. Many Columns signs are scattered in loose rows across the surface, some upright and some inverted. Several upward-pointing arrow shapes resembling Levitation signs sit around the center. Near the lower right are three Regions-like chevrons pointing left beside an arrow-like sign. Asterisk-shaped marks sit near the top left and top right, and a small wavy cluster lies right of center. These match no reference sign.
justification: Only part of the seal can be read. The many Columns signs give the magic a columnar push in set directions, and their numbers and lengths raise its range and power. The Levitation signs float the conjured material into the air. The Regions chevrons all point one way, which sends the magic toward that side. Because the central sigil cannot be identified and the hands hide large areas, the element and the full combination cannot be confirmed from what is visible.
effect: A sculpting spell that forms a dragon out of smoke that can fly through the air and roar. The visible Columns and Levitation signs fit the lifting and flying parts of this effect, but the hidden and unidentified portions cannot be checked from this view.
