name: Ever-Flowing Icepack
description: A manga panel with two seals drawn on paper beneath a floating mass. The left seal is mostly visible but cut off at the left frame edge, and its ring appears closed where visible. It holds a water sigil, upside down from this viewpoint, with one small Columns sign sitting opposite it near the ring. The right seal is mostly cut off by the right frame edge. Only part of its ring and several angled Columns signs along its edge show, and its center is hidden.
justification: In the left seal, the water sigil sets the element. A single small Columns sign gives one gentle, low-pressure direction instead of a strong beam, so the water settles rather than shooting off. In the right seal, several angled Columns signs set around the ring push the water in many slanted directions at once. That makes it spin rather than hold still. Its central sigil is hidden, but I assume it is a water sigil mirroring the left seal.
effect: The left seal stills water into a thin disc floating above the seal. Slightly angling its single small Columns sign would keep the water flowing steadily in a circle, giving an icepack that stays cold. The right seal, assuming the hidden part mirrors the visible angled Columns signs around a water sigil, sends water spinning rapidly and erratically above the seal.

name: Ever-Flowing Icepack
description: A manga panel of a table covered in papers and tools. One sheet near the center carries a small seal seen at an angle: a water sigil at the center, curved strokes at either side that seem to be the ring, and a tiny mark below the sigil that looks like a single small Columns sign. The drawing is too small to confirm whether the ring is open or closed or how the mark is angled. Other sheets show spiral and swirl marks that are too small and foreshortened to read.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water. A single small Columns sign opposite a water sigil directs the water's pressure in one direction rather than spreading it around the ring. Tilting that one sign slightly changes the direction of the push. Without clearer detail, the exact angle and the state of the ring cannot be read.
effect: If the mark is a single small Columns sign, the seal holds water as a thin disc floating above it. Angled slightly, the sign keeps the water flowing continuously in a circle, which keeps it cold, like an icepack that never warms. This reading assumes the unclear mark is that sign.

name: Fish Guidance
description: A manga panel showing a seal whose bottom portion is cut off by the panel edge. Only the top arc of the ring is visible, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen. At the center, a small inner circle encloses an angular, arrowhead-like sigil. In the upper left a Columns sign stands with a line running from it toward the inner circle, and a Crosshair sign sits beside it. A second Crosshair sits on the west side. Near the north point is a looped, figure-like symbol resembling an abstract fish, and a similar figure sits in the lower left. A Stability and Level Planes sign of three wavy lines sits in the upper right, with another set of wavy lines partly visible at the lower left edge. A second Columns sign lies on its side in the east. In the lower right is a branching, fork-like symbol that does not match any known sign. Any signs on the southern part of the seal are not visible.
justification: The enclosed central mark is the Guidance sigil, which draws objects to the seal's location when they match the parameters set by the other signs. The fish-like figures act as decorative sigils that define the target as water shaped into those forms, and the Crosshair signs aim the spell at whatever matches them. The Columns signs give the effect a directed, column-shaped reach, and the Stability and Level Planes signs keep the guided objects balanced on a level plane in the air.
effect: Guides flying water sculptures shaped as fish and birds so that they travel toward the location of the seal.

name: Flame Burst Spell
description: A manga panel of a figure holding a paper cone overhead, with a long paper strip unfurled from it into a large ring around them. The band of the ring carries a repeating row of alternating signs: Columns signs (T shapes) and arrow signs with triangular heads matching Pulling, set at an angle along the band rather than pointing straight inward. The left half of the band is fully visible. The right side is cut off by the panel edge, and the bottom is hidden by smoke and flame, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. The figure covers the center of the ring, and no sigil is visible inside it. A small round paper at the figure's chest bears a mark resembling a fire sigil, but it is too small to read clearly.
justification: The ring alternates Columns and Pulling around its whole visible length. Pulling draws material toward the seal, and when angled it adds a twisting motion; here it most likely draws in surrounding air to feed the flames. Columns shapes the effect into a column and pushes it in a set direction, and the many repeated Columns signs increase its range and output, giving the fire a forceful, beam-like burst. The ring itself holds no visible sigil, so the element comes from the separate small paper, whose mark appears to be a fire sigil. This assumes the hidden right and lower parts of the band continue the same alternating pattern.
effect: A fire spell that draws in surrounding air as fuel, produces a ring of fire, and then releases a larger, forceful explosion. This assumes the hidden parts of the band repeat the visible alternating pattern and that the small paper's mark is a fire sigil.

name: Flame Shot Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the lower left. A large fire sigil sits in the lower half of the seal rather than the center; its two side rays and bottom stem cross through the triangle's edges, and the stem reaches nearly to the ring. Directly above the sigil's apex is a single long Columns sign, its crossbar just above the sigil and its stem running up toward the north side of the ring. Two vertical stacks of five Regions signs each sit to the west and east of the Columns stem, all ten pointing north.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. A single Columns sign forms a column-shaped area of effect, and its length adds force along its stem, so the flame is driven toward the north. Regions signs that all point to the same side send the magic in that direction, so the ten north-pointing Regions signs add directionality and confine the fire to the space in front of the seal, letting it reach farther. Because the ring is open, the spell activates only once the ring is closed.
effect: Fires a directional flame that looks like a mix of a beam of fire and a fireball, shooting forward from the seal in the direction the Columns stem points.

name: Floatglow Lamp Seal
description: Two hands hold a round pad on which a seal is drawn, with a pen nib resting on the bottom of the ring. The seal is fully visible and the ring appears closed where the nib touches it. A small Light sigil sits at the center. Four Levitation signs sit at the north, east, south, and west points, each with its arrow pointing inward toward the sigil. Four Convergence triangles sit at the four intercardinal points, each turned so one point aims sideways.
justification: The Light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring keeps the effect modest. The four Levitation signs are equal in length and evenly spaced, so they are balanced, which floats the magic and tends to shape it into a sphere. The four Convergence signs focus the magic down to a single point. Together they gather the light into a compact, floating sphere rather than a beam.
effect: Produces a small, floating ball of light.

name: Floatglow Lamp Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the bottom. A small Light sigil sits at the center. Four Stability and Level Planes signs, each drawn with three wavy lines, sit at the north, south, east and west points; the east and west ones are turned sideways. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, angled along the diagonals toward the center.
justification: The Light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring points to a gentle, low-intensity glow. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Because the four Columns signs are evenly balanced, the light rises straight up rather than leaning to one side. Stability and Level Planes, also four and balanced, keeps the result floating level in the air. Together the signs shape light into a steady, floating column above the seal. The ring is open, so it must be closed before the spell activates.
effect: Produces floating light above the seal. With these signs, it most likely forms a beam of light hovering above the seal rather than a ball. This spell is used to light floating lamps. It activates only once the ring is closed.

name: Floatglow Lamp Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a light sigil at the center drawn at a moderate size relative to the ring. Four Levitation signs sit at the north, south, east, and west points, each with its arrow pointing inward toward the sigil. Four Convergence signs sit at the four intercardinal points, each triangle angled so that one point aims roughly toward the center. The layout is symmetric and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the magic as the creation of light, and its moderate size keeps the effect small. Levitation floats its target into the air, and four signs placed evenly around the ring balance it, which tends to shape the result into a sphere. Convergence focuses the magic down to a single point, so the light gathers into one compact body instead of spreading out. Together these make a contained, floating sphere of light.
effect: Produces a small ball of light that floats above the seal.

name: Floating Drops
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A wind sigil sits at the center, and its side strokes connect outward to two water sigils lying on their sides, one to the east and one to the west. Each water sigil runs into a Columns sign turned horizontally, with its crossbar set against the ring at the east and west points. Eight pairs of Regions signs surround the center: two near the north, two near the south, and one at each intercardinal point. Each pair has one sign pointing inward and one inverted sign pointing outward, tip to tip.
justification: The central wind sigil and the two water sigils make this a mixed spell: water is supplied and wind moves it and holds it aloft. The paired Regions signs point toward one another, inward and outward together, which confines the magic to the ring itself rather than the inside or outside of the seal. The horizontal Columns signs at the ends of the water sigils direct the magic along that plane. Because the ring is open, the seal would need to be closed before it activates.
effect: Creates drops of water that float in the air, generated only along the seal's outer ring.

name: Floating Drops
description: A manga page with several panels. In the top middle panel a seal is drawn on a round dish seen at a steep angle, ring closed, with an S-shaped spiral at the center that matches the wind sigil. Smaller marks sit around it near the edge of the ring, but they are too small and foreshortened to name. In the top right panel a hand with a pen draws on a flat round object. S-shaped marks with small dots beside them are visible, and the hand covers part of that seal. The large lower panel shows no readable glyph.
justification: The central spiral sets wind as the element, so the spell moves air. The shapes beside it may be water sigils, which would add water to the spell, but they cannot be confirmed at this size. The signs near the ring cannot be read, so how the magic is placed relative to the ring cannot be checked from the visible marks.
effect: Likely creates drops of water that float in the air and form only along the seal's outer ring. Paired Regions signs, one normal and one inverted, point toward each other and confine the drops to the ring. This assumes the unreadable marks near the ring are those paired Regions signs and the side shapes are water sigils.

name: Flowers of Light
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a light sigil, a square with a diamond inside and short lines extending from its four points, with a small dot at its middle; it is small relative to the ring. The light sigil is enclosed by a pentagon, and from each of the pentagon's five corners a long straight line runs outward toward the ring, dividing the outer area into five equal sections. This pentagon-and-spoke figure is the decorative flower sigil. Each of the five sections holds one identical sign: two curls joined on a short stem, with the stem pointing outward toward the ring and the curls opening toward the center, one at the south and the others spaced evenly around. These curl signs do not match any standard named sign.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light, and its small size points to a gentle, low-intensity glow. The decorative flower sigil sculpts that light into the rough shape of flowers. Its pentagon keeps it separate from the light sigil. The five identical curl signs around it are the flower sigil's modifiers, which set the type of flower and possibly how many appear. No directional signs are present, so the effect forms around the seal rather than being sent in any direction.
effect: Creates glowing flowers made of light. The light fades over time.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A fully visible seal in black ink on a clean background, ring closed. A wind sigil sits at the center, small relative to the ring, with its short strokes on either side. Around it is a Dancing Puppets sign: an inner circle with four small loops at the northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest points, curved lines crossing through each loop and reaching outward, and short straight strokes at the north, south, east, and west points. No other signs are present.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air and anything carried by it. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Dancing Puppets surrounds the sigil, with the sigil placed in its center as that sign allows. Paired with wind, Dancing Puppets lets objects fly and be moved through the air, but no aiming or control signs are present, so the movement has no set direction.
effect: Causes nearby objects to dart into the sky and fly around erratically, with enough force to carry some objects up into the air.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A manga panel of a cloak tumbling through the air above a small child who reaches up toward it, with speed lines and scattered debris. Beside the cloak, a small round disc is seen at a steep angle, with dark marks along one edge that may be part of a ring. It is too small and too foreshortened to show any sigil or sign. No other ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The only possible seal is a tiny, angled disc whose markings are unreadable, so no sigil or sign can be identified.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because no sigil or sign is legible.

name: Flying Watersculptures
description: A manga panel of water shaped like birds and fish flying through the air against a starry night sky. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The water shapes are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Flying Watersculptures
description: A manga panel of a figure in the center with arms stretched forward, flanked by two tilted jugs. The left jug carries bands of small round seals and rows of tiny marks around its body. Because they wrap around the curved surface, only the front-facing parts are visible. The right jug shows similar markings but is partly cut off by the panel edge and partly behind a speech bubble. The marks are drawn too small to pick out any sigil or sign, and it cannot be told whether any ring is open or closed.
justification: Nothing to decode. Seals are present on both jugs, but no sigil or sign can be matched to a known shape, and the curvature and framing hide much of each seal.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, as none of the visible seals are readable.

name: Flying Watersculptures
description: A manga panel of two figures holding hands and dancing on top of a large floating bowl, with several pots around them and water shaped like fish and birds swirling through the air. The pots carry only decorative bands of zigzags and dots. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The pot patterns are ornamental bands, not seals, and the water shapes are effects, not glyphs.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Flying Watersculptures
description: A manga panel showing an irregular splash of liquid with curling tendrils and scattered droplets, framed between two large blank speech bubbles at the left and right. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The splash and droplets are not a glyph, and no seal markings appear anywhere in the panel.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Forbidden Glow
description: A small manga panel showing a round surface with a seal drawn on it. The ring appears closed, and a hand holding a pen sits at the right edge without covering the seal. About eight small Columns signs are spaced evenly around the inside of the ring. At the center is a small, irregular, star-like mark that does not cleanly match any of the standard element sigils. Fine detail is limited by the size of the image.
justification: The evenly spaced Columns signs set the area of effect and send the magic outward in columns. Because they are balanced around the ring, no single direction is favored. The irregular central mark fits a Flickering Light sigil, a variant in the fire and light domain, so the spell produces unstable light rather than steady light or flame.
effect: Creates a brief, colorful burst of flickering, sparkling lights, similar to a small firework.

name: Glowstone Path Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a Light sigil at the center. At the east and west points sit Dispersion signs lying on their sides, each with its stem pointing inward, its crossbar facing outward, and its curve on the outermost side. At the north point is a Levitation sign with its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward at the sigil. It is flanked at the northwest and northeast by pairs of wavy lines that resemble a sideways Stability and Level Planes sign. Two long curved lines sweep down from either side of the sigil and cross near the south point, forming an elongated X. Below and outside these curves, at the southwest and southeast, sit a Diamond sign beside three diagonal parallel lines of increasing length, which resemble a Detection sign. These lower groups mirror each other.
justification: The Light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring sets a moderate intensity. The paired Dispersion signs make the light pour or spread outward instead of beaming in one direction. The inward-pointing Levitation sign and the flanking Stability and Level Planes signs govern movement and balance, which likely lets the surface be pressed down and settle back level. The Detection-like and Diamond signs near the crossing curves probably limit the effect to the object the seal is drawn on and trigger it on contact, though their exact roles are unclear.
effect: Makes a stone emit light when it is stepped on.

name: Grasping Wind
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A wind sigil sits at the center: an S-shaped stroke with short dashes on either side. Four Pulling signs sit at the intercardinal points (northwest, northeast, southwest and southeast), each with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the sigil. The linework is sketchy but every sign is legible.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air. Pulling is a directional sign that draws the target toward the seal when its arrow points inward, and all four signs here point inward. Because they are evenly spaced around the ring, the pull is balanced from every side and converges on the seal. If the signs are angled off the straight inward line, Pulling adds a twisting motion to the pull.
effect: Creates a strong wind current flowing toward the seal, with enough force to pull lighter objects to it. When the Pulling signs are slanted, the air twists into a vortex that spins objects as they are drawn in.

name: Guidance Seal
description: A manga panel with a seal drawn over a dotted screentone background. The seal is fully visible and its ring is closed. At the center sits a small inner circle with a spiral inside it, which matches the Sigil of Guidance. At the north point a long Columns sign runs from the center outward and ends in a thick, heavy bar. Small cross-shaped marks made of short dashes sit to the northeast and to the west-northwest; they resemble Crosshair signs. On the east side is a cluster of short strokes, including a sideways T-shaped mark and paired wavy strokes. In the southeast is a shape with a pointed body and fanned tail lines that reads as an abstract fish. In the southwest are two paired wavy strokes resembling Stability and Level Planes, next to an angled mark. A branching mark of unclear identity sits in the west. The drawing is coarse, so several of the smaller outer signs cannot be named with certainty.
justification: The Sigil of Guidance at the center sets the spell's purpose: it draws to the seal's location any objects that match the parameters set by the other glyphs. The Crosshair-like signs aim the spell at a target. The fish-like decorative shape limits that target to things shaped by the same design. The Columns sign gives the pull a direction. The Stability and Level Planes strokes keep whatever is drawn in balanced on a level plane.
effect: The seal acts as a final destination for a pursuing target. It attracts objects that match its parameters, here things shaped like the fish design, and guides them toward the seal's location.

name: Guidance Seal
description: A manga panel framed by ornate patterned borders, with a blank oval speech bubble in the upper middle and cloth pouches along the top edge. Below, on a flat stone among grass and rocks, a seal is drawn and seen at an angle. It is fully visible and the ring appears closed. A spiral sigil sits at the center. Two small nested circles, each holding its own glyph, sit inside the ring, one to the west and one to the northeast; their contents are too small to read. Small wavy marks resembling Stability and Level Planes signs and short T-shaped marks resembling Columns signs sit around the spiral, but the drawing is too small to confirm their exact count and orientation.
justification: The central spiral is the Guidance sigil, which draws matching objects to the seal's location, with the other parts of the seal setting what counts as a match. The two nested circles are embedded seals that serve as those parameters, so the spell targets whatever carries them. The wavy Stability and Level Planes signs keep the targets level as they travel, and the Columns signs give the pull a direction.
effect: Acts as a destination point: objects carrying the matching nested seals, here Pouch of Calling seals, are drawn toward the seal and fly to where it is planted. This reading assumes the nested circles hold Pouch of Calling seals, since their contents cannot be read.

name: Guidance Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a spiral sigil holding a downward-pointing arrow shaped like an inward Pulling sign. A long line rises from the spiral to a crossbar near the north edge, forming an elongated Columns shape joined to the sigil. Two Crosshair signs, set diagonally with their dashes around an open center, sit at the north-northwest and north-northeast. Below them, at the northwest and northeast, are two looping knotted signs that look like abstract fish. A two-line Stability and Level Planes sign sits at the west point and another at the east point. Two Columns signs at the southwest and southeast are angled outward. At the south point is a large fish-shaped figure with a triangular body and a forked tail of straight lines.
justification: The central spiral with its inward arrow is the Guidance sigil, which draws matching objects toward the seal. The two Stability and Level Planes signs keep whatever arrives balanced on a level plane. The two Columns signs, along with the elongated column rising from the sigil, set the column-shaped area and the direction the magic acts in. Crosshair makes the spell target whatever its short ends point at. The fish-shaped figures act as decorative sigils that limit that targeting to objects sculpted with the same fish shape. Together these make a seal that locks onto fish-shaped sculptures and pulls them toward itself.
effect: Acts as a final destination for a pursuing target. The Crosshairs aim the spell at sculptures shaped by the matching fish sigils, and the Guidance sigil draws them toward the seal's location.

name: Guidance Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A large Guidance sigil fills the center and lower half: a T-shaped bar at the north runs down into a wide spiral that coils inward and ends in a downward arrow with a triangle on its shaft, much like a Pulling sign. Two small nested seals, each with its own closed ring, sit at the northwest and northeast. Each holds a small quadrilateral at its center, four small triangles resembling Convergence signs, and pairs of crossing arcs, and the two are mirror images of each other. A two-lined Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn as horizontal wavy lines, sits at the west and another at the east. A Columns sign sits at the southwest and another at the southeast, each angled with its stem pointing in toward the center and its crossbar toward the ring.
justification: The Guidance sigil draws to the seal any object that matches the parameters set by the rest of the seal. The two nested seals supply those parameters, so only objects carrying that spell are targeted. Their inward-pointing Convergence-like triangles focus each nested spell to a point. The paired Stability and Level Planes signs keep the effect level and balanced. The two Columns signs set the pressure and direction the pull acts along. Everything is mirrored left to right, so the effect is balanced, and the closed ring lets the spell activate.
effect: Acts as a final destination for the objects it targets. Anything carrying the spell matched by the nested seals is drawn toward the seal's location, so those objects travel to wherever the seal has been planted.

description: A sepia-toned illustration of a witch in a wide-brimmed hat with a long decorated ribbon and a patterned gown. She holds a test tube in one hand and a dropper over another tube in the other, beside a table crowded with bottles and flasks. The ribbon and sleeves carry decorative patterns, but no ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The patterns on the clothing are ornament, not a seal, and the bottles show no glyph.

A circular emblem with spoke-like lines on the standing figure's robe is partly covered by the flask. It holds no identifiable sigil or sign. The zigzag band along the bed is ornamental. No readable seal is visible.

She holds a test tube in one hand and uses a stirring rod or dropper on a second tube with the other. Beside her is a small table crowded with flasks and bottles. Interlaced knotwork borders the left edge and a draped curtain hangs on the right. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.

name: Healingcraft
description: A manga panel showing a figure in a light tabard-like garment with a mark at the chest. The ring is closed and fully visible. A plain cross divides it into four equal quarters, and its arms reach the ring. A solid dot sits at each of the four points where the cross meets the ring: north, south, east and west. Nothing else appears inside the ring, and no sign sits around it.
justification: The cross does not match the fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil, or any known variant. None of the known signs appear. It resembles Selection or Crosshair only loosely, since it lacks Selection's square and Crosshair's broken arms. The four dots carry no known meaning. Because no element sigil and no recognizable modifier can be identified, there is nothing to decode beyond its symmetric four-way layout.
effect: The specific effect cannot be determined from the image, because the mark matches no known sigil or sign. Healingcraft as a whole is magic that heals the human body by curing the sick, weak and injured.

name: Healingcraft
description: A manga panel of a robed figure with a buttoned front and a wide pale collar, holding a large cloth in both hands. Two small cross-shaped emblems with rounded ends sit on the collar, one on each side. They are not enclosed in a ring and do not match any known sigil or sign. No seal is visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The cross emblems are clothing decoration, not a sigil or sign.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Healingcraft
description: A sepia illustration of two robed witches in pointed hats facing a burst of radiating light above clouds and rock spires. The left figure wears a tabard marked with a circle split into quarters by a cross. The right figure carries a round shield covered in ornate floral and swirling patterns, with a four-lobed motif at its center and small marks around the rim. Neither emblem shows a recognizable sigil or any sign from the known set.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The circular designs are ornamental emblems. They do not show an element sigil or an arrangement of modifier signs that can be read as a seal.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Icy Road
description: A seal drawn in ink on a stone floor, seen at a steep angle. The left side of the seal runs out of frame, and a hand holding a pen covers part of the east edge. The ring is unbroken along the visible arc, but its left portion is out of frame, so whether the ring is closed cannot be confirmed. At the center is a large sigil made of long straight lines crossing in a lattice; its left end is cut off. Around it, two kinds of signs alternate. The first is the Columns sign, drawn with its stem toward the ring and its crossbar toward the center. Six of these are at least partly visible, including two clipped at the left edge and one under the pen tip. The second is an unidentified sign: a square or rectangle holding a small angled corner mark. Six of these are visible, one partly behind the hand.
justification: The lattice sigil at the center is the Crystalize sigil, which turns surrounding material such as air or water into crystal or ice. The Columns signs face the inverted way, and inverted Columns spread their effect horizontally rather than upward, carrying the magic out past the ring. The boxed corner signs are even in spacing and count but do not match any known sign, so their role cannot be decoded.
effect: Freezes the air into a solid surface that reaches a long distance outward from the seal, though only up to a limited range. This assumes the hidden left side mirrors the visible right side.

name: Illusory Labyrinth
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn with two concentric rings. The outer ring is open at the bottom; the inner ring is closed. Between the two rings sit eight matching ornamental knot-and-scroll motifs at the cardinal and intercardinal points. At the center is a large unidentified sigil. It is a dome marked with three dots and ringed with triangular spikes, topped by a solid upward triangle over a bar, with a horizontal bar and a fan of downward stripes beneath it. Hooked to either side of the dome is a circle containing a Strengthening sign. About sixteen Columns signs are set in pairs at the north, east, south, and west, each with its short bar facing outward toward the ring. Many Regions signs run in arcs along the inside of the inner ring. They are angled to point along the circumference rather than inward or outward. Four branching, antler-like figures with curled ends sit at the intercardinal points. Three triangles resembling Convergence, each with a curling tail, sit at the west, east, and south, with their points facing outward toward the ring.
justification: The central sigil is none of the elemental sigils. It sets an unknown kind of magic, and its large size relative to the ring makes the spell very strong. The evenly balanced Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect without favoring one direction. The Regions signs decide where magic manifests relative to the seal. Because they point along the ring instead of in or out, they suggest the magic is carried around the seal in a circuit. The outward-facing Convergence-like triangles, the paired Strengthening signs, the antler-like figures, and the ornamental border are not identifiable, so their exact contribution cannot be read. The outer ring is open at the bottom, so as drawn the seal would not activate until that gap is closed.
effect: Creates a vast underground labyrinth in which space itself is distorted and loops back on itself. Anyone who walks too far ends up right where they started, so escape is impossible.

name: Integration
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the ring closed. An earth sigil sits at the center, flanked by its two dots, with an extra horizontal bar drawn beneath its lower point. Six Crushing signs surround it: one at the north, one at the south, and one at each of the four intercardinal points. All six are inverted, with their outer ends and middle vertex facing out toward the ring and their two remaining vertices facing in toward the sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the spell's domain to solid matter such as stone, sand, and soil. Crushing is a semi-directional sign. Normally it breaks a target into ever smaller pieces, but when it is inverted its effect is reversed. With every Crushing sign inverted, the earth magic reassembles crushed material rather than pulverizing it. The six signs are spaced evenly around the sigil, so the effect is balanced on all sides.
effect: Takes powdered or smashed solid particles within range and temporarily rearranges them into the shape of the object they originally came from, which makes it easy to identify an unknown powder. When the spell wears off or is removed, the material returns to its broken state.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel of two hands working over a scaled surface. One hand holds a long pen pressed to the surface, and the other hand is spread flat beside it. Between the fingers, a few ink strokes show: a small ring-like circle near the pen tip and some short curved lines. The ring, any sigil, and the surrounding signs are mostly hidden by the hands, so it is not clear whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: Nothing to decode. The visible strokes are too small and fragmented to match any sign or sigil.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel of a large dark wolf with patches of scales on its back and shoulders, leaping forward with jaws open over speed lines. Two small figures in pointed hats look on in alarm from the lower left, and another creature is partly visible at the left edge. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The wolf and the motion lines are panel art, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Light Beacon
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a small gap at the bottom beside the south sign. A small light sigil sits at the center. Four Columns signs are evenly spaced at the north, east, south, and west points. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center, so all four face the same way.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Because the four signs are equal and balanced, no side is favored, and the light rises as a single upright column above the seal. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it produces a stable beam of light pointing straight up from the seal.

name: Light Beacon
description: A manga panel. A hand holds two round discs, one in front of the other. The rear disc carries a seal with a light sigil at the center, drawn as a square overlapping a diamond with short lines extending outward. A Columns sign sits at the north point and another is visible at the west point. The east side has small marks that are mostly hidden behind the front disc, and the lower part of the rear seal is covered by the hand and the front disc. The visible stretch of the ring is closed, but much of its edge is cut off or overlapped. The front disc holds a second seal, ring closed, with a spiral inside a cloud-shaped outline at the center, surrounded by about eight Columns-like signs. That central glyph does not match the light sigil.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the rear seal creates and controls light. The Columns signs around it give the magic a column-shaped area of effect, sending it out as a beam. The visible Columns appear evenly spaced and balanced, so the beam goes straight up rather than leaning to one side. The front disc's seal uses a different central glyph and is a separate spell.
effect: The rear seal produces a steady beam of light rising straight up from the seal. This assumes the hidden Columns signs mirror the visible ones evenly around the sigil.

name: Light Tracer
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough, slightly broken ink lines, ring closed. A light sigil sits at the center, enclosed by a Stretch sign that wraps around it like an arch. A Link sign sits at the north point above them. No other signs are visible inside the ring.
justification: The light sigil sets the element as light. The Stretch sign around it turns the magic into long, flexible ribbons, which for light means thin strands. The Link sign joins objects that were broken off from or made from the same source, so it directs those strands toward the matching pieces.
effect: When drawn on one fragment of a broken object, the seal sends a string of light out to every other fragment of that same object, linking them together.

name: Light-Reducing Spell
description: A round lens with a seal drawn across it, set in a thin rim with a small piece of frame below. The ring is closed and fully visible. At the center sits a small diamond holding a few marks that are too small and sketchy to read, with a small circle overlapping each of its corners. A larger diamond surrounds it, and several small triangles matching the Convergence sign sit around it, mostly toward its corners. Short branched lines run outward between the circles, and pairs of lines form V shapes near the rim. The fine linework is faint, so individual strokes are hard to separate.
justification: No standard element sigil can be picked out. The center diamond resembles the Diamond sign and takes the central position. Its inner marks would set the exact element but cannot be read. The Convergence signs focus the spell's magic down to a single point, which fits an effect concentrated on specific light sources rather than spread across the whole lens. The branched lines and V shapes do not clearly match any known sign, so their contribution is uncertain.
effect: A vision spell that blocks out the brightest lights to protect the eyesight of the person looking through the lens.

name: Light-Reducing Spell
description: A manga panel showing a hand holding a hinged lens assembly. One round lens has a seal drawn across its face in fine marks, and glimmer lines cross part of it. Inside the rim there is a cluster of small overlapping circles near the center, small triangle shapes toward the edge that may be Convergence signs, and several short branched lines. No sigil can be identified, and the seal's own ring cannot be told apart from the lens rim, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be judged. The marks are too small and too broken up by the glimmer to name any sign with certainty.
justification: There is little to decode. If the triangles are Convergence signs, they would focus the spell's magic down toward a point, but no element sigil is legible, so it cannot be said what kind of magic is being focused or how the overlapping circles and branched lines modify it.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the image because the glyph is too small and obscured to read. The visible overlapping circles and triangle marks are consistent with a seal that blocks out the brightest light to protect the eyes.

name: Lockwax
description: A fully visible seal drawn in blue-violet on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a small inner circle holding an unfamiliar glyph: a small loop on top of a vertical stem, with a curved crossbar and two short splayed strokes at the base. It matches none of the element sigils. Three straight lines run from the inner circle to the outer ring and divide the seal into three equal sections. Each section holds one arrow-like sign with a triangular head at the end, roughly pointing toward the middle of its section, so there are three in total. Beside each arrow are two short lines, one bent at a right angle over the other. These do not clearly match any named sign.
justification: The central glyph is not a fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil, so the element or kind of magic cannot be read from it. The three arrow signs resemble directional arrows like Pulling or Levitation but do not match either exactly, and the bent-line pairs are unidentified. All three sections repeat the same arrangement, giving the seal threefold rotational symmetry, so whatever the modifiers do is applied evenly around the center. The inner circle walled off by the dividing lines suggests the effect is held tightly around a single fixed point rather than sent outward, but the specific signs cannot be decoded.
effect: Binds a scroll shut, sealing it so it cannot be freely opened. The strength of this protection and the way to undo it are not known.

name: Makeover Mask Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a small gap near the top left. A large Concealment sign fills the center: eight crossing spokes, with an eye drawn at the end of each of the four cardinal spokes. There is no element sigil. A Regions sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, both pointing inward toward the center. At the north point, above the upper eye, is a sign of three stacked horizontal lines resembling an equals sign. At the south point, below the lower eye, is a spiral-shaped sign. Neither of these two matches a known sign.
justification: Concealment takes the central position, so the spell's core is hiding the target's original form rather than working with an element. Regions signs determine where magic manifests, and with both pointing inward the effect is held within the ring, confined to the object the seal is drawn on. The three-line sign and the spiral are unidentified modifiers, so their exact contribution is unknown, though they likely shape the illusion that replaces what is concealed.
effect: Conceals the wearer's real face beneath an illusion that makes it look clean and like their best self, acting as magical makeup. It is unknown whether the illusion looks the same for everyone or adapts to each wearer's idea of beauty.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel. A hand holds an oval disc with a white-on-black seal, seen at a steep angle. A band of small dashes and dots runs around the rim inside the outer ring, which looks closed where visible. Fingers overlap the upper left edge. Near the top center is a sigil of concentric circles with a dot in the middle, matching the Obliviation sigil. A line runs down from it with several small branching, fork-like strokes on either side that may be Glaives, and a hook-shaped mark sits near the bottom. The foreshortening and rough rendering keep the smaller signs from being read with certainty.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil sets this as an Obliviation spell. If the forked strokes are Glaives, they set how deeply the magic embeds itself into the target's flesh. The rim dots and the bottom hook are too small to match to any known sign, so whatever narrower targeting they add cannot be read.
effect: Likely erases memories from the target's mind, removing knowledge of magic and the memories tied to it. Some versions of this seal limit the erasure to a period of time or to specific topics or people, but which version this is cannot be read from the visible marks.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel showing a round seal drawn in white on a black disc, the reverse of normal ink. The rim is a band of short white dashes and appears closed, though its left edge is overlapped by dark panel art. At the center is a sigil of concentric circles with a dot in the middle, matching the Obliviation sigil. A few small dot-shaped marks sit around the top of the sigil. Several branching, root-like lines run downward from the sigil toward the south edge of the ring, which read as Glaives. The image is small and coarse, so any finer signs between these elements cannot be made out.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil sets the magic as obliviation, which acts on memory rather than on a physical element. The Glaives below it set how deeply the magic embeds itself into the target's flesh, letting it reach the mind. The dot signs along the top likely narrow what is erased, but they are too small here to separate one variant from another.
effect: Erases memories from the target's mind, typically all knowledge of magic and any memories tied to it. Variants can instead erase a specific period of time or specific topics or people. The exact variant cannot be determined from the image because the smaller signs are not legible.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A close-up manga panel of a seal drawn in white on a dark round surface. Only the upper-right part is fully visible; the left side and bottom are cut off by the frame. The center holds a sigil made of concentric circles around a solid dot, which is the Obliviation sigil, with a short line rising from its top and a stem running down from its bottom. Several branching lines spread from the stem and end in forked, multi-pronged tips like Glaives signs; about four of these forks are visible, and the rest run out of frame. A band of small evenly spaced tick marks lines the visible arc of the outer ring. A short row of small dot-like marks sits inside the ring near its top right. Because part of the ring is out of frame, it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil with a central dot sets the spell as Obliviation magic, which acts on memory. The forked Glaives branching from below set how deeply that magic embeds itself into flesh. The dot-like marks and the ticked outer band are modifiers whose exact roles are not known, and the hidden lower and left portions may hold further signs that would narrow which memories are taken.
effect: Erases memories from the target's mind, with the Glaives setting how deeply the spell reaches. Depending on its added signs, it can wipe all knowledge of magic and the memories tied to it, a specific span of time, or specific topics or people. Which of these this seal does cannot be determined from the visible portion.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel showing a fully visible seal drawn in white lines on a solid black disc, ring closed. Off-center toward the upper left sits a sigil of concentric circles with a dot in the middle, the Obliviation sigil. A single straight line runs from the sigil to the ring's upper-left edge. About five branching, forked strokes resembling Glaives fan out from the sigil toward the lower right. A curved row of small dot signs follows the inside of the ring along the top and down the left side. Two feathered arrow-like signs follow the curve of the ring, one at the upper right pointing down and one at the lower left pointing right. None of these arrows or dots match a known named sign.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil sets the spell's purpose as obliviation, the magic of forgetting. The Glaives-like branches set how deeply the magic embeds itself into the target, which fits a spell that reaches into the mind. The dot signs and the curving arrows are unnamed modifiers. Their exact role cannot be read from the glyph alone, though they likely help define the scope of what is erased.
effect: Erases memories from the target's mind. Depending on its exact signs, the spell can wipe all knowledge of magic along with connected memories, erase a specific period of time, or remove specific topics or people regardless of when they were learned.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel showing a face in profile on the left and a raised hand on the right. The hand holds a dark, round, flat object seen almost edge-on, partly covered by the thumb and fingers. Thin branching tendrils hang from its lower edge. No ring, sigil, or sign can be made out on its surface.
justification: Nothing to decode. The dark surface is turned away and covered by the hand, so no sigil or sign is legible.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because no glyph is readable.

name: Mirror Cloak Spell
description: A manga panel showing a large seal drawn at a diagonal, with a dark-haired figure on the right raising both hands toward it. The outer ring has a scalloped edge of repeating looped bumps, resembling the loops of the Dancing Puppets sign. At the center is a Concealment sign, a starburst of crossing lines with small eye shapes around it. Hourglass-shaped Reflection signs sit inside the ring above and below the center. Three more Reflection signs sit in small circles outside the main ring, at the upper right, left, and bottom, joined by straight lines that form a large triangle overlapping the main seal. Several hooked, zigzagging strokes resembling Envelopment signs are scattered inside the ring. A speech bubble covers the lower left of the seal, and the figure's hands and fingers cover part of the lower right, so the ring is only partly visible and whether it is closed cannot be confirmed.
justification: No element sigil is visible, so the central Concealment sign carries the spell, much as some signs can stand in the center in place of a sigil. Concealment hides a target, and the Envelopment-like strokes wrap that effect around whatever the seal covers. The triangle of linked circles holding Reflection signs reads as a second seal laid over the first. Reflection targets a reflected image on the drawn surface, and together with the projecting part of that overlay it turns the hidden target into an outward illusion. The covered sections may hold further signs, such as Projection, that cannot be read here.
effect: Wraps the target in shadow to hide it, while projecting the reflected image of a nearby beast so the target appears to be that creature. The guise shifts in and out with a smoke- or steam-like effect and a hissing sound.

name: Mirror Cloak Spell
description: A manga page of four panels showing a figure in a scaled cloak, a hand pulling the scaled cloak away amid puffs of smoke-like cloud, a startled young witch, and a wide shot of a woman wearing a scaled garment. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere on the page.
justification: Nothing to decode. The scales and smoke are art, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Mirror Spell
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a clean background, ring closed. There is no sigil at the center. Inside the ring sit four Reflection signs, one at each cardinal point: the north and south ones stand upright like hourglasses, and the east and west ones lie on their sides. A bracket-shaped Projection sign is set into the ring at each cardinal point, just outside each Reflection sign, for four Projection signs in total. At the four intercardinal points, small satellite circles sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by angled lines, and each holds one small Reflection sign.
justification: With no sigil, the seal does not create or move any element. It works only through its signs. Reflection targets an image reflected on the surface the seal is drawn on. Each inner Reflection sign is paired with a Projection sign facing outward on the ring, so the reflected image is sent outward from the seal. The four satellite Reflection signs, linked to the main ring, probably widen the range of reflections the seal can draw from. The layout is evenly balanced on all four sides, so the effect has no single direction.
effect: Draws on an image reflected in the reflective surface the seal is drawn on and projects it outward as an illusion, such as the reflected form of a nearby beast. It depends on that reflective surface, and its effect alone, without a concealing spell layered beneath it, is not confirmed.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background, with all rings closed. An outer band between two concentric rings holds a continuous chain of curled Wind signs. Inside it, the outermost section of the inner ring is packed with many Columns signs set at varying angles. At the center sits a three-line Stability and Level Planes sign, with small Columns signs around it. Four smaller sub-seals sit at the cardinal points. The north and south sub-seals each hold a three-armed whorl-shaped sigil, a Whorling Wind sigil, ringed by three Columns signs. The east and west sub-seals each hold an S-shaped wind-family sigil, a Wind Underfoot sigil, inside its own inner circle, surrounded by small paired marks. These marks are too small to name with full certainty but match Levitation and Aeriforms Defined. In the spaces between the sub-seals are curled Wind signs grouped with Columns signs.
justification: No fire, water, earth or light sigil appears; every sigil present belongs to the wind family, so this is wind magic throughout. The central Stability and Level Planes sign takes the place of a main sigil and balances the target in a level plane. The Columns around it and the dense band of Columns direct pressure and set the range. The Wind Underfoot sub-seals, paired with Levitation and Aeriforms Defined, support a solid object in the air. The Whorling Wind sub-seals with Columns add rotating air. The Wind signs and angled Columns between the sub-seals likely add a turning component, though the exact role of the Wind sign is uncertain.
effect: Lets the object it is drawn on fly while staying steady, level and upright, even while it is being pulled along.

name: Petrification
description: A fully visible, highly complex seal on a clean background, outer ring closed. The center holds an unfamiliar sigil made of interlocking squares around a small nested diamond. It is surrounded by an inner ring lined with a band of small dotted script-like marks. At the north, south, east, and west points, long stems with arrowheads pointing inward toward that inner ring reach out from the center, flanked by curling scrolls and tipped with Dispersion-like half-circle signs. In each intercardinal quadrant sits a half-circle enclosing a cluster of crossed lines with a small circle, accompanied by rows of Dispersion signs and long hooked lines that match Envelopment, plus small diamond-on-line signs resembling Piercing. Four smaller circular seals cut into the outer ring at the cardinal points: north holds crystal-shaped diamonds and branching snowflake-like motifs with small Columns signs; west holds a dotted eye surrounded by a zigzag band; east holds droplet shapes over a wave line; south holds linked small circles with curving strokes. Each of these is flanked by a pair of eye-like signs in corner brackets. The outermost band, between the sub-seals, carries repeated Columns signs paired with short parallel lines.
justification: Dispersion signs make the magic pour outward from the seal. The Envelopment signs make that effect wrap around whatever it reaches. The inward-pointing arrowheads and Columns signs set direction and reach. The cardinal sub-seals add their own elements: crystal-like forms to the north, water-like forms to the east, and an eye-like pattern to the west that may hold the targets in place. The interlocked central sigil and several of the surrounding signs do not match any known sign, so how they combine to petrify cannot be fully read.
effect: Turns everything nearby, living or inanimate, into an unknown rock-like material, and likely freezes time for whatever it petrifies.

name: Petrification
description: A manga panel of a figure turned to jagged stone, one arm raised and holding a small pendant-like object, with crystalline spikes rising around the base. The held object shows only indistinct marks, and no ring, sigil, or sign can be made out anywhere in the panel.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The stone figure and spikes are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel of a hand holding a round object wrapped in flame, with a seal drawn on it, fully visible and ring closed. A large triangle is inscribed in the ring. At the center sits a fire sigil variant: a small triangle with three lines running outward from it, each ending in a filled square. Three branching, feather-like signs sit between the triangle's sides and the ring, at the north, east, and southwest, each pointing inward. Short pairs of parallel dashes sit in the remaining gaps between them. Outside the ring, three small looped marks with filled dots are attached by short lines at the west, northeast, and south. None of the surrounding signs match a named sign. The flame shading lies over the seal, but the lines remain legible.
justification: The central fire sigil variant sets the element as fire, and the square-ended lines set it apart from the plain fire sigil. The inscribed triangle and the three-fold arrangement of branching signs, dash pairs, and outer marks repeat evenly around the ring. That points to a balanced, centered manifestation rather than one aimed in a single direction. The individual effects of these unnamed signs cannot be decoded from shape alone, so the spell's behavior rests on the sigil variant.
effect: Forms an artificial flame that looks and acts like real fire and gives off light, but produces no heat. It can be touched without injury, still scares off beasts, and needs no fuel, so it never goes out.

name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel with a fully visible seal, ring closed, set against grey textured shading. A large triangle is inscribed in the ring, with a small filled square at each of its three corners. At the center sits a small triangle crossed by a horizontal bar. It looks like a fire sigil with a crossbar and is close in shape to the Strengthening sign. Three identical branching signs sit just outside the triangle's edges, at the north, southwest and southeast. Each is a vertical stroke with angled side strokes, and none matches a known sign. Three small round knobs sit on the outer edge of the ring, at the northwest, northeast and south, lined up with the triangle's corners. Some fine strokes are soft at this resolution.
justification: The central triangle with its crossbar is a variant of the fire sigil, Unburning Flames. It places the spell in the domain of fire but changes what kind of flame is made. The inscribed triangle, corner squares, branching signs and ring knobs are modifiers outside the standard set, so their individual effects cannot be read from the sign rules. Their three-fold symmetry around the sigil points to an evenly shaped, contained flame rather than a directed one.
effect: Forms an artificial flame that looks and behaves like real fire and still gives off light, but produces no heat. It can be touched or held without any risk of burns, needs no fuel, and does not go out.

name: Playland of Sand
description: A manga panel of a large sandcastle with towers, spiral slides, arched supports, and crystal-topped turrets, surrounded by sand flowers and sparkles. Sound effect lettering fills the upper right. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The sandcastle is the result of a spell, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

In the main panel, a robed figure with a pointed hat writes in an open book resting on their lap. That page also shows faint, tiny markings partly covered by the writing hand. Blank speech bubbles cover parts of the panel. No sigil or sign can be identified, and no ring can be judged as open or closed.
justification: There is nothing to decode. Seal markings are present, but they are too small and too partly covered to identify any sigil or sign.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A manga panel of two hands holding up a tied cloth pouch with a diamond-shaped patch sewn on its front. A small circular seal is drawn on the patch, fully visible and ring closed, with a small dot on the ring at the north and south points. At the center is a Calling sigil: a small diamond flanked by two long curved strokes that bow outward and run from north to south. Four small triangles, read as Convergence signs, sit at the intercardinal points. Two larger triangles sit at the east and west points, pointing inward toward the diamond. Short vertical marks sit at the north and south points between the curved strokes. The fingers rest on the patch's edges and do not cover the ring, but the small scale leaves fine detail soft.
justification: The central Calling sigil sets the spell's nature, which is recording a phrase and echoing it repeatedly. The four Convergence signs placed evenly around it focus that magic down to a single point. The larger inward-pointing triangles and the vertical marks are additional components in a symmetric arrangement and add to the targeting side of the spell. Together they form a layered spell, with an inner seal that records sound and an outer seal that drives pursuit.
effect: Records a spoken phrase and makes its target repeatedly echo it while pursuing a set destination.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A small manga panel. A cloth pouch in the lower right has a ring drawn on it that appears closed and fully visible. Inside the ring is a central mark with smaller marks on either side, but the lines are too small and coarse to match to any sigil or sign. Several small round objects in the upper left carry tiny circular markings that are also unreadable.
justification: A ring and some inner marks are present, but no sigil or sign can be identified. With no element and no modifiers legible, there is nothing to decode.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A manga panel. Two hands hold a small round disc with a seal drawn on it. Its ring looks closed, and a few tiny marks circle a central mark, but they are too small and blurred to match to any sigil or sign. Behind the disc, a larger pattern is drawn on cloth. It shows curved ring-like lines, a hollow square, and several triangles. Fingers and thumbs cover much of this pattern, and the panel edge cuts off its outer part, so it is only partly visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode reliably. No element sigil can be identified on the small disc, and its surrounding marks cannot be told apart. The larger pattern on the cloth is too covered and too cut off to read as a seal.
