name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A manga panel showing a tied cloth pouch resting on a pile of round discs, each marked with a small star-like mark and a ring of tiny dots. Behind the pouch at the upper left, part of a larger seal ring is visible with at least two triangle shapes near its edge, which look like Convergence signs. Most of the seal, including the center where a sigil would sit, is hidden behind the pouch, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed. The marks on the discs are too small to read.
justification: The visible triangles match the Convergence sign, which focuses a spell's magic down to a single point. The sigil and the remaining signs are covered, so the element and the full set of modifiers cannot be read, and the signs cannot be combined into a full spell.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because the sigil is hidden. The visible Convergence signs only show that the spell's magic is focused toward a single point.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed. At the center is a diamond outline flanked by two long curved vertical lines that bow in toward it. Two half-lens shapes sit at the east and west points, their tips touching those curves. Together this composite figure forms the Sigil of Calling. Short straight vertical lines sit directly north and south of the diamond. Four outlined Convergence triangles sit at the four intercardinal points, each with a point aimed toward the center. Two solid filled triangles are attached to the inside of the ring at the north and south points, both pointing inward.
justification: The central Calling figure sets the kind of magic: recording a phrase and echoing it back. The four Convergence signs are evenly spaced around it with points turned inward, which focuses the spell's magic down toward a single point. The filled triangles on the ring and the two vertical lines are not matched signs, so their exact roles cannot be read individually. Their mirrored placement at north and south suggests they belong to the outer layer of the seal, which drives pursuit of a destination, while the Calling sigil forms the inner layer that handles the recorded sound.
effect: Makes the target repeatedly echo a recorded phrase while it pursues a target destination.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a diamond, flanked east and west by two half-lens shapes whose curved sides point inward toward it. Together these form the Calling sigil. Two long vertical lines run north to south on either side of the diamond. They bow inward at the middle, where the tips of the half-lens shapes meet them. At the four intercardinal points sit four Convergence triangles, each with one point aimed toward the center. There are no filled triangles and no other signs.
justification: The Calling sigil sets the magic: it records a phrase and echoes it repeatedly. The four Convergence signs are evenly placed, each with a point aimed inward, so the magic centers down on a single point. This gives the spell a focused target to move toward. The two vertical lines have no established sign meaning on their own. The seal works as two layers: a recorded-sound part around the Calling sigil and a pursuit part around it.
effect: Records a spoken phrase and makes its target echo that phrase over and over while it travels toward a set destination.

name: Purify
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a water sigil: an S-curve flanked by two droplets, with the left droplet pointing up and the right droplet pointing down. A Refuse sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. In each, the diamond lies toward the ring and the crossed legs reach toward the sigil. Ten Purification signs, curled hooks, surround the center. Five arc over the top half from west to east, and five arc under the bottom half, mirroring the upper set.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. The many Purification signs, an asymmetric sign tied to cleaning water, direct that water magic toward separating out impurities. The two Refuse signs are directional signs that collect unwanted material and waste toward where they point. Placed on either side of the sigil, they gather the separated waste. Together these form a water-cleaning seal.
effect: Purifies wastewater by separating waste from the water, leaving it clean and collecting the unwanted material aside.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An animated frame in which a cupped hand holds a small stack of paper with a seal drawn on the top sheet. The ring is fully visible and closed, foreshortened into an oval by the angle. A small sigil sits at the center, and its lines are consistent with a fire sigil, though the detail is soft at this size. Four signs are spaced evenly at the north, south, east and west points. Each is an arrow-like shape with a crossbar that matches the Levitation sign, with its pointed end facing inward. No other signs are visible, and nothing covers the seal.
justification: The central fire sigil sets the element to flame, and its small size relative to the ring points to a modest flame. Levitation signs float the spell's magic and any light object above the seal, with their length setting carrying weight, distance or speed. Four of them placed evenly around the center keep the effect balanced, which lets the flame gather and hover rather than drift in one direction.
effect: Creates a ball of flame that levitates directly above the seal. It can also float a light object along with the flame. The number of Levitation signs can vary without changing the basic effect.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A manga panel with a small seal drawn on a sheet of paper lying on a table, seen at a steep angle. The ring is closed. A small mark at the center resembles a fire sigil. Four short arrow-like signs sit around it, roughly at the north, south, east and west points. A wisp of drawn smoke trails down into the upper part of the seal and overlaps it. At this size and angle, the exact shapes of the sigil and signs cannot be confirmed.
justification: The central mark most likely sets the element as fire. The four evenly spaced arrow-like signs match the shape of Levitation signs, which float the magic and light objects above the seal. Evenly balanced Levitation holds the flame in place as a sphere rather than sending it in one direction. Because the glyph is tiny and partly overlapped, this reading depends on the signs being Levitation rather than Columns.
effect: If the signs are Levitation, the spell creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can lift light objects with it. If they are Columns instead, the flame also sets the surface the seal is drawn on alight.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An anime frame of two hands over a round notebook page, one holding a pen with its nib resting on the ring line at the upper left. The seal is fully visible, and the ring appears closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center, slightly tilted. Four Levitation signs sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest and southeast points, evenly spaced, each with its arrow pointing inward toward the sigil. The fingers rest on the page's edge outside the ring and do not cover any sign.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces flame. Its small size relative to the ring means a modest intensity. Levitation is a directional sign that floats its target above the seal, and four of them placed evenly and pointing inward keep it balanced, which shapes the flame into a sphere and holds it in place rather than pushing it to one side.
effect: Creates a small ball of flame that floats directly above the seal. It can also lift light objects along with it. The length and number of the Levitation signs set how much weight the spell can carry.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An anime frame of a seal drawn on a sheet of paper on the grass, viewed from above at a distance. Glowing light washes over the sheet. The ring appears closed and fully visible. Four short signs sit evenly at the north, south, east, and west points, all of similar length. Their shape fits Levitation or Columns, but at this size it is unclear whether they end in arrowheads. A small mark sits at the center where a sigil would be, too tiny and washed out by the glow to identify.
justification: Four equal signs spaced evenly around the center make a balanced seal, so the spell should act straight up from the seal rather than leaning to one side. If the signs are Levitation, the spell floats its magic above the seal. If they are Columns, it projects the magic upward as a column. The center sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the glyph itself.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the image because the sigil is unreadable. Assuming the center is a fire sigil and the four signs are Levitation, the spell creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can also lift objects that are not too heavy. If the signs are Columns instead, the flame would also set the surface the seal is drawn on alight.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A line drawing of a small round disc with a seal drawn on it, lying among a ring of scattered leaves. The inner ring of the seal looks closed, and the seal is fully visible, though small. A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn rotated so its triangle points to the right, with its side strokes and stem crossing it. About four small T-shaped signs are spaced evenly around the sigil near the ring. They resemble Columns signs, but they are tiny and only roughly legible.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element to flame. It takes up a moderate share of the ring, which suggests ordinary intensity. The modifiers are spaced evenly around it, so their pull is balanced and no single direction dominates. Columns signs send the spell's effect upward as a column above the seal. A balanced fire seal of this layout is the Pyreball Seal, drawn here in its Columns form rather than with Levitation signs.
effect: Creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can carry light objects with it. In this Columns form, the surface the seal is drawn on is also set alight along with the flame.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the lower left. A large fire sigil sits at the center, taking up a good share of the ring's interior. Four Levitation signs sit evenly at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward at the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces flame, and its large size relative to the ring means a fairly strong flame. Levitation is a directional sign that floats its target. With four identical signs spaced evenly and all pointing inward, the lift is balanced, which shapes the flame into a sphere and holds it directly above the seal rather than sending it in any one direction. Because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it creates a ball of fire that floats directly above the seal. The Levitation signs can also lift objects that are not too heavy, and the number and length of those signs set how much weight can be carried.

name: Qifrey's Water Dragon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. Four water sigils sit in the outer band at the north, east, south, and west points. Each is flanked by a pair of Columns signs, giving eight in total, with their crossbars toward the ring and stems pointing inward. Four Expansion signs, each made of three nested corner brackets, sit at the four intercardinal points with their corners pointing outward. Inside these is a pentagon with a short tick at each vertex pointing outward and five small water droplets just outside its edges. Within the pentagon, four Convergence triangles sit at the north, east, south, and west, each with a point facing inward. The center holds a Dragon decorative sigil: an angular, zig-zag body with fin-like strokes, a triangular head at the upper right, and a curved tail below.
justification: The four water sigils make this a water spell. The Dragon sigil at the center shapes that water into a dragon. The pentagon with droplets is a variant of the Flower sigil, with its arches replaced by water droplets, and it gives the water the form of a water lily. The inward-pointing Convergence signs draw the surrounding water together to a single point so the spell can use it. The Expansion signs have their corners pointing outward, which makes the shape grow. The eight Columns signs are evenly balanced around the ring, so they drive the magic straight out from the seal.
effect: Draws water from nearby clouds, and likely from bodies of water, and forms it into a giant dragon made of water. The dragon then turns into a water lily before the spell stops working.

name: Qifrey's Water Dragon
description: A manga page with several panels. Most panels show figures and a large dragon shape, with no glyph in them. At the bottom right of the lowest panel, a small slice of a seal shows along the panel border, with part of the ring's edge curving across it. A few signs are partly visible on this slice. One resembles a Selection sign, a square crossed by lines. Another resembles an Orb sign, a circle with a vertical line. Fragments of other marks sit beside them but are too small or too cut off to name. The center of the seal, any sigil, and the rest of the ring lie outside the panel, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: Only a narrow edge of the seal is visible and no sigil can be seen, so the element of the spell is unknown. The few signs that can be made out are modifiers. A Selection-like sign would limit the effect to the object it is drawn on, and an Orb-like sign would gather material in a spherical space. Without the sigil and the remaining signs, these fragments cannot be combined into a spell.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because the visible fragment shows no sigil and too few signs to identify the spell.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal in black ink on a white background, with the ring closed. A large Rain sign fills most of the interior, drawn slightly tilted: a square with inward-curving sides, with a set of about three parallel lines crossing each side and reaching out toward the ring. A water sigil sits in the open center of the Rain sign, turned on its side, with its S-curve between the two droplets. No other signs are present.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works on water. The Rain sign is semi-directional and, when not inverted, summons its target; a sigil can be placed in its center, as it is here. Together they call water down from above. The sigil is moderate in size relative to the ring, so the intensity is moderate. Because the line work and ring are loose and uneven, the result may vary, since the quality of the ring strongly shapes this spell.
effect: Summons rain. Water falls from above, either as a single mass that drops abruptly or as gentle, gradual rainfall. The quality of the ring and the sign lines plays a significant role in which of these happens.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: An anime frame of a stack of round paper discs held from the side by a hand, with a pen nib resting on the top disc. The seal on the top disc is fully visible, seen at an angle. A water sigil, two drops flanking an S-curve, sits at the center inside a Rain sign: a four-pointed star with curved, inward-bowing edges, its points facing north, east, south and west, with three parallel lines crossing each of the four diagonal corners. The Rain sign is drawn in its normal orientation, not inverted. A thin ring runs near the edge of the disc. The pen nib touches it on the west side, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is closed. The water sigil is fairly large within the ring.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The Rain sign surrounds the sigil, which sits in its empty center, and in its normal orientation it summons the spell's material from above rather than pushing it away. A water sigil inside an upright Rain sign therefore brings down water as rainfall. The fairly large sigil suggests a moderately strong effect. How evenly the ring is drawn changes how the rain manifests.
effect: Summons rain, making water fall from above onto the area. Depending on the quality of the ring, the water either gathers into an orb overhead that drops all at once or falls gently and gradually like natural rainfall.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a wind sigil drawn as a horizontal double spiral, with no flanking strokes visible. Two smaller fire sigils sit at the north and south points, each with its apex pointing toward the center, so the northern one appears upside down. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, for two in total.
justification: The large central wind sigil sets the main element, so the spell moves air. The two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity, which makes this a mixed wind and fire spell. Crosshair directs a seal's magic at whatever its shorter ends point toward, so the two Crosshair signs aim the heat into the surrounding air. Together they produce moving, heated air.
effect: Creates warm winds that evaporate moisture and dry objects within the seal's radius.

name: Rainflinger
description: A line drawing of two hands holding an unrolled scroll with an oval seal drawn on it. The ring appears closed, though the right thumb rests over its lower-right edge. A wind sigil sits at the center, drawn as an S-curve with short dashes on either side. Two smaller fire sigils flank it, one to the upper left and one to the lower right, both tilted. Small Crosshair signs mark the north and south of the ring, with a few loose dashes near them. The signs are drawn loosely and at small size, but each one can be identified.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the main element as moving air. The two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity than the wind, because they are smaller relative to the ring. Crosshair is a directional sign that aims the seal's magic at whatever its shorter ends point toward. Here the Crosshair signs direct the heat onto the moving air, so the seal produces warm wind.
effect: Sends warm wind across the area of the seal, evaporating moisture and drying anything within its radius.

name: Rainwarding
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a large Rain sign drawn inside-out: a square with concave sides and pointed corners, with three lines on each side pointing inward toward the empty middle instead of outward. No element sigil is drawn in the center. A Regions sign sits at each of the north, south, east, and west points, all four pointing inward, each with a straight bar between it and the central sign. Two smaller unmatched signs flank each Regions sign, eight in total, each a short diagonal line with one dot on either side.
justification: Rain is semi-directional and radially symmetric, so turning its lines inward flips it inside-out and inverts it. An inverted Rain creates an area where the target cannot exist or is pushed away, the reverse of summoning it. The four inward-pointing Regions signs confine the magic to the space inside the ring. The barred lines and the dotted diagonal signs cannot be matched to any known sign, so their part in the spell is unknown.
effect: Removes water from a set space, keeping the area dry by pushing water out or preventing it from being there.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as a double ring: an outer circle and an inner circle, both closed, so the ring is closed. The inner circle is empty, with no sigil at the center. Four small Repetition signs sit on the band between the two circles at the north, east, south and west points. Between them, eight groups each consist of a Convergence triangle flanked by two Columns signs, giving sixteen Columns and eight Convergence in all. Each Columns sign has its crossbar toward the outer circle and its stem toward the center. Each Convergence triangle has one point aimed inward.
justification: No element sigil is present. The four Repetition signs take that role, and Repetition is the sign that continuously resets a target to the state it had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs create column-shaped areas of effect and set the range or quantity of the magic. Their even spacing around the ring balances the effect so it pushes in no single direction. The inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and pack loose particles tightly together. Because the Repetition signs sit on the band rather than in the middle, the empty inner circle is left as the space where the target rests.
effect: Continuously reverts the target to the state it had when the spell first affected it, so any change is undone and the object stays like new. This restores its physical form and its temperature, so it can make soft objects spring back into shape, keep things from rotting, or repair damage.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The inner circle is empty, with no sigil at the center. Four Repetition glyphs sit in the band between the rings, at the north, east, south and west points, each rotated to follow the curve of the ring. Each of the four arcs between them holds the same sequence: a Columns sign, a Convergence triangle, and a second Columns sign. That makes eight Columns signs in total, each with its crossbar toward the outer ring and its stem toward the center. Each Convergence triangle sits with one point angled inward.
justification: No element sigil is present. Repetition takes that role instead, repeated four times around the band, and it remains a sign that sets the time-resetting behavior. The Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect, and because their stems all point inward they aim it at the empty inner circle. The Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and pack it tightly. Together they concentrate the resetting effect on whatever occupies the inner circle. The arrangement is symmetric in all four directions, so no direction is favored.
effect: Continuously resets the target to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, physical form and temperature included, so it stays like new. This keeps soft material springy, stops things from rotting, and undoes damage or other changes.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a gap at the lower left. An outer band of sixteen Convergence triangles runs around the inside of the ring, each with one point aimed inward. Inside that band are six Repetition signs in a hexagonal arrangement: one north, one south, and one at each of the four diagonals. At the center sits a circle with four Diamond-shaped points straddling its edge at north, south, east and west, plus four short ticks on the circle at the intercardinal points. No element sigil is present.
justification: There is no element sigil; Repetition takes that role here, as one of the few signs that can stand in for a sigil, and six copies multiply its time-resetting effect around the seal. The sixteen inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and draw it tightly together at the center. The central circle with four Diamonds suggests the effect is limited to the contents held by the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn.
effect: Once the ring is closed, the seal continuously resets its target to the state it was in when the spell first took hold, keeping it like new by restoring its form and temperature whenever it changes, for example by stopping food from rotting. The Diamonds likely confine this effect to whatever the marked container holds.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. The center holds a Repetition sign in place of a sigil, drawn as a small inner circle inside a larger circle, with a long S-shaped stroke running through both and sweeping out into open arcs at the upper left and lower right. Six Columns signs sit in two groups of three, one group arcing from the west-northwest to the north and the other mirrored from the south to the southeast. Each Columns sign lies sideways along the ring, with its stem pointing counterclockwise. At the northeast and southwest sit two large X-shaped crosses whose strokes meet off-center. They resemble Collection signs without the closing bar. No element sigil is present.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Repetition sign drives the spell. It resets whatever it affects to the state the object had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs, all turned the same way around the ring, push that effect in a rotating, column-shaped area rather than one straight direction. The two X-shaped crosses, if read as Collection, gather material from around the seal for the spell to act on. The ring is open, so the spell is not active as drawn.
effect: Continuously reverts a target object to its earlier state after any change, keeping it like new. It can restore an object's shape and temperature, keep things from rotting, or make soft materials spring back to their original form.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible diagram of a large seal with a thick outer ring, ring closed, and a smaller closed inner ring at its center. Four Repetition signs, each in its own small circle, sit on the outer band at the north, east, south, and west points. Between them sit groups of a Convergence triangle flanked by two Columns signs. Inside the inner ring, a Billow sign sits at the center with Collection signs to the north and south and Convergence triangles to the east and west. Four small circles around it each hold a small seal with an earth sigil, Columns signs, and Crushing signs. Three labeled insets sit outside the main seal: a small earth seal labeled Wall Breaker, a Billow-centered cluster labeled Billow Cluster, and a lone Repetition sign labeled Sign of Repetition.
justification: This is a compound seal with no single element sigil at its center. The four small earth seals with Columns and Crushing are Wall Breaker seals, which crush stone into sand. The central Billow cluster works as follows: Collection gathers that material, Convergence packs the loose particles together, and Billow, sitting in place of a sigil, turns them into a soft cloud-like mass. The outer band of Repetition signs, flanked by Convergence and Columns, keeps resetting the result to its original state. Together these let the crushed sand take its shape and keep returning to it.
effect: Crushes stone into sand, gathers and packs it into a soft, billowing bed that is comfortable to rest on, and continuously reverts it to its original state whenever it is disturbed or changed.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A manga panel. A hand grips a round, flat object seen almost edge-on, so the seal on its face is heavily foreshortened. The ring follows the rim and is visible along the right edge, but the left side curves away behind the hand and the thickness of the rim, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. Two Repetition glyphs are clearly visible down the middle: circles with an inner spiral, a central dot, and short tick lines. Partial copies of the same glyph appear at the top and bottom edges. Between them sits a lumpy, cloud-like cluster of scalloped shapes around an oval with dots and lines, possibly a Billow sign, but it is too distorted to identify with confidence. Along the right inner edge runs a row of small triangles resembling Convergence signs, alternating with chevron and zigzag marks that may be Crushing or Collection signs. The left portion of the seal is hidden.
justification: Repetition can stand in the center in place of a sigil, and here several Repetition glyphs repeated across the seal make Repetition the core of the spell, so the seal's job is to keep resetting its target. The ring of Convergence-like triangles around the edge would focus the magic and pack loose material tightly, and the possible Crushing, Collection, and Billow-like marks would gather and shape material. These modifiers cannot be confirmed at this angle and only refine how the resetting is applied.
effect: Continuously reverts the target object to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, so it stays like new and snaps back if changed. This reading rests on the clearly visible Repetition glyphs and assumes the hidden left side carries the same arrangement as the visible right side.

name: Repetition Seal
description: Two manga panels. In the left panel a round wooden lid with a seal drawn on it is held up near the left edge, and the panel border cuts off its left side. A Repetition glyph sits at the center: a ring with an inner curl around a central dot. Diagonal strokes cross through it in an X-like pattern. Small marks run around the inner edge of the ring but are too small to identify. Because the left side is cut off, it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. The right panel shows barrels and a loose lid with no legible seal.
justification: Repetition can sit in the center in place of a sigil. Here it takes that central spot, so the seal works on time rather than on an element. The surrounding modifiers are illegible at this size, so only the core behavior can be read.
effect: Continuously resets the target to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, keeping it like new. The exact variant cannot be read from the image because the surrounding signs are illegible.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A manga panel showing a round object with a seal drawn on it. A Repetition sign sits at the center, drawn as a small circle with an inner curve around a dot. Small signs ring it: X-shaped marks that resemble Collection signs on the right and lower left, Y-shaped marks near the top and lower left, and a row of three T-shaped marks along the bottom that resemble Columns signs. The upper-left quarter is covered by heavy dark hatching and a pointed object, which hide the signs and the ring there. The ring looks unbroken where it can be seen, but its hidden portion cannot be checked, so it is not known whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: The Repetition sign takes the place of a sigil at the center, so this is a repetition seal. Repetition continuously resets what the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. The surrounding signs are too small and partly hidden to identify with certainty. They would set what material the spell targets and how it is shaped.
effect: Continuously reverts the target object to its earlier state whenever it changes, keeping it like new. The exact variant cannot be determined because the surrounding signs are obscured.

name: Ring of Fire
description: A manga panel of two hands holding a stack of round discs, with a pen nib touching the top disc. A small, foreshortened mark that resembles a fire sigil, a triangle with short strokes, sits near the middle of the top disc, next to a smaller cross-like stroke. The pen and the steep angle hide most of the drawing. No ring edge and no surrounding signs can be made out.
justification: The triangular mark points to a fire sigil, which sets the spell as fire magic. The signs that would set how the fire behaves cannot be read, and the ring cannot be seen, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed.
effect: The visible sigil indicates a spell that creates fire. How the fire is shaped or directed cannot be determined from the image.

name: Ring of Fire
description: A manga panel of a caped, hatted figure in the middle of a large circle of flames, with heavy action lines and sound effect lettering on both sides. The round shape is made of fire, not ink, and no ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The circle of flames is a magical effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Rising Platform of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the lower left. A large water sigil fills the center. Four Levitation signs sit near the north, east, south and west points, each turned sideways so its arrow runs along the ring rather than toward or away from the center. Together they form a pinwheel pointing clockwise. Four Columns signs sit at the four intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing at the sigil.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring makes the effect strong. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Four of them placed evenly means the column is balanced and rises straight rather than leaning to one side. Levitation floats the target. Because these directional signs are turned sideways and spaced evenly around the ring, their sideways pulls cancel out, leaving only the lift. Together these signs make a lifting column of water.
effect: Generates a surging column of water that lifts the object the seal is drawn on straight up into the air. The ring is open, so the spell is not yet active.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel of a figure crouched atop a rising surge of water, with part of a hat brim at the right edge. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The wave is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel showing a pair of boots stepping on the ground beneath the hem of a robe. Several curved ink strokes on the ground form arcs that look like parts of a seal's ring, possibly two concentric arcs, with sections passing under and behind the boots. No sigil and no signs are visible. The interior of the arcs is blank or covered by the boots, and the edges of the curves run out of frame or fade into the ground texture, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: Only ring-like arcs are legible. Without a visible sigil or any signs, there is nothing to decode, and the element and modifiers cannot be read from this image.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, since no sigil or signs are visible.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel with a figure standing on a large seal drawn on the ground, seen at a steep angle. Only the far arc of the ring shows along the bottom edge of the panel, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed. Along the inside of that arc, small signs alternate between T-shaped Columns signs and V-shaped Regions signs. The figure's boots cover part of the arc. The center of the seal, where a sigil would sit, is out of frame, and so are any inner signs.
justification: Columns sets a column-shaped area of effect, pushed in a given direction. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the ring. Alternating them around the outer edge suggests a forceful column rising from the seal. Because the center is hidden, the sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the image.
effect: Assuming the hidden center holds a water sigil and the rest of the ring repeats the visible Columns and Regions pattern, the spell raises a surge of water high into the air and carries whoever stands on the seal up with it. The element itself cannot be determined from the visible part.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel showing a tall surge of water rising and curling upward from a rocky area, with a tattered cloak edge at the left and the sound effect "FWOOM" across the top. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the image.
justification: Nothing to decode. The rising water is a spell effect, not a glyph, so there are no signs or sigil to read.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a wind sigil at the center flanked by three short tick marks on each side. Six Levitation signs point inward toward the sigil, one at the east, one at the west, and four on the diagonals between them. Each Levitation sign has a small two-line sign shaped like an equal sign just beyond its outer end, making six of these unidentified signs in all. Six larger glyphs alternate with them, at the north, the south, and the four remaining diagonals. Each is a Columns sign with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing inward, capped by an inward-pointing Regions chevron. The pairing makes each one look like an enlarged Levitation sign. The arrangement is radially balanced.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing air rather than creating it. The inward Levitation signs set the air in motion and carry force. The Columns signs gather the effect into a column or beam, and the inward-pointing Regions signs keep it manifesting from within the ring. Because all six of each sign are balanced around the center, no single side dominates. The result is a steady, even stream of air from the seal's face rather than a lopsided burst. The function of the equal-sign marks is unknown.
effect: Creates a steady, continuous gust of wind from the face of the seal. The gust pushes a sail and propels a water vessel using air.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A manga panel showing a round disc with a seal drawn on it, mounted on a short post. A large dark shape in the foreground covers the left half of the disc. On the visible right portion, the edge of the ring and a scattering of small strokes can be seen, some of them arrow-like, but they are too small and roughly drawn to match to any sign. The center of the seal is not visible, so no sigil can be identified. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told.
justification: There is nothing reliable to decode. Without a visible sigil, no element can be set, and the few marks on the exposed edge are too indistinct to name as specific signs.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: An anime frame of a large round wooden disc with a seal drawn on it. The right third of the disc is cut off by the frame edge, so the seal is only partly visible, and whether the ring is open or closed cannot be confirmed. A wind sigil sits at the center, flanked by its short side strokes. Rays of signs radiate from the center toward the edge, about four of them visible on the left and lower half. Each ray has an equal-sign mark near the rim, then a Columns sign, then an arrow pointing inward that resembles Levitation. One of these inward arrows sits at the north, and Columns signs mark the west and south points. A separate block mounted at the top of the disc carries a Columns sign over an inward-pointing Regions shape. The signs on the right side are hidden past the frame edge.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air. The Columns signs give that air a column-shaped area of effect and push it in a set direction. The inward arrows, in the Levitation and Regions style, set where the effect manifests and how strongly it pushes. The equal-sign marks are unidentified modifiers. Together they form a seal that drives a directed current of air outward from its face.
effect: Produces a steady gust of wind that pushes against a sail to propel a water vehicle forward. This assumes the hidden right side mirrors the visible rays, completing the six-fold pattern.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A large round disc carrying a seal, with a standing figure covering its left half. Only part of a wind sigil is visible at the center: the right side of its S-curve peeks out beside the figure's arm, along with the short tick marks on its right. Three small Levitation signs are visible on the right side, at the northeast, east and southeast, each pointing inward toward the sigil. Three equal-sign shapes, each made of two parallel strokes, sit near the rim outside them in the same three directions. Larger signs that look like a Columns sign joined to a Regions chevron sit at the north, northeast, southeast and south; the north one sits in a squared notch at the top edge, and the south one is partly hidden by the figure's hand. No separate ring line can be seen apart from the disc edge, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed. Everything on the left half is hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air rather than creating it. The Levitation signs and the Columns-and-Regions pairs are directional signs. Columns sends magic out as a beam with pressure in a set direction, Regions decides where the magic manifests, and Levitation moves the target, so together they drive a steady push of air. The equal-sign shapes have no known effect. The visible right half is evenly arranged in sixfold groups, so the hidden left half is assumed to mirror it.
effect: Produces a steady gust of wind that pushes a sail forward and propels a water vehicle. This assumes the hidden left half mirrors the visible right half. The spell is toggled by a small gap in the ring that can be pushed closed to activate it.

name: Sand Bridge
description: A fully visible glowing seal on a stone surface, made of two concentric rings, both closed. Inside the inner ring is a Sigil of Sand: a vertical stroke with an S-curve wound around it. On each side of the sigil sits a dot and an inward-pointing chevron. In the outer band, the north and south points each hold an Immobility sign between two Solidification signs, each drawn as two small circles joined by a line. The east and west sides mirror each other from top to bottom. Each side has small outward-facing Partition signs near the corners, then Strengthening signs, then Columns signs. At the east and west points are a Binding curve and a Sigil of Bridging, an arch over short vertical strokes. The glow softens some fine strokes, but every glyph is readable.
justification: The Sigil of Sand sets the material, so the spell moves existing sand rather than creating it. The second ring adds further effects and stronger magic to the core spell. The Columns signs raise the sand upward, and the Sigil of Bridging shapes it into a bridge with a flat walkway and arches. Solidification makes the sand more solid, and Binding makes it act as a single unit. Immobility holds that shape in place, and Strengthening makes it harder and more durable. The Partition signs outline the area the structure fills.
effect: Raises large amounts of sand into an arch bridge. The bridge hardens and keeps its shape until the magic wears off, and it can bear the weight of people and their cargo while it lasts.

name: Sasaran's Cloak Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two rings. The outer band is a double ring packed with repeated chevron markings, matching the Windows sign, which lines the seal like an extra ring. Inside it, a thicker inner ring holds the main body. It appears to have a small break at the upper left, so it reads as ring open there. At the center is a Concealment sign: an eight-armed star with four eye shapes set on its diagonals. Four wind sigils sit north, east, south, and west of the star, each flanked by small tick marks resembling short Columns signs. At the four cardinal points on the inner ring sit loop-and-arc shapes matching the parts of the Dancing Puppets sign. At the four intercardinal points, four Envelopment signs cross the inner ring, each with small Columns-like marks beside them.
justification: The four wind sigils set the element: moving and manipulating air. Combined with the Dancing Puppets loops on the ring, wind lets the target object fly and be steered within the air from a distance. The central Concealment sign hides the target, and the four Envelopment signs make that effect surround whatever the seal is drawn on. The outer Windows ring connects two spaces that are not physically joined, so magic can pass through the seal from one location to another.
effect: Wraps the object the seal is drawn on in concealing shadow. It lets that object be flown and steered from afar, and lets spells be cast through it remotely, as if through a portal, while the caster stays somewhere else.

name: Scalewolf Curse
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The ring is doubled, with a band between the inner and outer circles, and triangular points ring the outside: four large points at north, east, south, and west, and smaller points spaced evenly between them. At the center sit three dots arranged in a triangle, one above and two below. An arc curves over the dots like a dome, and its ends meet a horizontal bar beneath them. Four short vertical stems hang from the bar, each ending in a downward fork. This shape resembles the lower half of a Gathering sign but does not match any known sign exactly.
justification: The three-dot triangle is the sigil and sets what kind of magic the spell is. It is not one of the elemental sigils. The same sigil appears in a labyrinth illusion seal. The arc, bar, and four forked stems, and the spiked double ring around them, do not match any known sign. Their individual roles cannot be decoded. They are what turn the magic into a lasting change to the target's body rather than a passing effect.
effect: A forbidden spell that permanently transforms a person's body. If the target is wearing something made with scalewolf fur and scales, that item fuses with them and they are turned into a scalewolf.

name: Seal of Expansion and Levitation
description: A fully visible seal drawn in orange on a yellow background, ring closed. A Selection sign sits at the center. Four Expansion signs, each a set of three nested right-angle brackets, frame it at the intercardinal points with their corners pointing outward. Stability and Level Planes signs, each made of three wavy lines, sit in the four gaps between the Expansion signs at north, south, east and west. Eight small Columns signs sit near the ring, two in each intercardinal space beside the outer corners of the Expansion signs. They are faint and small but readable.
justification: There is no element sigil. The seal is built entirely from signs, with Selection at the center taking the place of a sigil. Selection limits the spell to the object the seal is drawn on. The Expansion signs have their corners pointing outward, which is their normal orientation, so they make that object grow; corners pointing inward would shrink it instead. Stability and Level Planes balance the target in a plane in the air, which supplies the floating. The eight Columns signs are balanced around the ring, so they give a column-shaped area of effect with no lean in any one direction. The arrangement reads as an expansion effect and a levitation effect drawn together in one ring.
effect: Makes the object the seal is drawn on grow in size and float steadily in the air, balanced on a level plane.

At its center is a dense, cross-hatched knot of lines that cannot be matched to any known sigil or sign. Inside the ring sit several smaller sub-rings holding clusters of loop-shaped figures, with many small marks scattered between them. Outside the main ring, satellite circles are joined to it by short lines: a few large ones and several small ones. The satellites at the left and right edges are cut off by the frame and partly hidden behind thick curved shapes crossing the panel. Every sign is too small and too blurred to identify.
justification: Nothing can be decoded with confidence. The central glyph matches no element sigil, and no surrounding sign is legible enough to name. The layout, a main seal ringed by linked satellite seals, shows that several sub-spells are combined, but what each one contributes cannot be read.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the visible signs. The spell as a whole is known to drive and control the movement of a legged chair.

name: Serpent's Bed of Sand
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, built from three nested rings, all closed. The outer band, between the outer and middle rings, holds four Repetition signs at the north, east, south, and west points, each sitting across the inner edge of the band. Each quadrant between them has a Columns sign, then a Convergence triangle, then another Columns sign, for eight Columns and four Convergence in total. Each Columns sign has its crossbar on the outer side and its stem pointing toward the center, and each Convergence triangle has one point facing the center. Inside the middle ring, a small central ring holds a Billow sign at its center, with four Collection signs at the intercardinal points around it. Four smaller rings sit at the intercardinal points, each linked by short lines to both the central ring and the middle ring. Each small ring holds a diagonally turned earth sigil, two small Columns signs along the diagonal, and two angular stepped marks on either side that match Crushing signs.
justification: The seal combines several linked seals. The central ring is Billow in the sigil position, with Collection signs that gather surrounding material and turn it into a cloud. Each of the four linked rings pairs an earth sigil with Crushing and Columns signs, which is the core that crushes ground into fine sand. Their links feed that sand into the central cloud. The outer band uses Repetition in place of sigils, together with Convergence and Columns. Convergence packs loose particles tightly, and Repetition keeps resetting the cloud to its first state, so it cannot lose its consistency.
effect: Crushes the surrounding ground into fine, soft sand and gathers it into a large, fluffy cloud. The cloud is strong enough to hold up even a dragon. Because it keeps resetting to its original state, it regains its shape once the weight is removed.

Farther out, a Columns sign sits at each of those four points. Four small hash-like marks of crossed double lines sit at the intercardinal points; they are too small and rough to match to a known sign. No element sigil is visible.

Together they form the billow cluster core, which turns gathered material into a fluffy cloud. The Columns signs give the magic a direction and range. The earth component, which crushes ground into sand, and the Repetition component, which restores the cloud's shape, cannot be read here. The hash-like marks may stand in for those components, but that cannot be confirmed.
effect: Gathers surrounding material and turns it into a fluffy cloud. The full spell crushes the ground into soft sand and forms it into a large cloud strong enough to hold a dragon, and the cloud returns to its original shape once the weight is removed. name: Slime Rendering Seal
description: A manga panel showing the outline of a human body lying flat, with a network of seals drawn across it. On the chest is a small closed ring holding a curled glyph that loosely resembles the Wind sign but does not clearly match any known sigil. About six lines radiate out from this ring, each ending in a Glaives sign, so the Glaives sit outside the ring while staying connected to it. Beside the torso are three small two-circle shapes similar to Solidification, and a line with short side branches runs down from the chest to a second ring on the belly. That ring is mostly hidden by a large white speech bubble, and only part of an unreadable glyph inside it shows. One arm carries lines with bands at the elbow and wrist and Glaives at the ends. The legs carry herringbone lines with bands near the ankles and Glaives at the tips. The hips and the upper part of the legs are covered by the speech bubble.
justification: Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, and they are the only sign that can be drawn outside the ring as long as it stays connected. Here they run along the chest, arm and legs, which spreads that deep embedding across the whole body. The two-circle shapes resemble Solidification, which makes the magic connected to them more solid. The central curled glyph and the hidden belly ring cannot be matched to known signs or sigils, so the element and most modifiers cannot be read directly.
effect: A forbidden spell that transforms the target's body into slime. The Glaives drive the magic deep into the flesh throughout the body. The exact mechanism cannot be decoded from the visible glyphs.

name: Smokesculpting Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a spiral with a vertical line running through it. The line ends at the north point in an asterisk-like starburst and at the south point in a stem with two stacked chevrons, close to a Pulling or Gathering shape. Two zigzag signs that match inverted Crushing flank the spiral to the east and west. Four Columns signs sit around the spiral, two above and two below. Four teardrop signs shaped like the drops of the water sigil sit at the intercardinal points. At the east and west points are two more asterisk-like starbursts, each fused with a short line like a Columns sign. No standard element sigil from the fire, water, earth, wind, or light set is present.
justification: The central spiral with its vertical shaft does not match any known sigil or sign, so it takes the sigil's place and likely sets the spell's unusual material. The teardrops echo the water sigil's drops and suggest vapor or steam rather than solid matter. Inverted Crushing reforms crushed material into its original shape, as in Integration. The Columns signs send the result upward in a column above the seal. The starburst and Columns hybrids likely spread or shape the airy material, but their exact rule is not known.
effect: Creates a sculpture of smoke, or possibly steam, that recreates the shape of the ingredients added to tea. Instead of reforming the ingredients themselves, it rebuilds their form out of smoke.

Two wavy signs that match Crushing sit directly east and west of the spiral, facing outward, so they are inverted. Further out at east and west are asterisk-like signs joined to a short bar, resembling an asterisk fused with a Columns sign. Several T-shaped Columns signs are spaced around the upper and lower arcs. Small raindrop shapes like the drops of the water sigil sit near the ring at the upper and lower corners. The inverted Crushing signs reverse the crushing effect, so material is reformed into its original shape rather than broken apart. The Columns signs send that effect upward in a column above the seal. The raindrop signs echo the water sigil's drops, which fits a vapor or steam component. The asterisk-and-column hybrids and the north and south terminals of the central line do not match any known sign, so their exact role is uncertain.
effect: Creates a sculpture of smoke, or possibly steam, above the seal that recreates the original shape of ingredients added to tea. It reforms the shape of nearby ingredients in smoke instead of reforming the ingredients themselves.

name: Snowfending
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the ring closed. A fire sigil sits at the center, about a third the width of the ring. A Stillness sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. A hooked S-shaped curve sits at the north point, with a mirrored copy at the south point. It resembles the central stroke of the wind sigil without its side marks. Four two-line Stability and Level Planes signs flank these S curves, one on each side at north and at south. Four forked signs, each a long stroke aimed at the center with two short prongs opening outward, sit at the four intercardinal points. They do not clearly match any named sign. The layout is symmetric left to right and top to bottom.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a heat spell, and its moderate size suggests a steady rather than violent output. The Stability and Level Planes signs keep the effect balanced as a level plane. The Stillness signs hold the magical effect static in a single location instead of letting it drift or disperse. The S-shaped signs echo the wind sigil and probably tie the heat to the surrounding air. The forked signs at the intercardinal points have no known meaning, so their role in shaping the spell is unclear.
effect: Holds a steady layer of warmth in place over a target area, keeping snow from settling on whatever lies beneath it.

name: Snugstone Spell

A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn fairly large, with its three short strokes extended so they cross into the triangle. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, all inverted, with the crossbar toward the center and the stem pointing outward toward the ring. At the north, east, south and west points sit four matching signs that do not match any named sign: each is a large arc with a smaller cup nested inside it, both opening outward toward the ring.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as fire or heat, and its size relative to the ring sets the intensity, tuned so the output stays mild. Inverted Columns spread their effect horizontally rather than as a vertical beam, similar to Dispersion, so the heat radiates outward in all directions instead of shooting upward. The four nested-arc signs are arranged symmetrically and are likely what tones the fire down into gentle warmth without a flame, though their exact rule is unknown. Because the ring is open, the seal is inactive as drawn.
effect: Radiates gentle warmth outward without producing a flame, balanced so the surface is warm to the touch but never hot enough to burn.

The ring appears closed, but a jagged crack runs across the whole seal from the west edge through the center to the east side, and smaller cracks branch toward the north. A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn small relative to the ring and split by the crack. Inverted Columns signs sit at the south and east points, with the crossbar toward the sigil and the stem toward the ring. Curled hook-shaped symbols that match no named sign sit at the southwest and southeast, and similar curls appear at the northwest and northeast where the crack lines run through them. The north and west points are obscured by the crack and the shading, so any signs there cannot be read.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring keeps the output gentle. Inverted Columns spread their effect sideways instead of beaming it upward, much like Dispersion, so the heat leaks evenly outward rather than shooting in one direction. The unidentified curled symbols probably temper the fire, turning flame into plain warmth. Since the seal looks symmetric, I assume the hidden north and west points also hold inverted Columns.
effect: Radiates steady warmth outward from the stone without producing a flame. It is balanced to the size of the seal so the stone is warm to the touch but never hot enough to burn.

A Columns sign sits on either side of it, at the southwest and southeast, each angled with its stem pointing in toward the center. Two Wind signs flank the Sights Set: one at the northwest, a curve with its loop at the top, and one at the northeast, a mirrored and rotated curve with its loop at the bottom.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The pair of Columns signs makes the fire manifest as a column or beam reaching a moderate distance from the seal. The two Wind signs placed as mirror images twist that flame so it moves in a spiral. The Sights Set sign lets the caster aim where the effect is directed.
effect: Produces a single spiraling column of flame that the caster can aim in a chosen direction.

name: Sylph Shoes Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a variant of the wind sigil: an S-shaped double spiral flanked by curved arcs on either side instead of short ticks. Around it, a single band of signs alternates between Convergence triangles and Levitation arrows, roughly eight of each, all pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The central sigil is the wind underfoot variant of the wind sigil, which sets the spell as wind magic that supports solid objects suspended in air. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. The inward-pointing Levitation signs float the target into the air, and because they are evenly balanced around the ring, the lift stays stable. The alternating Convergence signs focus that magic onto a single point, keeping the lift centered on the object the seal is drawn on rather than spreading outward.
effect: Lifts the object bearing the seal off the ground and lets it fly, carrying whoever wears or rides it through the air.

name: Time Stop
description: A fully visible seal in black ink on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a small inner circle holding a solid dot, with no element sigil. Four straight spokes run from the inner circle to the north, south, east, and west, and each ends in a Y-shaped fork that meets the outer ring, enclosing a small triangle against it. At the four intercardinal points sit L-shaped corner marks that form small right-angled triangles against the ring. None of these geometric signs match a named sign.

The surrounding geometric signs are unnamed, so their individual roles cannot be read, but together they make up the time-freezing structure. No Regions signs are present, so the effect stays within the bounds of the ring.
effect: Freezes the motion of anything it targets, as if time had stopped for that thing. With no Regions signs, it only affects what lies within its ring. Replacing the central dot with a sigil limits the effect to a specific kind of target.

name: Time Stop
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. A fire sigil sits at the center of the inner ring and fills most of it. Its three short strokes cross the sides of the triangle instead of sitting just outside them. The band between the inner and outer rings is filled with a geometric lattice of eight spokes running out from the inner ring. The four cardinal spokes at north, south, east and west each end in a Y-shaped fork that opens outward onto the outer ring. The four intercardinal spokes each split into one horizontal and one vertical line that meet the outer ring, forming boxed cells. None of these lattice shapes match a named sign. There is no central dot and no Regions sign.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on flames and heat. The large sigil relative to the inner ring points to a fairly strong effect. The angular lattice of unnamed geometric signs is the time-freezing structure, and it normally surrounds a central dot. Here the fire sigil takes the dot's place, which narrows the freeze to heat instead of everything inside the ring. No Regions signs move the effect elsewhere, so it stays within the bounds of the ring.
effect: Freezes time for whatever it targets, as if time had stopped for that thing, limited to the area inside the ring. With a fire sigil in place of the central dot, the freeze applies to heat, holding warmth in place so it does not escape or fade.

name: Time Stop
description: An illustration of a large egg-shaped vessel with a metal cap, side handles, and a stapled crack across its upper half, resting in a scaled bowl stand on three clawed feet. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere on it.

The ring appears closed and is fully visible within the frame, but the seal is small and shaded by line art. Inside the ring are angular, geometric strokes in a triangular, star-like arrangement around a dark center that may be a central dot. No element sigil can be recognized. The individual signs are too small to match to known signs.

The dark center fits a central dot like the one at the core of the Repetition sigil, which marks time magic. The surrounding strokes look like unnamed geometric signs rather than any catalogued sign. Because the individual signs cannot be read, how they modify the spell cannot be decoded.

The effect reaches only things within the ring unless a sign such as Regions changes that. This reading is tentative, because the individual signs cannot be read.

name: Tracking Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with its outer ring closed. A long horizontal line runs across the full width of the center, with a zigzag line weaving over and under it; this central figure matches none of the known sigils or signs. Two inner arcs follow the inside of the ring: one runs from the north point around the west side and ends in a small forked mark near the west, and the other runs from the south point around the east side and ends in a matching forked mark near the east. At the north point, a small circle hangs from a short stem joined to the upper arc, and a mirrored circle-on-a-stem sits at the south point. In the northeast and southwest are two diamond shapes, each crossed by two curved strokes; they resemble the Diamond sign but are not a clean match. In the northwest and southeast are two small signs built from short vertical bars crossed by horizontal and angled strokes, which also do not match any known sign. The whole layout has two-fold rotational symmetry.

None of these marks can be firmly identified, so their individual functions cannot be read. The circle-on-stem marks only loosely resemble half of a Solidification sign, and the crossed diamonds only loosely resemble Diamond, so neither can be relied on. The paired, rotated placement of every element suggests a balanced spell whose effect does not point in one direction.
effect: Marks a magical item so it can be tracked. How each sign and the central figure contribute to this is unknown.

name: Twinned Bottles
description: Two hands each hold a stoppered round-bottomed bottle partly filled with liquid. A small medallion sits inside each bottle, tilted at an angle, with faint etched marks on its face. The marks are tiny, foreshortened, and seen through glass and liquid, so no ring, sigil, or sign can be identified, and it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed.

name: Twinned Bottles
description: A fully visible seal on a pale, grainy background, ring closed. No element sigil is present. At the center sits an hourglass figure, an inverted triangle above an upright one, joined by crossing lines that resemble a Reflection sign. Four single-line corner brackets frame it, each corner pointing outward like the corners of an Expansion sign. A short horizontal dash sits on each side of the center, one east and one west. Eight identical small glyphs, each a cluster of curved and angled strokes, are spaced evenly around the inner edge of the ring. They do not match any named sign.

The center resembles Reflection, and the outward-pointing corners resemble Expansion, which would mean growth. However, the meanings of these ancient glyphs are lost, so the sign rules cannot be reliably applied. The strict radial and mirror symmetry suggests a balanced, two-way effect rather than one with a direction.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. Eight Columns signs sit evenly around the inside of the ring at the four cardinal and four intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. The center holds no element sigil. Instead, four half-disc shapes are arranged in a pinwheel around an empty middle point, with their flat edges facing north, east, south, and west in rotating order. Four small X-shaped marks sit at the intercardinal positions between the half-discs. Neither the half-discs nor the X marks match any named sign or sigil.

There is no element sigil, so nothing sets what kind of magic is produced. The pinwheel of half-discs and the X marks are unidentified symbols, and their rotating arrangement may add a turning or swirling behavior, but this cannot be confirmed. Without a known sigil or known central signs, the seal cannot be fully decoded.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with an irregular, wobbly ring that is closed. The center holds an unidentified sigil made of a long horizontal line and a vertical line crossing at right angles, overlaid by two long, narrow looped petals that cross each other diagonally, giving a star- or flower-like shape. effect: The effect cannot be fully determined because the central sigil is unidentified. The eight balanced Columns signs show that whatever magic the sigil produces would manifest as a column rising straight up from the seal, with greater range or quantity than a seal with fewer signs.

name: Unknown Magic
description: Five separate small seals on a clean background, all fully visible. At the top is a ring closed around a plain cross with a solid center, unlike the Crosshair sign, whose center is broken. At the upper right is a ring closed around a small upright triangle with no extra strokes, so it is neither the fire sigil nor the downward-pointing Convergence sign. The three closed rings meet the condition for activation, while the two open rings would not activate as drawn. Without identified glyphs, there is nothing to decode beyond that structure.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The central glyph is not a standard element sigil. It is a tall arch, like an upside-down U with long legs, crossed horizontally by a straight bar that extends past both legs and ends in a small open circle on each side. The bar-and-circles part resembles a horizontal Solidification sign. Six Columns signs are evenly spaced around the center. Each is turned sideways so its stem runs along the ring instead of pointing inward or outward, and all six stems point clockwise. Six small open circles alternate with the Columns signs, one between each neighbouring pair. Nothing is cut off or hidden.

The part that resembles Solidification may make the result more solid, but this is uncertain because it is fused into a larger shape. Columns is a directional sign, so its angle sets the direction of the spell. Six Columns all turned the same way around the ring would push the spell in a circle. The small open circles do not match any known sign, so their role cannot be decoded.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because the central glyph is unidentified. Going by the sign rules alone, the six clockwise Columns signs would drive whatever the spell produces around the seal in a clockwise motion.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with every ring closed. Several concentric rings run around the outside, and between two of them sits a band of many small hooked strokes. At the center is a triangle with three short lines radiating from it, like the fire sigil. Each line ends in a small circle where it crosses or touches the triangle, so this is a variant of the fire design. Eight identical units are arranged radially around the sigil, and each has three parts. Nearest the ring is a long zigzag with several peaks, like a stretched Crushing sign. Below it is a Columns-like sign with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center, flanked by two parallel strokes. A single dot sits on the inner side. Eight S-shaped wavy lines sit between the units, also arranged radially.

The Columns-like signs pointing toward the center would normally direct the magic in a column. The zigzags resemble Crushing, which breaks a target into pieces. The wavy lines, the dots, and the band of hooked strokes match no known sign, so they cannot be read. Because all eight units are identical and evenly spaced, the effect is balanced in every direction rather than aimed one way.
effect: The effect of this seal is unknown and cannot be determined from the image. The visible signs point only to a fire-related spell that is spread evenly around the seal.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Eight identical Levitation signs are evenly spaced around it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward at the sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.

Here all eight signs are the same length and point inward in a radially balanced arrangement. When Levitation is balanced, the lifted material tends to settle into a sphere, and no sign pulls the effect toward any one direction. No other modifiers are present to shape, harden, or aim the result.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A Light sigil sits at the center: a square with a smaller diamond inside it and a short line extending outward from the middle of each side. Eight Dispersion signs are evenly spaced around it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point. Each has its long stem pointing out toward the ring, its crossbar in the middle, and its arc facing in toward the sigil. No other signs are present.

All eight signs are the same size and orientation and are spaced at equal angles, so the seal is fully balanced and no direction is favored. The result should be light spreading evenly on all sides of the seal instead of forming a focused beam.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center, drawn as a triangle with a short stroke crossing each side, and it takes up only a small part of the ring. Eight Columns signs surround it, evenly spaced at the four cardinal and four intercardinal points. All eight are the same length and share the same orientation, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing at the sigil. No other signs are present.

Because all eight signs are equal in length and spaced evenly all the way around, they are balanced. The spell therefore has no pull in any sideways direction and should rise straight up from the seal.

The center holds an unmatched sigil: a triangle whose three corners each extend into a looped curl, with a small open circle beyond each of the three loops. Between the corners sit three groups of three short radiating strokes, two upper and one lower, each with a longer middle stroke, resembling the Aeriforms Defined sign. The eight chevron-and-stroke units all point the same way around the ring, which suggests rotation or circulation. Neither these units nor the three lone strokes match a named sign, so their combined behavior cannot be decoded from the known sign rules.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image. The central sigil and the outer pinwheel units do not match any known sigil or sign.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A Billow sign, a four-lobed loop, sits at the center where a sigil would normally be, and no element sigil appears. Four Collection signs surround it at the north, south, east and west points. Each has its closed triangle facing outward and its open legs facing the center. Further out, four Levitation signs sit at the cardinal points, each with its bar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward. The four Collection signs face inward in their usual orientation, so they gather material from above and around the seal for Billow to convert. The four inward-pointing Levitation signs are balanced on all sides, which floats the result above the seal, and balanced Levitation tends to shape it into a sphere. The intercardinal signs cannot be identified, so their contribution is unknown.

name: Unknown Magic

The east and west signs resemble Binding, which halts the target material and binds it to act as one unit, but their added circle and sideways orientation make that reading uncertain. The bottom line and the altered V do not match any known sign or sigil variant, so the full combination cannot be decoded.

A large S-shaped stroke runs diagonally across the center from lower left to upper right; each end curls inward into a small loop, and each of its two arcs carries a small half-circle bump on its outer side, one at the bottom of the lower arc and one at the top of the upper arc. name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a small empty circle with no sigil inside it. Four long Columns-like signs run from the central circle out to the ring, one at each of north, east, south and west. effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image. The seal has no identifiable sigil, and the central circle has no known meaning, so only the balanced Columns-style structure can be read.

name: Unknown Magic

The center holds a large Selection sign: a square crossed by a vertical and a horizontal line, both reaching well past the square's edges. There is no element sigil. Four Columns signs sit at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest points. Each has its crossbar toward the center and its stem pointing out toward the ring. name: Unknown Magic

name: Unknown Magic

Three Convergence signs sit at the triangle's points: one north of the apex and one beside each lower corner, all pointing downward. name: Unknown Magic

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A Light sigil sits at the center, with a dot at its middle and short lines extending north, south, east, and west from the diamond's points. A Columns-like stroke runs diagonally from each of the square's four corners and ends in a crossbar, giving four corner signs. Around these, eight tilted T-shaped Columns signs are spaced evenly, each rotated slightly so they form a pinwheel. Between them, at evenly spaced points, sit eight identical unnamed glyphs. justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. It resembles Levitation but lacks Levitation's base crossbar, so it does not match any known sign and its function cannot be decoded.
effect: This is a spell component whose modifier effect is unknown and cannot be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single symbol on a clean background: eight straight lines of equal length radiating from a shared center point, evenly spaced like an asterisk or starburst. It has no ring, no sigil, and no other signs. It resembles the crossed lines at the core of the Concealment sign, but without that sign's eye-shaped marks.
justification: This is one standalone symbol, not a seal. It does not match any named sign or sigil. Its radial symmetry and lack of a distinct front suggest it would behave as a non-directional mark that cannot be inverted, but its role cannot be decoded.
