effect: A spell component whose function is unknown. The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single symbol, fully visible on a clean background. It is a long horizontal baseline with a thick, double-lined arch at its middle: two concentric semicircles rising from the line and opening downward onto it, like a tunnel or bridge span. There is no ring and no sigil. The shape loosely recalls the stacked curves of Binding, but the baseline joining the arch sets it apart, and it does not match any named sign.
justification: This is one symbol, not a seal, so there is no ring and no element for it to act on. It is not a known named sign, so no sign rule tells how it modifies a spell, and there is nothing to decode beyond its shape.
effect: This is a spell component whose modifier effect is unknown, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Valance Leech Counterclock
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink with gray shading, ring closed. The outer ring is a wide band split into shaded segments by short radial lines. A large upright triangle fills the ring with its corners touching the band. Inside it sits a circle, then a smaller upright triangle, then a hexagon framing a smaller hexagon, with lines joining their corners into a faceted pattern. At the very center is a small elongated, looped figure with short strokes branching off it, matching the Valance Leech decorative sigil. There is no element sigil, and none of the standard signs such as Columns, Regions, or Crushing appear.
justification: The nested ring, triangles, circle, and hexagons form the counterclock framework, which reverses time for whatever the spell targets. With no element sigil, the spell does not act on fire, water, earth, or wind. The Valance Leech decorative sigil at the center limits the effect to the physical counterpart of its design, so the time reversal applies only to valance leeches.
effect: Temporarily rewinds valance leeches to the physical state they were in 24 hours earlier. When the effect ends, they are meant to return to how they were when the spell was drawn.

name: Valance Leech Counterclock
description: A fully visible seal with the ring closed. Inside the ring is a six-pointed star made of two overlapping triangles. The space between the star and the ring is divided into shaded diamond and trapezoid panels. At the center of the star sits a hexagon framed by a beveled hexagonal border. Inside it is a small, finely drawn sigil shaped like a curled, segmented leech body with short lines branching off it. No element sigil appears, and none of the standard modifier signs can be matched.
justification: The star, the panelled outer band and the nested hexagons form the counterclock framework, which reverses time temporarily rather than calling on fire, water, earth or wind. The central glyph is a decorative valance leech sigil. Decorative sigils limit a spell's effect to the physical counterpart of the creature they depict, so the counterclock effect applies only to valance leeches.
effect: Temporarily rewinds valance leeches to the physical state they were in 24 hours earlier. Once the effect runs out, it returns them to the state they had when the seal was drawn.

name: Valance Leech of Light
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A light sigil sits slightly below the center. Above it, in the upper part of the ring, is a large decorative sigil: an angular, many-sided body with short limb-like strokes branching off its corners, the decorative sigil of a valance leech. Five Columns signs surround these. Two sit at the northwest, two at the northeast, and one is directly south of the light sigil. All five are drawn inverted, with the crossbar facing the center and the stem pointing out toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. The valance leech decorative sigil gives that light the rough form of a valance leech. The five Columns signs are all inverted. Inverted Columns spread their effect outward and sideways like Dispersion instead of beaming it in one direction. The light therefore spreads out into the sculpted shape rather than shooting off as a beam.
effect: Creates a glowing sculpture of light in the shape of a valance leech, with the light dispersed outward to fill the form. Light made this way fades over time.

name: Vapor Bubble Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background made of two concentric rings. The outer ring is open at the lower left, and the inner ring is broken only where two signs cross it. A Water sigil sits at the center of the inner ring. In the band between the rings, a sideways Wind sigil sits at the east point and another at the west point. Six Columns signs sit in the band with their bars toward the outer ring and their stems pointing inward: one at north, one at south, and one at each of the four diagonal positions near the east and west sides. Four Cooling signs, each a slanted line with dots on either side, sit between the north and south Columns and their neighbors. Two Gathering signs, one at north and one at south, cross the inner ring with their arrowheads pointing in toward the Water sigil.
justification: The Water sigil sets the core element, so the inner ring is a water spell. The outer ring adds effects to it. Its two Wind sigils move the surrounding air, and the Cooling signs chill it. The inward-pointing Gathering signs actively draw material in toward the water core. The six evenly spaced Columns are balanced, so they direct the gathered magic toward the center rather than any one side. Together, cooled, moving air gives up its moisture, which is pulled into the central water spell.
effect: Gathers moisture from the surrounding air and stores it as an orb of fresh water.

name: Wall Bend
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a round surface, seen at a steep angle and drawn very small. An object reaches in from the upper left, and the panel border cuts off the lower and right parts of the surface. Where the ring is visible it looks closed. Several arrow-shaped marks sit around the middle, pointing at angles, and could be Pulling signs. A looped, figure-eight-like mark sits left of center. The central sigil and the remaining signs are too small and distorted to identify.
justification: If the arrow marks are Pulling signs, they would draw the target material toward the seal, and their angle would set the direction of the pull. The sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the image. The looped mark and other small shapes do not clearly match any known sign.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the image. If the central glyph is an earth sigil paired with Pulling signs, the spell takes hold of nearby earthen materials such as stone, soil and brickwork and pulls or bends them in a direction set by the seal. The other signs may help spread the material.

name: Wall Bend
description: A manga panel of a figure in a pointed hat and cape reaching up toward a brick wall, pressing a small square card against the bricks. The card carries drawn markings, but they are tiny and partly covered by the hand and fingers. No ring, sigil, or sign can be made out.
justification: Nothing to decode. Some markings are present on the card, but no element sigil or individual sign is legible.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Wall Breaker Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a gap in its lower left between roughly the seven and eight o'clock positions. An earth sigil sits at the center: a top bar, a vertical stem, an angled V-shaped body, and the two side dots. It has an extra horizontal bar drawn across its base. One Columns sign sits at the east point and one at the west point. Each has its crossbar at the outer end near the ring and its stem pointing toward the sigil. A large Crushing sign sits at the north point and another at the south point. They mirror each other, with their open ends facing the center.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, wood, and soil. The two Crushing signs, set at right angles to the Columns, break the targeted material into pieces. Because these Crushing signs are large, the pieces are ground very small. They are drawn in their normal orientation, not inverted, so the effect is pulverizing rather than reforming. The paired Columns direct and push that force along their axis. This is the arrangement of the Wall Breaker seal. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate until it is closed.
effect: When the ring is closed, the spell breaks through the solid object it is drawn on and grinds the material down to dust or sand.

name: Wall of Wind
description: A manga panel with a seal drawn in ink. The upper part is covered by a large white shape, and a dark vertical line crosses the right side, so the full ring cannot be seen and it is unclear whether it is open or closed. A wind sigil sits near the center. Along the left side runs a cluster of small triangles matching Convergence signs. Along the bottom edge is a row of about five inverted Columns signs. Between the sigil and that row is a curved, semicircular line with small marks along its edge. The rest of the seal is hidden or cut off.
justification: The wind sigil sets the spell to move air. Inverted Columns manifest horizontally instead of vertically and spread their effect outward, so the air is pushed out from the seal rather than up. Convergence focuses the magic about a single point, which keeps the moving air centered on the seal. The semicircular sign on the Columns side frames that outward push around the sigil. Together these produce a ring of moving air around a center. The hidden portions may hold more signs that cannot be read here.
effect: Creates a circular wall of air that is difficult for objects or people to pass through, which can be used to contain people or animals. This assumes the hidden part of the seal does not change the core arrangement that is visible.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, enclosed by a Holding sign whose two curved arms bracket it on the left and right, each ending in a small dot near the bottom. At the north point is a cluster of three signs: a central sign pointing upward that reads as Dispersion, flanked by two Columns signs that mirror each other on either side. At the south point, below the sigil, is a Pointing sign.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water magic. Holding keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Pointing makes the water taper into a cone. The two mirrored Columns signs define the broad base of that shape, and Dispersion pushes the effect outward, so it takes form outside the confines of the ring rather than inside it.
effect: Shapes water into a large pen nib that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the water to saturate it, turning the nib into a tool for drawing large seals across stone, sand, or other broad flat surfaces.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a gap at the lower left. A water sigil sits at the center, large relative to the ring, enclosed by a tall Holding sign whose two curved strokes wrap around it, with a dot outside each lower end. North of the sigil is a Dispersion sign drawn as a T with its arc above the crossbar, pointing outward toward the top of the ring. It is flanked by two Columns signs turned on their sides and mirrored, one on each side, with their stems facing the Dispersion sign. South of the sigil is a single Pointing sign, a triangle crossing a horizontal bar with a hook curling up at each end.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its large size points to a strong effect. Holding keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. The mirrored Columns signs set a column-shaped body that forms the base of the shape, and Pointing tapers the water into a cone, so together they make a nib. Dispersion lets the magic spill outward past the seal, so the form appears outside the ring instead of within it. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn until it is closed.
effect: Forms water into a large hovering pen nib that sits at an angle below the seal. Conjuring ink poured into it saturates the water, so it can draw large seals across stone, sand, or other wide flat surfaces.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, enclosed by a Holding sign: two tall curved brackets on the east and west sides, each with a dot beside its lower end. A Pointing sign sits south of the sigil. At the north point is a T-shaped sign with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the sigil, shaped like Columns but without the curved stroke of Dispersion. It is flanked by two Columns signs turned sideways and mirrored, with their crossbars on the outer sides and their stems pointing inward toward the north sign.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works with water. The Holding sign around the sigil keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. The two Columns signs define the broad base of the form, and the Pointing sign tapers the water into a cone. The north sign sits where Dispersion belongs and acts like Dispersion, letting the effect manifest outside the ring instead of within it.
effect: Shapes water into a large pen nib that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the water to saturate it, turning the nib into a giant pen. It can then draw large seals on stone, sand, or any flat, expansive surface.

name: Warmth-Retention Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the outer ring closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center inside its own inner circle. Four straight spokes run from the inner circle to the outer ring at north, south, east, and west, and each one forks into a Y where it meets the ring, enclosing a small triangle against the ring. At the four intercardinal points, right-angle corner marks sit against the ring with their corners pointing inward, each boxing off a small square segment. This spoke-and-corner pattern does not match any named sign.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element to heat. It is small relative to the outer ring, which keeps the intensity low. The surrounding spoke-and-corner structure is a single unnamed sign laid out with radial symmetry and no directional marks pointing outward, so it holds the fire's effect in place around the seal rather than projecting it. Together these give a mild, contained heat.
effect: Maintains a steady, low heat on whatever the seal is used on.

name: Warmth-Retention Seal
description: A manga panel with a small inset diagram of a seal beside a rounded vessel resting on a stand, with an arrow pointing from the inset to the stand's rim. The seal is fully visible with the ring closed. At the center, a small fire sigil sits inside its own small inner circle. Around it, a single radial sign fills the ring, made of lines that divide the space into segments. Inward-pointing chevron shapes sit at the north, east, south, and west points, with angled corner shapes at the four intercardinal points. This surrounding sign does not match any named sign.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as heat and flame. It is drawn very small relative to the ring, which keeps the intensity low, so the spell gives gentle heat rather than open flame. The unidentified radial sign enclosing the sigil is symmetric and surrounds it on all sides. Its exact rule is not established, but it is the part that keeps the low heat steady and lasting rather than letting it flare or fade.
effect: Maintains a low, steady heat on whatever the seal is applied to, keeping it warm without strong burning.

name: Water Bolt
description: A manga panel showing a large oval seal drawn on a flat surface, seen at an angle. The left and top edges of the ring are visible. The right side is cut off by an overlapping blank shape, and the bottom is cut off by the panel border, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed. A row of Piercing signs, each a long line through a diamond, runs diagonally across the middle of the seal. Four of them are legible, and a further line near the left is partly hidden. About four V-shaped Regions signs sit spread around the row, all pointing the same way, toward the lower edge of the panel. Splashing water and a sleeved hand cover the upper left, and a curved shape near the center left may be the central sigil, but the splash hides it too much to identify.
justification: The Piercing signs make the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many are created. Regions signs that all point to the same side send the magic in that direction. Taken together, the row of Piercing signs between the matching Regions signs fires a volley of bolts in one direction. The element cannot be confirmed from the hidden center. Assuming it is a water sigil and that the hidden part holds a fifth Piercing sign, the layout matches a seal of five bolts.
effect: Creates five bolts of water that surge forward at an upward angle. This assumes the obscured center is a water sigil and that the cut-off part of the seal completes the row of five Piercing signs.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A small water sigil sits near the bottom, drawn lying on its side. Five Piercing signs stand upright in a row across the middle in a shallow arch, with the center one highest and the outer ones lowest. Four Regions signs sit between and beside them: two high, above the gaps flanking the central Piercing sign, and two lower, just inside the ring at the west and east edges. All four point the same way, toward the bottom of the seal.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many form, so five signs give five bolts. Regions signs that all point to the same side send the magic in that direction, which gives the volley a single shared heading. As drawn, the ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap at the bottom is closed.
effect: Creates five bolts of water that surge forward together at an upward angle as an offensive volley. The more Piercing signs are drawn, the more bolts are produced.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. A water sigil sits just above the center of the inner ring. Across the top are three Sights Set signs, each with its arrow pointing at the sigil. The north one has a diamond resting on the outer ring and an arrow running straight down. The northwest and northeast ones have square heads on the outer ring and arrows running diagonally inward. Two Convergence triangles sit between these three arrows. At the east and west points sit two Strengthening signs, turned sideways so their triangles point in toward the sigil. Below the sigil, a single Piercing sign runs down toward the south edge of the inner ring. It is flanked by two Regions signs whose points angle inward toward the center.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. A water sigil with Piercing and Regions signs is the core of a water bolt. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many form, so one sign means one bolt. The three Sights Set signs aimed at the sigil let the caster aim the spell at a chosen target. Convergence focuses the water to a single point and packs it tightly. The Strengthening signs make it harder and more durable. The inward-pointing Regions signs control where the magic manifests relative to the seal.
effect: Forms a single focused, hardened bolt of water and fires it at a target the caster aims at. It is an offensive water projectile.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. A water sigil sits in the upper center. Above it, three Sights Set signs point inward at the sigil: one from the north and one each from the northwest and northeast, with their diamond tails resting on the outer ring. Two Convergence signs sit between them, one on each side of the north Sights Set. Strengthening signs, drawn tilted, mark the west and east. Below the sigil, three Piercing signs stand side by side. Two Regions signs at the southwest and southeast point inward toward the center.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Piercing makes the water manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many, so three signs give three bolts. Sights Set aims the spell at a chosen target. Convergence focuses the magic toward a single point. Strengthening makes the result harder and more durable. The inward-pointing Regions signs keep the magic forming within the seal before it is sent out.
effect: Creates three hardened bolts of water and fires them as offensive projectiles at a target the caster aims at.

name: Water Cage
description: A manga panel showing two seals joined by a connecting line. The larger seal on the left is an oval with its ring closed and a water sigil at the center. It is ringed by small, roughly drawn signs. Chevron-shaped marks resembling Regions signs and zigzag marks resembling Crushing signs can be made out, but the remaining marks are too small and sketchy to identify. The smaller seal on the right, ring closed, holds a single Pulling sign whose arrow points along the connecting line toward the larger seal. Its right edge sits near the panel border.
justification: The water sigil sets the larger seal's element. The Regions signs set where the magic manifests relative to the ring. Pointed toward the Crushing signs, they appear to shape the water into a bounded form rather than letting it spread freely, though the unreadable signs leave the full arrangement uncertain. The smaller linked seal has no sigil of its own and only a Pulling sign, which pulls things toward where its arrow points. Here the arrow points at the larger seal.
effect: Creates a spherical cage of water around the target. The linked Pulling seal draws the target toward the larger seal so it is caught inside the cage more easily.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of an oval seal held between two hands, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. On either side of it is a tall stacked sign matching Mimicry, one west and one east, with fingertips overlapping their outer edges. Along the north edge is a row of small marks: what look like two Columns signs pointing in opposite directions, with a small figure between them that is too small to identify. Along the south edge is an alternating row of five marks: three short vertical strokes and two Regions signs pointing downward. Parts of the left and right edges of the ring are hidden by the fingers.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes water. The Mimicry signs beside it guide the movements of whatever form the spell takes. The opposed Columns signs and the downward Regions signs control where the water manifests relative to the seal, and the vertical strokes between the Regions signs cannot be identified. The figure along the north edge is not legible enough to confirm what shape the water takes, though its place between the Columns fits a shape-giving sigil.
effect: Creates a horse out of water that can be mounted, guided, and controlled like a regular horse, with Mimicry guiding its movements. This assumes the illegible figure at the north edge is the sigil that gives the water a horse's shape, and that the covered edges hold nothing beyond what is visible.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of a large surge of splashing water rising upward, with a figure riding on it and another figure running below amid speed lines. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The water is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of a horse-shaped figure pulling a cart along a rocky, wet path, with a figure in a pointed hat seated on the cart. A cylindrical fitting is mounted at the horse's head. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The horse and cart are effects and scenery, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga illustration of dozens of round discs, each carrying a seal, falling around a figure in a pointed hat. The matching seal is on a disc at the lower left, ring closed, drawn very small. A water sigil sits at the center. Above it is a figure that reads as a horse decorative sigil, and on either side of the water sigil are vertical signs that match Mimicry. Along the bottom of the ring runs a row of small marks, some of which look like Regions signs pointing downward. The neighbouring disc touches its lower right edge. At this scale the individual strokes, including any Columns signs beside the horse sigil, cannot be read with certainty.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water. The horse decorative sigil sculpts that water into a horse shape. Mimicry signs make the shaped water imitate the movements of what the decorative sigil depicts. The downward-pointing Regions signs set where the magic manifests relative to the seal. The remaining marks are too small to decode, so this reading rests on the clearly visible sigils and the general layout.
effect: Creates a horse out of water that moves like a real horse and can be mounted, guided and controlled by the caster. This assumes the unreadable small signs match the rest of the layout.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A water sigil sits at the center. Directly above it is a large angular horse-shaped decorative sigil, with a short dash beneath each of its front and back legs. At the upper left and upper right, flanking the horse, are two Columns signs turned on their sides, mirror images of each other with their stems pointing toward the horse. A Mimicry sign stands to the west and another to the east of the water sigil, both drawn tall and slightly tilted. Along the bottom of the ring is an alternating row of three plain straight strokes, angled like spokes, and two small Regions signs whose points face up toward the center. The straight strokes do not match any known sign.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell creates or shapes water. The horse decorative sigil gives that water the rough shape of a horse. Mimicry imitates the movements of whatever its decorative sigil depicts, so the water figure moves the way a horse does rather than holding still. The paired Columns around the horse set where that magic is directed and how hard it pushes. Regions signs pointing inward keep the magic manifesting within the seal's ring rather than outside it. The unidentified straight strokes alternating with them likely refine this, but their role cannot be read. The ring is open, so the seal must be closed to activate.
effect: Creates a horse sculpted out of water that moves like a real horse. It can be mounted, guided, and controlled by its caster much like a regular horse.

name: Water Orb
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn as an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, one pointing up and one pointing down. A Columns sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, each with its crossbar near the ring and its stem reaching toward the center. Four Orb signs, each a circle crossed by a diagonal line, sit at the four intercardinal points. Their diagonals are mirrored left to right, so the arrangement is symmetric.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The four Orb signs are non-directional and define a spherical space above the seal where the controlled material collects. Material fills that space from the bottom up and stays subject to gravity. The two balanced Columns signs push the effect upward in a column, lifting that space above the seal. The sigil's orientation does not change its known effect. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until it is closed.
effect: Creates an invisible spherical container above the seal that holds water. Water poured directly into it fills the sphere from the bottom up, the way it would fill a cup.

name: Water Rose
description: A manga panel showing a rose shape made of liquid rising on a long stem, surrounded by scattered droplets and splashes. A hand holding a pen sits at the right, and another hand at the bottom holds a dark, flat object seen edge-on. A hat brim curves along the left side. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: Nothing to decode. The rose and droplets are an effect, not a glyph, and the object in the lower hand shows no markings from this angle.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Waterflinger
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. Two smaller fire sigils mark the north and south points, mirroring each other across the center. One Crosshair sign sits at the east point and one at the west point, flanking the water sigil.
justification: The large central water sigil sets the main element, and the two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity, since a sigil's size relative to the ring sets its strength. Crosshair makes the seal's magic target whatever its shorter ends point at. Here the two Crosshairs sit on either side of the water sigil, so the fire's heat is likely directed at water.
effect: The exact effect is unknown. It likely targets water with heat to evaporate it, driving the water away.

name: Watersculpture
description: A manga panel of a horse-like figure made of water rising from a pool beside stone walls, with a figure watching from the lower right. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The water figure is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Watersculpture
description: A manga panel of two hands holding a cut-glass cup as a stream of liquid pours into it, with sound effects above. The surface of the liquid swirls into a rough shape. The cup and the saucer beneath it carry lattice and petal patterns, but no ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The patterns on the cup and saucer are ornament rather than a glyph, and the shape in the liquid is an effect, not a seal.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Watershot Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the lower left. A water sigil sits at the center, filling a moderate share of the ring. Eight Columns signs surround it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point. Each has its crossbar facing outward toward the ring and its stem pointing inward. Seven of them are short and roughly equal in length. The Columns sign at the south point has a much longer stem that reaches up nearly to the sigil.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works with water, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Columns signs make magic manifest as a column or beam, and their number sets the range or quantity of magic produced. When all Columns signs are equal, the beam rises straight up from the seal. Lengthening a Columns sign adds pressure or power in its direction, so the elongated south sign makes the stream lean or push in that direction rather than rise straight up. The open ring means the seal is inactive until the ring is closed.
effect: Creates a stream of water that shoots up from the seal in a column. With all eight Columns signs of equal length, it fires straight up. Here the longer south sign adds pressure on one side, so the stream is directed off vertical.

name: Windowway Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background made of three concentric circles, all closed. The outer band, between the outermost and middle circles, is packed with a continuous run of identical zigzag, lightning bolt-shaped marks all the way around. The inner band, between the middle and innermost circles, holds a continuous run of identical chevron marks resembling Regions signs. Every chevron points clockwise along the band rather than inward or outward. The central space inside the innermost circle is empty, with no sigil or other sign.
justification: Bands of many identical simple markings lining the seal like extra rings are the Windows sign. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically connected, so the repeated zigzag band acts as Windows lining the spell. The chevron band behaves like Regions signs set to point around the ring rather than in or out. They likely direct where the passage manifests and keep it on the ring itself. The seal has no sigil because its magic is spatial rather than elemental. No location mark sits in the center, so the destination is not specified by anything visible.
effect: Opens a gateway between two distant locations, letting someone pass through from one place to the other. The seal works only as one of a matched pair, each drawn uniquely so it links to its partner and no other.

name: Beast Repellent
description: A seal in black ink on a white background. The ring appears closed, and its left edge touches the image border. At the center is a large unidentified sigil with a tall vertical stem, a crossbar on top, angled branches along the stem, and bracket-like strokes on each side. A light sigil, a square overlaid with a diamond and short spokes, sits at the east and another at the west. A small unidentified sign, a little rounded shape with short marks around it, sits at the north and another at the south. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, between the light sigils and the north and south signs; the two upper ones read as Y-like strokes and the two lower ones as T-like strokes.
justification: The two light sigils give the spell a light element, and they flank an unidentified central sigil that likely sets the spell's main purpose. The four Columns signs are evenly balanced, so the magic is projected outward from the seal in columns without favoring one direction. The small signs at north and south are an unidentified modifier, and the seal is laid out symmetrically around the center.
effect: Repels animals, keeping beasts away from the area around the seal. How it repels them is not certain, but the light sigils suggest it uses light.

name: Beldaruit's Smoke Sculpture
description: A manga panel showing a close-up of a large, dense seal drawn on a flat surface. A left hand rests flat across the lower left of the seal and a right hand holds a pen over the right side, hiding several areas. No ring is visible, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed, and the panel edges cut off the seal on every side, leaving it only partly visible. Many small Columns-like signs run in rows and diagonal lines across the upper middle. A vertical axis runs down the center with stacked shapes: at the top, a form with teardrop marks resembling a water sigil; below it, branching arrow shapes resembling Gathering or Levitation signs; then small circles and a figure-like shape. Asterisk-like marks sit at the upper left and upper right. A row of chevrons along a horizontal line at the lower right resembles Gathering or Pulling signs. Small dashed curves and paired T-shaped marks fill the lower center. Much of the seal is too small, hidden, or out of frame to name with confidence.
justification: The large number of Columns signs suggests the magic is raised and directed upward in several places. The stacked arrow signs along the central axis suggest material is drawn in and lifted. However, no central sigil can be identified with certainty. The hands and the panel edges hide large parts of the layout, so the visible signs cannot be combined into a full reading.
effect: The full seal forms a fake dragon out of smoke that can fly through the air and roar. The visible portion is consistent with lifting and shaping material, but it does not confirm this effect on its own.

name: Billowing Collection
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. A four-lobed Billow sign sits at the center where a sigil would normally go. Four Collection signs surround it, one each at the north, east, south and west points. Each has its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing inward toward the center. No element sigil is present.
justification: Billow is a sign, but here it takes the place of a sigil at the center. It sets the core behavior of the spell, which is turning material into a fluffy cloud. The four Collection signs gather material above and around the seal so the spell can use it. Their open sides face inward, which is their usual orientation. They are evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced on all sides rather than pushed in one direction. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. It works on whatever material is brought to it.
effect: Gathers any material directed into the seal and converts it into a soft, fluffy cloud that is very comfortable to sit on.

name: Bird of Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background, ring closed. The center holds a light sigil: a small square set inside a diamond, crossed by long diagonal strokes that form an X through it. A Launch sign sits at the north point, opening toward the center. A Dispersion sign sits at the south point, its stem pointing toward the sigil and its curve facing outward. At the east and west points are mirrored wing-like figures, each made of two stacked curved arcs with a small inward-pointing notch where they meet. Each figure has three short dashes on its outer side, beyond the arcs.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the seal creates and shapes light. The east and west figures mirror each other and read as the two halves of a bird design. They give the light the shape of a bird. Launch at the north sends that light out in a strong but brief burst, which carries it high into the air. Dispersion at the south lets the magic pour outward instead of holding it to a fixed beam. Together these make a loose, outward-moving bird of light rather than a steady lamp.
effect: Creates a bird made of light that bursts upward and flies around for some time before fading. It can serve to entertain, to signal for help, or to distract.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A fully visible seal with a thick, closed ring, surrounded by motion lines and printed in heavy halftone dots. Two pale glare spots, one on the left interior and one on the upper right, wash out parts of the seal. At the center is a curved, hooked stroke with a dot inside it, closer to the inner curl of the Repetition sign than to any clear element sigil. Around it sit about six or seven small marks, all blurred. These include a branching, footprint-like mark with several prongs to the northwest, a hooked mark to the west, short parallel strokes to the southwest, an inverted-V mark to the south that could be Regions or Launch, and a triangular mark to the east that could be Convergence or Strengthening. None of the surrounding signs can be matched with confidence.
justification: The ring is closed, so the seal would be active. The halftone and glare blur the glyph too much to identify the center glyph or any surrounding sign with certainty. If the central curl is Repetition, it would hold the object in its original state rather than set an element. The branching and arrow-like marks around it cannot be confirmed, so the modifiers cannot be decoded.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the visible glyph. The seal is known to let the pennant it is drawn on be steered by the caster, wrapping it around people and objects to bind them. The signs that would confirm this are not legible here.

name: Floating Drops
description: A manga page with several panels. In the top middle panel, a hand holds a round dish with a seal drawn on it. A wind sigil is visible at the center. Small X-shaped and short stroke marks are scattered around it toward the edge of the ring, but they are too small to match to specific signs or count reliably, and it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. In the top left panel, a dish is held near a face, but its drawn surface is not visible. In the top right panel, a pen draws on a round object held in a hand. An S-shaped glyph resembling the wind sigil and a few curls beside it are visible there, and the rest is covered by the hand and pen. The large lower panel shows no readable glyph.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the spell as one that moves air. The small marks near the ring may be paired Regions signs, one normal and one inverted, pointing toward each other. That arrangement would restrict the magic to the ring itself. Water sigils beside the center would add water as a second element. None of these can be confirmed at this size, so only the wind sigil is read with certainty.
effect: Likely creates drops of water that float in the air and form only along the seal's ring. This assumes the unreadable marks are flanking water sigils and opposing pairs of Regions signs.

name: Floating Expansion
description: A fully visible seal drawn in orange on a yellow background, ring closed. A Selection sign sits at the center in place of an element sigil. Four triple-lined Expansion signs surround it at the four intercardinal points, each with its corner pointing outward toward the ring. In the gaps between them, at north, south, east and west, sit four Stability and Level Planes signs drawn as three wavy lines. Small Columns signs sit near the rim on either side of each Stability and Level Planes sign, pointing in toward the center.
justification: No element sigil appears, so the Selection sign at the center limits the spell to the object the seal is drawn on. Expansion is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward it makes the target grow rather than shrink. Stability and Level Planes keeps the object balanced on a plane in the air, and the inward-facing Columns signs give that lift a vertical push. Together they enlarge and float only the object bearing the seal.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on grow to many times its original size and levitate in the air.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A fully visible seal in black ink on a white background, with the outer ring closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Around it is a single Dancing Puppets sign, drawn as an inner ring with four small circles at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest points. Curved lines cross through those circles and reach outward, and short straight strokes mark the north, south, east and west of the inner ring. No other signs are present.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Dancing Puppets placed around a sigil lets the target's movement be manipulated, and paired with wind it lets objects fly and be thrown about in the air. With no directional signs, the motion has no set direction and behaves erratically.
effect: Sends nearby objects darting into the sky and moving around erratically, with enough force to carry some objects up into the air.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A manga panel of a hooded cloak tumbling through the air with speed lines behind it, and a small curly-haired girl below reaching up toward it. A small round object with a few indistinct marks floats beside the cloak, but it is too small to show a ring, sigil, or recognizable sign. No legible seal or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. No sigil or sign can be identified, and the flying cloak is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Forbidden Flames
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a flat surface, seen at an angle so the ring looks like an ellipse. The ring appears closed and fully visible, with smoke billowing up from its upper edge. At the center is a small glyph made of a vertical stroke flanked by a dot on each side and an inward-pointing chevron on each outer side, like a Cooling sign with added chevrons. It matches none of the fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigils. At the north, east, south, and west points sit four circular glyphs. The north one is a circle crossed by a diagonal slash, close to the Orb sign. The east, west, and south ones are circles enclosing a triangle-like A shape, similar to Strengthening drawn inside a circle. At the four intercardinal points sit Columns signs, one each, oriented around the ring.
justification: The central glyph is an unidentified sigil, so the element cannot be read directly from it. Four Columns signs spaced evenly around the ring are balanced, so the magic manifests as a column rising straight up from the seal rather than leaning in any one direction. The four circular cardinal glyphs are unidentified modifiers; their resemblance to Orb and Strengthening is only partial, so their exact role cannot be confirmed.
effect: Creates a small fire that burns like an ordinary fire spell. It has no confirmed forbidden properties.

name: Forbidden Glow
description: A manga panel showing a round seal drawn on paper. A hand holding a pen sits at the right edge beside the ring but does not cover the glyph. The ring appears closed. About eight small T-shaped Columns signs are spaced evenly around the inside of the ring, each aligned along a radius. At the center is a small radiating, star-like sigil that does not match the fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigils. The seal is drawn small, so fine details of the central sigil are hard to make out.
justification: Columns make magic manifest as a column or beam. Because these signs are evenly balanced around the ring, no single direction dominates, and the effect rises straight up from the seal. The central sigil sets the kind of magic, but it is not one of the standard element sigils. It is a variant whose output resembles light that flickers rather than holds steady.
effect: Creates a brief display of glowing, flickering sparkles of light above the seal.

name: Gathering Shadows
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. The center holds a Concealment sign, an eight-armed star whose north, east, south, and west arms each end in an eye mark. There is no element sigil. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast positions, off the four diagonal arms of the central sign.
justification: The seal has no element sigil. Instead, the Concealment sign takes the center and sets the spell's purpose: hiding a target. The four Envelopment signs make that effect surround whatever the object covers, so the concealment wraps around the target rather than acting on a single point. The balanced placement of four Envelopment signs at the diagonals spreads the effect evenly over the drawn object.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on absorb all light that strikes it, so it disappears into shadow. Anyone who covers themselves with the object is concealed within the shadows along with it.

name: Grasping Wind
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough black ink on a white background, with the ring closed. A Wind sigil sits at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short strokes on either side. Four Pulling signs sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points, each with its arrowhead pointing in toward the sigil along the diagonal. No other signs are visible.
justification: The Wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves existing air. Pulling signs with their arrows pointing inward draw the spell's element toward the seal, so four of them around a Wind sigil pull the surrounding air toward the center from all sides. Because the four signs are evenly spaced, the pull is balanced rather than biased in one direction. Pulling signs set at an angle add a twisting motion, but these appear to point mostly straight inward.
effect: Creates a strong wind current flowing toward the seal, with enough force to pull lighter objects toward it. If the Pulling signs are slanted, the air twists into a vortex that spins objects as they are drawn in.

name: Illusory Labyrinth
description: A fully visible seal in black ink, ring closed. It has three concentric rings: an outer band filled with a zigzag of small triangles, a middle band of looped knot motifs with small scrolls at the cardinal and intercardinal points, and the inner ring that holds the spell. Just inside the inner ring, a continuous band of small chevrons runs around the whole circumference, matching the shape of Regions signs. The center holds a large unfamiliar sigil: a dome with three dots and short spikes along its edge, a horizontal bar beneath it, and a cluster of dark vertical strokes hanging below. A tall dark triangle points north above it, with two smaller dark triangles flanking it. To the east and west of the center sit two circles that each contain a triangle. Roughly twenty Columns signs radiate around the central sigil, some normal and some inverted. Four forked, branching signs sit at the intercardinal points. Signs combining a triangle with an S-like curl mark the east, west, and south points; the southern one is an inverted triangle over the curl. None of these match a known sign or sigil.
justification: The central sigil does not belong to the Primary Tetrad. It is the same sigil found in the scalewolf curse, so it does not set an ordinary elemental effect. The many Columns signs set where the magic manifests and project it in columns from the seal. Because they are spread roughly evenly around the center, the spell extends in all directions rather than one. The ring of Regions-like chevrons controls where the magic manifests relative to the ring. Running continuously around the edge, it plausibly bounds the effect and turns it back on itself. The circled triangles, branching signs, and triangle-and-curl signs are unidentified, so their exact roles cannot be decoded.
effect: Creates a vast labyrinthine area in which space itself is distorted and loops infinitely. Anyone who walks too far comes back out where they started, so escape is impossible.

name: Integration
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a small gap at the bottom. An earth sigil sits at the center. Six Crushing signs surround it, all inverted. One sits at the north point as a W shape and one at the south point as an M shape. The other four are stretched zigzag Crushing signs at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest, angled to follow the curve of the ring. No other signs are present.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter. Crushing is a semi-directional sign, so its direction does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Normal Crushing breaks solids into smaller and smaller pieces. Inverted Crushing does the opposite and pulls crushed material back into its original form. With only inverted Crushing signs around the earth sigil, the whole seal is built to reform matter rather than break it. Because the ring is open, the spell would not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Takes powdered or smashed solid particles within its range and temporarily rearranges them into the shape of the object they came from. This makes an unknown powder easy to identify. When the spell wears off or is removed, the material falls back into its broken state.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel set against a scale-like background. One hand holds a pen with its tip pressed to a surface, while a second hand rests flat beside it. Under the pen and fingers are a few ink marks: a small circle near the pen tip and some short curved strokes. Most of the drawing is covered by the hands and pen, so no sigil or sign can be identified. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen.
justification: Nothing to decode. A glyph appears to be present, but the visible strokes are too fragmentary and too hidden to match any sigil or sign.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel of a large black scaled wolf leaping forward with its jaws open, while two startled figures in pointed hats watch from the lower left. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: Nothing to decode. The panel shows a creature and onlookers, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Light Beam
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough black line on a white background. The ring shows a small gap at the bottom, so it is open. A small Light sigil sits at the center, drawn loosely with doubled strokes on its square, diamond, and spokes. Four Columns signs sit at the north, east, south, and west points. Each has its crossbar against the ring and its stem pointing inward, so none is inverted.
justification: The Light sigil makes this a spell that creates and controls light. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Columns makes the magic manifest as a column or beam, and longer signs add force in their direction. The four Columns signs are equal in length and evenly spaced, so they balance one another and the beam rises straight up from the seal rather than leaning to one side. Because the ring is open, the spell would need the gap closed before it activates.
effect: Creates a beam of light shining straight up from the seal. The more precisely the glyphs are drawn, the steadier the beam.

name: Light Tracer
description: A small, fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and drawn with a rough doubled line. At the center sits a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with short lines extending outward. It is wrapped by a Stretch sign, an arc that curves over the top of the sigil and opens toward the bottom. A single Link sign sits at the north point above the arc. No other signs are visible.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell makes and shapes light. Stretch surrounds the sigil as it is meant to and draws the magic out into a long, flexible ribbon, which turns the light into a thin string. Link identifies objects broken off from the same source and connects them, so the string of light runs between those pieces. The closed ring allows the spell to activate.
effect: When drawn on one fragment of a broken object, the spell sends a string of light from that fragment to every other fragment of the same object, tracing the connection between the pieces.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A small, tilted, dark oval seal drawn in white lines. The center shows a glyph of concentric circles with a dot in the middle, and several short white strokes radiate outward from it toward the ring, with small marks scattered around them. The seal is foreshortened and very small, so none of the surrounding signs can be matched to a named sign. A pale shape overlaps the upper left edge. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told.
justification: The concentric circles with a central dot and the radiating hand-like strokes match the memory erasure sigil and its attached keystones. Those keystones resemble Glaives, which set how deeply magic embeds itself into the flesh. The smaller marks that separate one variant from another are too small to read, so only the core spell can be identified.
effect: Likely erases memories from the target's mind. Variants can wipe the mind entirely, wipe all memory of magic, wipe all memory of a secret or conversation, or wipe all memory of a person. Which variant this is cannot be determined from the image, because the surrounding signs cannot be read.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel showing a close-up of a girl's face in profile on the left, with a hand reaching in from the right toward her eyes. Between the fingers sits a small dark round shape with a few thin trailing lines below it and some tiny white marks on and around it. The fingers cover most of the shape, and what remains is too small and dark to show a ring, sigil, or any identifiable sign.
justification: A seal appears to be present, but no sigil or sign can be matched, and whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told. There is nothing legible to decode.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A small manga panel showing a round seal drawn in white lines on a black disk. The ring appears closed. At the center sits a sigil of concentric circles with a dot in the middle. Several branching, hand-like lines spread out from it, mostly toward the south and sides, and resemble Glaives signs. A few small dots are scattered inside the ring. The right edge is clipped by the panel border, and the image is too small to read the finer marks.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil sets the kind of magic, which is not one of the elemental sigils. The branching Glaives-like strokes set how deeply the magic embeds itself into its target. The small dots are additional signs, but they are too small to identify, so the exact variant cannot be read from the visible marks.
effect: Erases memories from the target's mind. Known variants wipe the mind entirely, wipe all memory of magic, wipe memory of a secret or conversation, or wipe all memory of a person. Which variant this is cannot be determined from the image.

name: Mirror Spell
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a clean background. The main ring is closed and has no element sigil at its center, which is left empty. Four smaller closed satellite circles sit at the northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest points, each holding a single tilted Reflection sign. Inside the main ring are four more Reflection signs: upright at north and south, turned sideways at east and west. At the four cardinal points the ring bulges into bracket-shaped signs that match Projection, flanked by partial-circle and line shapes. Angled lines from those shapes run out to connect each satellite circle to the main ring.
justification: With no sigil, the seal is driven entirely by its signs. Eight Reflection signs, four inside the ring and one in each satellite, make targeting a reflected image the core of the spell. The four Projection signs send that captured image outward. The linking lines tie the satellite Reflection signs into the main ring, so the reflections they capture feed the projection.
effect: Reflects whatever is looking at the seal by capturing its image and projecting it outward. When linked with a spell that gathers shadows, it lets the bearer take on the appearance of any animal that gazes at them. Its full effect on its own is not known.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A fully visible, highly complex seal drawn in black line on a white background, with an outer ring and an inner ring, both closed. The band between the two rings is filled with a repeating chain of small curled Wind signs. Just inside the inner ring, many Columns signs, some single and some doubled, line the edge pointing inward. Four smaller closed circles sit at the north, south, east, and west. The north and south circles each hold a three-armed whorl sigil, a variant of the wind sigil, ringed by three Columns signs. The east and west circles each hold a wind-like S-shaped sigil with mirrored markings, surrounded by small signs that resemble Levitation and Aeriforms Defined. Small curled signs sit in the open space between the four circles. At the center is a three-lined Stability and Level Planes sign.
justification: The four sub-circles each contain a wind-family sigil, so the whole seal works with air. The north and south whorl sigils are Whorling Wind, which moves air by rotating it, and their three Columns signs push that motion in a set direction. The east and west sigils are Wind Underfoot, which supports solid objects in the air, and the Levitation and Aeriforms Defined signs around them add lift. The central Stability and Level Planes sign keeps the target balanced on a level plane like a float on water. The many Columns signs along the inner ring direct the overall force, and the outer band of Wind signs adds further wind behavior. The seal is mirrored top to bottom and left to right, so the effect is evenly balanced.
effect: A wind spell that keeps a carriage aloft and lets it fly while being pulled through the air. It holds the carriage level and stable throughout the flight.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A manga panel showing the lower part of a very large seal. The top of the seal runs past the frame, and a hand and a figure holding a pen cover the bottom center and right, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen. The outer edge is a band between two concentric rings, filled with a repeating row of small curled signs that match the Sign of Wind. Just inside it, a dense row of Columns signs lines the inner ring all the way around the visible arc. Toward the middle sits a small circle holding a three-armed spiral sigil in the style of a whorling wind sigil, with small Columns signs set around it. To its left is an S-shaped spiral resembling the wind sigil, also with short Columns-like marks nearby. Further curls on the right are partly hidden under hatching. The middle of the seal is cut off, so the full set of sigils and any central signs cannot be read.
justification: The visible sigils are all wind variants, so this is a wind spell. The three-armed spiral reads as Whorling Wind, which moves air by rotation. The S-shaped spiral reads as a wind sigil of the Wind Underfoot kind, which supports solid objects in the air. The Columns signs around the inner sigil and along the inner ring direct that air in a set direction. The Sign of Wind repeated around the outer band adds a further wind modifier whose exact role is unclear. The many sigils and the evenly spaced rows of signs suggest a symmetric seal. This reading assumes the hidden half mirrors the visible half, with a second whorling sigil and a second wind-type sigil.
effect: Moves and directs air beneath a large object to keep it aloft and flying while it is pulled along. This assumes the parts of the seal that are cut off or covered mirror the visible part.

name: Petrification
description: A manga panel of a figure turned to jagged, rock-like material, one arm raised and holding a small object aloft, surrounded by crystalline spikes. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible, and the held object shows no readable markings.
justification: Nothing to decode. The stone-like figure and spikes are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Petrification
description: A large, fully visible seal drawn on a page and viewed at a slight angle, with the outer ring closed. At the center sits a smaller inner ring holding a pinwheel of overlapping rotated squares around a small central square, which matches none of the five base sigils. A band of small repeating marks surrounds this inner ring, made of Columns-like and Dispersion-like strokes separated by dots. Outside the band are four arc-enclosed signs of crossed strokes ending in small circles at the north, east, south and west. Each has three small Dispersion-like signs beside it and a cluster of long hooked strokes resembling Envelopment, mixed with straight strokes topped by small loops. Four branch-like signs with curled bases sit diagonally between these groups. Four large circles intersect the outer ring at the corners. The upper left holds a snowflake-like crystal design, the right an S-shaped spiral flanked by drops, the lower left a dotted circle inside a jagged star, and the lower right a four-lobed knot around a small circle. Each large circle is flanked by two small signs of a circle set inside a V. The outermost border band carries short Columns-like marks and groups of three slanted strokes. The fine strokes are small, but no part of the seal is cut off or hidden.
justification: The seal is a compound of many parts and has no single base sigil at its core. The central pinwheel is an unfamiliar sigil, and the four large rim circles act as linked sub-seals, each adding its own sigil, including a crystal-like design and a spiral-and-drops design. The repeated Columns-like and Dispersion-like strokes spread the magic outward around the seal rather than sending it in one direction. The hooked Envelopment-like strokes wrap that effect around whatever it reaches. The branch-like signs at the diagonals resemble Glaives, which set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh. Read together, these signs describe magic that pours outward in all directions, coats its targets, and sinks into them.
effect: Turns everything nearby, living or inanimate, into a rock-like material of unknown nature.

name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel showing a fully visible seal against grey shaded tone, with the ring closed. A large triangle is inscribed inside the ring, its three points touching or nearly touching it. A small filled square sits at each of the triangle's vertices. A fire sigil, small relative to the ring, sits at the center inside the large triangle. Three branching, feather-like signs sit in the spaces between the triangle and the ring, one at the north and one each at the southwest and southeast. None of them clearly matches a known sign. Three small round knobs are attached to the outside of the ring, at the northwest, northeast and south. A few small strokes near the triangle's edges are too small to read.
justification: The fire sigil sets the spell as fire magic, and its small size points to a gentle intensity. The large triangle with squares at its vertices, the three matching branching signs and the three outer knobs are arranged with threefold symmetry around the sigil. None of these match a known sign, so their exact roles cannot be decoded sign by sign. Because they repeat evenly, they act on the flame the same way on every side rather than pushing it in one direction, which fits a steady, contained flame.
effect: Creates a flame that gives off light but no heat. The flame can be touched without injury, which makes it useful as a safe light source and for scaring off beasts.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn fairly large relative to the ring. Four Levitation signs are placed at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points, evenly spaced, with their arrowheads pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and controls flame, and its fairly large size gives a strong flame. Levitation floats the magic above the seal, and when the signs are balanced the result tends to take the shape of a sphere. Four equal signs evenly placed around the sigil are balanced, so the flame forms a floating ball. The length of the Levitation signs sets how much weight the spell can carry.
effect: Creates a ball of fire that floats above the seal and also lifts any object that is not too heavy placed directly above it.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A manga panel. A sheet of paper lies on a table with a small oval seal drawn on it, seen at a steep angle. The ring appears closed, though a wisp rising from its upper edge makes the top hard to read. Inside are a small central mark and four tiny marks at the north, south, east, and west points. At this size they look like short arrow-like strokes, possibly Levitation signs, but neither the central sigil nor the signs can be clearly identified.
justification: The layout of one central glyph with four matching signs at the cardinal points fits a balanced seal, but the strokes are too small to confirm. If the center is a fire sigil and the four signs are Levitation, the fire sigil would set the element and the balanced Levitation signs would lift the result above the seal.
effect: The effect cannot be fully confirmed from the image. If the center is a fire sigil ringed by Levitation signs, the spell creates a ball of fire that levitates above the seal and can lift light objects held directly above it.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal in black ink on a white background, ring closed. A large Rain sign fills most of the ring: a square with inward-curving sides and pointed corners, with three parallel lines crossing each of its four sides at north, east, south, and west. A water sigil sits in the empty space at the center of the Rain sign, drawn turned on its side so the S-curve runs roughly horizontally with one teardrop above it and one below. No other signs are present.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water, and its large size within the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Rain is a sign that surrounds a central sigil and summons the target material, here water, to fall within its area. The Rain sign is drawn the normal way, not flipped inside-out, so it brings water down rather than pushing it away. The rotation of the sigil does not change its meaning, and with the ring closed the spell is active.
effect: Generates a shower of rain that falls over the seal's area.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal in black line work on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. A small fire sigil marks the north point and another marks the south point, both drawn compactly with their triangles oriented toward the center. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, each a long vertical stroke crossed by short horizontal ends.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. The two small fire sigils add a second, heat-based element above and below it; their small size relative to the ring keeps that effect mild. The two Crosshair signs direct the seal's magic at whatever their short ends point toward, so the combined water and fire magic is aimed at the water around the seal rather than producing new water.
effect: Creates a water-repellent area, forming a bubble devoid of water within the spell's radius. Whether it does this by repelling the water or by drying it away is not known.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a small gap at the bottom. At the center is a horizontal double spiral, a variant of the wind sigil drawn without its side strokes. North of it is a modified fire sigil: an upright triangle with two lines crossing over it in an X. South is a matching modified fire sigil, inverted so the triangle points downward. One Crosshair sign sits at the east point and one at the west point, each with its short ends facing the ring and the center.
justification: The central wind-variant sigil sets the spell as air magic. It is the largest glyph in the ring, so it drives the main effect. The two modified fire sigils above and below add heat. One is inverted, which matches the drying arrangement of this seal. The two Crosshair signs aim the magic at whatever their short ends point toward, which confines the effect to the area around the seal. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn.
effect: Clears water from the space around the seal. It either repels water to leave a bubble free of water within its radius, or, with the inverted fire sigils, dries things off and warms them up. The ring must be closed for the spell to activate.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a horizontal double spiral, an S-shaped curl that reads as a variant of the wind sigil, drawn without the side ticks of the base wind sigil. At the north point sits a fire-like glyph: a triangle pointing down toward the center, with two diagonal strokes crossing over it in an X. At the south point sits a matching fire-like glyph, a triangle pointing up toward the center with its own crossing strokes. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. The seal is symmetric north to south and east to west, with no other signs.
justification: The wind-variant sigil at the center sets the base magic as air. The two modified fire glyphs add heat to that air. Both point inward, so the heat acts within the seal. The two Crosshair signs direct the effect onto whatever their shorter ends point at, which keeps it focused on a defined area around the seal. Together these produce warm, moving air acting on a set area, which pushes water out of that space. A nearly identical form with inverted fire glyphs and a broken line through each triangle dries and warms instead. The strokes here are too small to tell those two forms apart with certainty.
effect: Creates a water-repellent area that forms a bubble free of water within the spell's radius. The closely related drying form instead dries off objects and warms them up.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed, forming a band around an empty center. No sigil sits in the middle. Four Repetition signs sit on the band at the north, east, south and west points. In each of the four quadrants between them is a group of three signs: a Convergence triangle pointing inward toward the center, flanked on each side by a Columns sign with its crossbar toward the outer ring. That makes four Repetition, four Convergence and eight Columns signs in all.
justification: Repetition can stand in for a sigil and is the basis of the seal; it continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs set an area of effect in the shape of a column, and their count raises the range. The inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and can make loose material pack tightly together. Spread evenly around the band, these balanced signs apply the reset uniformly to whatever lies within the inner ring.
effect: Reverts the affected object to its original form, making it like new. Rotten food becomes fresh, dirty clothing becomes new and clean, and any later change, such as added embroidery, is undone.

name: Reverse Time
description: A manga panel of an open book held in a hand. On the right page is a large circular seal with the ring closed, filled with straight lines that form overlapping triangles and other geometric shapes in a star-like arrangement. There is no recognizable element sigil at the center. Fingers cross the lower right part of the seal and hide some lines, and the line work is too small to separate into individual named signs. The left page shows several smaller glyphs: one resembling a Repetition sign, a swirl shape, and a ringed circular pattern. These are too small to read in detail.
justification: No element sigil can be identified, so the seal does not take its behavior from a primary sigil. Its structure of straight lines forming geometric shapes in a star-like layout matches the family of time-reversal seals. These are related to Repetition, which resets objects to an earlier state, but they work without the Repetition sigil. The individual signs cannot be decoded at this size, and the covered portion is assumed to mirror the visible geometric pattern.
effect: Reverses time on the target to undo wear and other damage, for up to one day. When that time runs out, the glyph vanishes and the target returns to the state it would have without the spell. The glyph can be reapplied to repeat the effect. This reading assumes the hidden part of the seal follows the same symmetric geometric pattern.

name: Reverse Time
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on skin, framed by pulled-back clothing. Inside the ring is a six-pointed star made of straight lines, filled with nested triangles and smaller geometric shapes radiating from a central point. No element sigil is identifiable. Small branch-like marks sit outside the ring at the upper left, upper right, top, and below. They do not clearly match any known sign. Hands overlap the left and right edges of the ring, and fabric covers part of the lower marks, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is closed. The visible top and bottom arcs appear unbroken.
justification: The seal has no recognizable sigil. The central design is built entirely from straight-line geometry in a six-pointed star, which marks a time-reversal seal rather than a Repetition seal, since no Repetition sigil is present. The external branch-like marks may act as modifiers, but they are too small and partly hidden to identify, so their individual contributions cannot be decoded.
effect: Reverses time on the target, undoing wear and other damage. The effect lasts at most one day and is not permanent. When it expires, the glyph vanishes and the target returns to the state it would have been in without the spell. The seal can be reapplied to repeat the effect.

name: Rising Platform of Water
description: A fully visible, roughly drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, with its two droplets flanking the central curve. Eight signs surround it in alternating order. Four Levitation signs sit at about the north, east, south and west points, each turned on its side so the arrow lies roughly sideways rather than pointing straight at the center. Four Columns signs sit between them at the intercardinal points, each oriented outward from the sigil.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The outward Columns signs give it a columnar area of effect, and because there are four balanced around the ring, the column forms evenly over the seal instead of leaning to one side. The four sideways Levitation signs are also balanced, so their lifting effect acts straight up on whatever the seal is drawn on rather than carrying it in one direction. Together the signs form a rising pillar of water that carries its object upward.
