effect: Generates an upward surge of water in a column that lifts the object the seal is drawn on straight up into the air, acting as a rising platform.

name: Rising Wave
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the bottom. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn at moderate size relative to the ring. A ring of Columns signs runs around the inside edge, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Small V-shaped Regions signs alternate with the Columns across the upper half only. The lower Columns stand alone, and the space around the gap at the bottom is empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Columns signs make the magic manifest as a column and drive it with force, and their number raises the amount of water produced. Regions signs set where magic manifests relative to the seal. Because they appear only on the upper half, the surge is biased toward that side, so the column of water leans and travels at an angle rather than straight up. The ring must be closed before the spell will activate.
effect: Creates a powerful surge of water that rises diagonally upward, strong enough to launch the caster into the air.

name: Sand Bridge
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a round disc, seen at a steep angle and drawn in rough, sketchy ink. The outer ring appears closed, with a narrow outer band of small marks too tiny to identify. A small inner ring at the center holds a sigil that is too small and foreshortened to name. Around it radiate several signs shaped like two small circles joined by a line, which match Solidification. They are clearest on the upper left and lower side. Other short, branching signs sit on the right side, but they are too blurred to match. The upper right edge of the disc runs off the panel, and the far side is compressed by the angle.
justification: The Solidification signs make the material the seal controls more solid. Grouped around the center, they suggest a spell that forms loose material into a firm structure. The central sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the image. The remaining signs are too blurred to say how the structure is shaped or held in place.
effect: Raises loose earth and sand into a solid temporary bridge that can be crossed until a permanent one is built. Only the hardening part of this can be read from the visible Solidification signs. The rest is assumed from the seal being a sand bridge, since the sigil and most signs are not legible.

name: Sand Bridge
description: A manga panel showing a large arched bridge of sand spanning a river, seen from above, with a girl in the foreground looking up at it in excitement. Two blank rectangular boxes sit in the upper part of the panel. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere.
justification: Nothing to decode. The bridge is the result of a spell, not a glyph, and no part of a seal appears in the image.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, since no glyph is visible.

name: Scalewolf Curse
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The inner ring sits inside a thicker outer band studded with outward-pointing triangles, with larger triangles at the north, east, south, and west points and smaller ones spaced evenly between them. At the center are three dots arranged in a triangle, one above and two below, under an arch that opens downward. The arch's ends rest on a horizontal bar, and four short stems hang from that bar, each ending in a downward-pointing fork. None of these central marks matches a known element sigil or named sign.
justification: No element sigil is present. The three-dot triangle is a keystone also found in the illusory labyrinth seal, which marks this as forbidden-style magic rather than a standard tetrad spell. The arch, the forked bar, and the spiked outer band match no named signs, so their individual roles cannot be decoded. The seal's function rests on what is known about it as a whole, not on reading its parts.
effect: Permanently transforms the target's body into a beast form. If material from a creature, such as a scalewolf's fur and scales, is fused with the body, the target takes that creature's shape.

name: Sealchair Glyph
description: A manga panel showing a large compound seal drawn on a flat wooden surface between two curved, leg-like shapes. At the center is an oval main ring that appears closed. Inside it sits a dense central glyph of crossing strokes, flanked by several smaller enclosed rings packed with clustered marks. Lines run outward from the main ring to satellite circles: larger ones at the upper left, upper right, left and right, and several small ones along the edges. The upper satellites are cut off by the top of the frame. The left and right satellites are partly hidden behind the curved legs. Every sign, inside the main ring and in the satellites, is too small and too blurred by screentone to match to a known sign or sigil.
justification: Nothing can be decoded. No sigil can be identified, so the element is unknown, and no individual sign is legible enough to name. That leaves no modifiers to combine. The layout does show a main seal linked to multiple satellite seals, but what each part contributes cannot be read.
effect: The signs and sigils are not readable, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Serpent's Bed of Sand
description: A rough ink sketch of a fully visible compound seal on a plain background, outer ring closed. A wide outer band runs between two concentric rings and holds two kinds of marks in alternation. One is a spiral eye-like glyph matching Repetition, which appears about six times around the band. The other is a group of a Columns sign, an inward-pointing Convergence triangle, and a second Columns sign, which appears about five times, each group turned to follow the band. Inside the inner ring is a central square holding a circle with a four-lobed Billow shape. Around it sit several small closed seals, about five, each with a tiny sigil and signs that are too small to read individually. A few stray ink marks surround the drawing.
justification: The outer band of Repetition glyphs with paired Columns and Convergence is a repetition seal. It keeps resetting whatever it affects to its original state, while Convergence packs loose particles tightly together. Billow sits at the center in place of a sigil and turns available material into a fluffy cloud. The small ring seals around it are assumed to be earth seals that pair an earth sigil with Crushing and Columns to grind stone into sand, though their contents cannot be confirmed at this resolution. Together, the parts crush stone into sand, gather it, billow it into a cloud, compact it so it can bear weight, and keep it from falling apart.
effect: Creates a large, fluffy cloud made of sand that is firm and stable enough to hold up a dragon. The repeating layer continually restores the cloud to its original shape.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a clean background, ring closed. A wind sigil with its short side strokes sits in the lower part of the ring, toward the south, rather than at the center. A single elongated Levitation sign runs from the north edge of the ring down to just above the sigil, its crossbar at the north and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves air. Levitation is a directional sign, so its angle and length steer where the spell acts. Its length also sets how far the target travels, how much weight it carries, and how fast it moves. Here it is stretched across nearly the whole ring along a single axis. With only one Levitation sign and nothing to balance it, the moving air is pushed one way along that axis instead of holding the target in place.
effect: Produces a strong thrust of moving air in one direction along the line of the Levitation sign. When drawn large enough on a big surface such as a sail, it can make that object fly.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A manga two-page spread. On the left, large spherical rocks float above a wide landscape, with inset panels of a girl looking upward and a girl clinging to a rope-lashed pole. On the right, a figure hangs from a sail on a pole above a boat that leaps out of splashing water, with large black bars behind it and a small inset showing the sail and the boat. The sails show only plain tone, with no ring, sigil, or sign visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The flying sail and the leaping boat are effects, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Snugstone Spell
description: A close-up manga panel of an oval stone with a seal drawn on it. Several dark cracks run across the stone, cutting through the ring and the glyphs. A fire sigil sits at the center, split by a crack. An inverted Columns sign, crossbar toward the center, sits at the south point, and a matching inverted Columns sign is visible at the east point. Four curled, crescent-shaped signs sit at the intercardinal points. The north and west points are obscured by the cracks and dark lines, so any signs there cannot be read. The inner ring line is broken by the cracks, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be confirmed.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as fire. Columns inverted around the sigil spread their effect horizontally outward instead of beaming it upward, behaving much like Dispersion. The curled signs at the intercardinal points are a radial modifier that tempers the fire's output, turning flame into gentle heat. Assuming the hidden north and west points mirror the visible inverted Columns, the seal pushes mild heat evenly out on all sides.
effect: Radiates a steady, gentle warmth outward in all directions without producing any flame. This assumes the obscured north and west signs match the visible inverted Columns.

name: Spell of Reduction
description: A manga panel showing the edge of a box or lid with a hand beneath it. A fragment of a seal runs along the edge. A curved stroke, a short vertical line, a small Diamond sign, and nested angle marks resembling one corner of an Expansion sign are visible. The ring and the rest of the seal are cut off by the edge of the box and the panel framing, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed, and no sigil can be confirmed.
justification: The Diamond sign is identifiable, and the nested angles match part of an Expansion sign. The curved stroke may belong to a central Repetition glyph, but too little is visible to confirm it. Expansion is semi-directional: corners pointing outward make the target grow, and corners pointing inward (inverted) make it shrink. Diamond likely restricts the effect to objects inside the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. The visible angles are too fragmentary to show which way they face.
effect: Likely shrinks items placed inside the container to far below their normal size. This assumes the hidden part of the seal holds inverted Expansion signs around a central glyph, with Diamond signs in the gaps, mirroring the visible fragment.

name: Spike
description: A manga panel of a crouching figure behind a large curved spray of debris, with several thick spikes flying through the air and one embedded in the ground. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The spikes and spray are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Sylph Shoes Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The center holds a large Wind Underfoot sigil, a variant of the wind sigil: an S-shaped double spiral flanked by curved strokes on both sides. Around it, a single band of signs runs inside the ring, alternating between Convergence triangles and Levitation arrows, roughly eight of each. The triangles have one point aimed inward, and the arrowheads also point toward the center.
justification: The Wind Underfoot sigil makes this wind magic of the kind that supports solid objects in the air, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Levitation lifts the target into the air, and its even, balanced spacing keeps the lift steady on all sides. Convergence focuses the magic about a single point, so the lift stays centered under the target instead of spreading out. With every sign evenly spaced and pointing inward, the seal pushes no particular way and the target is held aloft.
effect: Lets the wearer float and fly above the ground. The seal is drawn in two halves that only form a closed ring, and so only activate, when the two halves are brought together.

name: Tracking Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, outer ring closed. Inside it run two partial inner arcs, one sweeping from the west up over the north and one from the south around to the east. A straight horizontal line crosses the full center, overlaid by a zigzag line of repeated peaks resembling a chain of Crushing shapes. There is no recognizable element sigil. At the north, a small circle hangs on a stem that runs up to the inner arc, resembling one end of a Solidification sign. At the northeast sits a Diamond shape crossed by two curved strokes, similar to Holding curves. At the northwest is a hash-like sign of short horizontal bars crossed by vertical strokes, which matches no known sign. A small two-stroke tick sits at the end of the upper inner arc. The lower half repeats all of these as a 180-degree rotation: a circle on a stem at the south, a crossed Diamond at the southwest, the hash-like sign at the southeast, and a tick at the end of the lower arc.
justification: With no element sigil, the type of magic is not fixed by an element glyph, and the central zigzag-and-line motif may be serving that role instead. The Diamond-like signs may limit the spell to objects other than the one it is drawn on, and the Solidification-like circles may firm up the effect. However, none of the signs exactly match known forms, and their combined function is not established. The strict rotational symmetry suggests the spell is meant to be balanced and act evenly rather than in one direction.
effect: Marks a magical item so that it can be tracked afterward. How the individual signs contribute to this effect is not known.

name: Twin Bottle's Spell
description: A manga panel showing the curved, dark surface of a bottle. A small oval seal is drawn on it, seen at an angle, with its ring closed and a bright glow radiating around it. Faint marks inside the ring, including a cross-like shape near the center, can be made out, but the glow, the screentone, and the small scale blur every line. No sigil or sign can be matched to a known form.
justification: Nothing to decode. The seal is present, but its sigil and signs are too small and too washed out by the glow to identify. No element or modifier can be read.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Wall Breaker Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a small gap at the bottom. An earth sigil sits at the center. One Columns sign sits at the west point and one at the east point, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the sigil. One Crushing sign sits at the north point and one at the south point, both facing the normal way rather than inverted.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell that acts on solid matter such as stone, wood, and soil. Normal Crushing signs break the target into smaller and smaller pieces until it is a powder; the larger the signs, the finer the result. The paired Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect and push it in a set direction, driving the crushing through the material. Because the ring is open, the spell is drawn but not yet active; closing the ring would cast it.
effect: Breaks through the solid material it is drawn on and reduces it to dust or sand.

name: Water Bolt
description: A manga page. The top panel shows part of a large seal drawn on the ground. The curve of its ring runs along the left side, and the rest is cut off by the panel borders, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen. Across the middle runs a row of at least three Piercing signs, each a straight line with a diamond along it. Near them are a few small chevron marks that look like Regions signs, though their exact direction is hard to read. Splashing water and a foot pressing down on the seal hide much of the interior. No sigil can be identified in the visible area. The bottom panel shows a figure holding a staff, with speed lines and no glyph.
justification: Several Piercing signs in a row make the magic manifest as projectiles, and their number sets how many. Regions signs that all point the same way send that magic in one direction. Together they describe a row of projectiles fired one way. The sigil that would set the element is not visible, so the element cannot be confirmed from what is shown.
effect: Likely shoots a row of water bolts straight ahead, with more Piercing signs producing more bolts, and works best when drawn large. This assumes the hidden part of the seal holds a water sigil, which cannot be seen here.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel showing an oval seal drawn on a surface, ring closed and fully in frame, with fingers or tool tips pressing in at the east and west edges. A water sigil sits at the center. Beside it on the east and west sit tall stacked signs that resemble Mimicry, though their outer parts are partly covered where the hands overlap. Along the north is a row of small signs that look like Columns with a peaked mark among them, too small and rough to identify with certainty. Along the south is a row of alternating straight lines and V-shaped marks that resemble Regions signs pointing toward the center.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water. The Mimicry-like signs make the magic imitate the movements of a creature form. The marks in the north row likely include the sign that shapes the water. The Regions-like V marks control where the magic manifests relative to the ring. Because the north row is not clearly legible, the shaping sign cannot be confirmed.
effect: Creates a horse made of water that moves like a real horse and can be used to pull a vehicle. This assumes the illegible north row holds the horse-shaping sign.

name: Water Pen
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, drawn in black line. A water sigil sits at the center. A Holding sign wraps around it, with one curved bracket on the east and one on the west, each ending in a dot at the bottom. At the north point is a joined figure that reads as a Dispersion sign with two Columns signs projecting sideways from either end, forming an H-like shape. At the south point is a Pointing sign, a triangle with a crossbar flanked by two curled strokes.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the seal acts on water. Holding keeps that water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Pointing tapers the water into a cone or blade. The Columns and Dispersion signs at the north set where the shaped water manifests and let its magic seep outward from the formed body rather than shooting off as a beam.
effect: Creates a dagger-shaped glob of water that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the dagger to saturate it, turning it into a pen that can draw very large seals on almost any surface.

name: Watershot Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal with the ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn small relative to the ring. Around the inside of the ring sit about seven small Columns signs, each with its bar toward the ring and its stem toward the center: one at north, one at each upper diagonal, and others down the east and west sides. At the south point a single larger Columns sign stretches from just below the sigil to the ring, noticeably longer than the others.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size keeps the effect modest. Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect and push it in a given direction. More Columns signs raise the range or amount of water produced. When all are balanced and of equal length, the water rises straight up from the seal. A longer Columns sign adds pressure in its direction, so the extended southern sign likely tilts or strengthens the stream on that side.
effect: Creates a stream of water that shoots out from the seal, straight up when the Columns signs are balanced. The longer southern sign likely adds extra push on that side.

name: Wind Wall
description: A manga panel with part of a seal visible. A large white rounded shape covers the top of the seal, and vertical lines cut across the right side, so the seal is only partly visible and it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed. Near the center is a spiral stroke that matches part of a wind sigil, with a small dot beside it. About six small triangles that match Convergence signs are scattered across the upper left. A curved band with small tick marks along its edges arcs around the lower side of the sigil. Below the band, a row of four or five Columns signs runs along the bottom edge. They are drawn as T shapes, with the bar toward the center and the stem toward the ring, which is the inverted orientation. The upper and right parts of the seal are hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element as moving air. The row of inverted Columns signs makes the magic spread outward horizontally, in a band, rather than rise as a beam. The Convergence signs on the opposite side focus and compact the magic about a point, which keeps the air dense and holds it in shape. The ticked arc around the sigil on the Columns side appears to outline the curve along which the air manifests. Together these signs form a curved, dense barrier of air.
effect: Creates a circular wall of air that is difficult for objects or people to pass through, so it can be used to contain people or animals. This reading assumes the hidden top and right parts follow the arrangement visible here.

name: Windowway Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of three closed concentric circles that form two narrow bands, so the ring is closed. The outer band is filled all the way around with small zigzag, lightning bolt-shaped marks set side by side. The inner band is filled all the way around with chevrons that resemble Regions signs, all pointing the same way around the circle in a clockwise direction. The large central area is empty, with no sigil and no other signs inside it.
justification: The two bands of identical, repeated marks lining the seal like extra rings match the Windows sign. Windows does not sit beside a sigil like a conventional sign. Instead it wraps the seal in a band of simple repeated markings, and its variants differ in their mark shapes, which fits the zigzag band here. The inner chevrons look like directional Regions-style signs and are all angled the same way, which suggests they set a flow around the ring. The seal has no element sigil and no location symbol in the center, so it relies entirely on these bands to work.
effect: Opens a gateway between two distant locations, letting one pass from one place to the other. It only functions as part of a matched pair, with each seal varied so that it links only to its own partner.
